unmappedHistorical.quote: “Something inside us said, 'no more.' we had begun to have silent thoughts that maybe the dope was killing us.”
unmappedHistorical.body:
Many of us used for years and did not realize we had a problem. Even when we became aware that something was wrong, most of us could not accept we were addicts. Just as recovery is a process, and not a single event, so too was this realization. Seeds began to germinate and this allowed recovery to become possible.

We may have realized drugs were shortening our lives, but we had no desire to stop using. Perhaps some of us thought that one day we would have an epiphany, get religion, or just grow up and make a decision to change. Deep down, we may have already known we lacked the power to do so, even if we hadn't quite admitted it to ourselves on a conscious level.

Many of us continued using long after we realized we had lost control, or that we were slowly dying or risking overdose. Some of us were fully aware that we were addicts and still continued to use.

The reasons we continued to use may be as varied as each individual addict. Some of us knew we were addicts but saw our lives as manageable, only vaguely aware that our using might be the cause of our problems. Others knew their lives lacked even a passing resemblance to manageability. Some of us knew our drug use was only a symptom of a larger problem. We were unaware that the cause of our symptoms was a disease called addiction.

No matter what, the process was that opened our minds to recovery we all came to the same realization, we lacked the capability to stay clean. This realization actually made our recovery possible.
unmappedHistorical.moment: through N.A., I have a choice. Having admitted that the drugs were killing me, I can finally surrender to the N.A. Program. When I follow it to the best of my ability, I can finally begin living!

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Grey book “not from preaching nor from judgement, but from sharing our experience, strength and hope do we recover.”
unmappedHistorical.source: Grey book, chapter five, page 83, lines 4-6quote”
unmappedHistorical.body: Meditation….when we did hear others share, we usually heard about their struggles, their mistakes, and what they did to find a new way to live, free from guilt, shame, and active addiction. When we got to Step Three, we were further relieved to learn that no one was going to force their religion on us. In fact, the God of our own understanding did not mean the God we grew up with, or the conception of God many of us had when we first came in. And what a relief! Not too many of us came in with a very healthy conception of a Higher Power, if we had one at all. As we progressed through Steps four and five our sense of relief only increased as we learned we not only got to figure out our own sexuality and our own moral code, but that no one was going to prescribe it for us. As long as we were not hurting other people, it seemed we could be comfortable with who we were and confident in who we were becoming as we formed our values and realized what they were. Some of us made decisions to give up old behaviors, while others realized things they had judged themselves mercilessly for in the past were the result of shame, and having someone else's moral code forced on us. We may have had both experiences, or even run the gamut on a single issue as our recovery progressed and evolved. What an undeniable feeling of freedom to realize that, maybe for the first time in our lives, we were becoming capable of making adult decisions and defining who we were, with the help of a loving Higher Power.
unmappedHistorical.moment: I will not preach the N.A. Program, nor will I judge other people or moralize with my fellow addicts. I will share my own personal struggles and what I did to find a new way to live in happiness...clean! I will be grateful for the gift of choice and, through sharing my experience, strength and hope, make this same gift available to others.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “As we become more closely involved with others we will learn to share our pain and it will lessen.”
unmappedHistorical.source: -grey book, chapter four, Step Twelve, page 68, lines 33-34
unmappedHistorical.body:
Many of us come to N.A. very guarded. In our old way of life vulnerability equated to weakness, and weakness, to our sick way of thinking, equated to death. Many of our fears were well founded. After all, in our active addiction, being vulnerable opened us up to the predatory behaviors of others in active addiction. The few times we allowed ourselves to open up, we got burned. Whether our dealer was a respectable doctor prescribing us our drugs-of-no- choice or we literally lived on the street, many of us lived by the code of the street: we must show no weakness in order to survive.

In reality, nothing could be further from the truth. Our inability to be vulnerable was keeping us sick. Refusing to admit our weakness was, in fact, killing us.

In recovery we learn to open ourselves up to those who truly want to help us. We learn, first hand, that "the therapeutic value of one addict helping another is without parallel". We learn to trust, and we learn to be trusted. We may even learn that people in N.A. are sick; just like we are. On the rare occasions someone

Violates that trust, we learn it is not fatal. We may even feel a certain sense of empathy toward the offender, for we know too well what it is like to be in that sick state of mind. We can even be grateful in such situations for the opportunity to practice the principles of our Traditions.
unmappedHistorical.moment: I will have faith in someone in N.A. who believes in me and wants to help me in my recovery. My thoughts will be on people who are not using and who have found a new way to live. I will share my pain and my recovery with these new associations. I will embrace the gift of vulnerability, realizing I truly have nothing to fear.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Being clean we will eventually have to learn to cope with success. Success scares us because in the past it proceeded failure. We could not afford to feel good because we remembered the pain of disappointment.
unmappedHistorical.body:
We are powerless over our addiction. We are, and when we begin working on our 1st Step, we are brought to the stark reality that it’s a whole lot more that we are powerless as well. This is part of building a foundation for our recovery.

However, we have problems with the good and the bad situations that arise in our daily lives. Just focusing on all the bad things that we are powerless over, and the bad feelings and emotions that these situations cause us, is missing half the truth. Too many addicts only focus on all the negative. This is in our nature to do. We are also powerless over the good situations, and feeling s and emotions that they produce. We as addict like to take credit for successes, and blame others for failures. Once we are c lean a while, and begin the journey we will need to overcome the fears, and emotions that have controlled us all our lives.

This includes when things are going good, or bad...many of our patterns will eventually reveal that after a success or good time in our life, it was immediately followed by an even deeper plunge into the darkness of addiction. Today we have the tools to help us to cope with the good and the bad, and need to get used to success being followed by even more success instead.
unmappedHistorical.moment: we will put our fears aside, with the help of God, and the program, we can grow to trust that success is not a prelude to failure. We can share with others our pain, and our feelings so that we can better deal with the situations as they arise, good or bad.

unmappedHistorical.quote: "As soon as we became acquainted with the Fellowship and the basic ideas of the program, we began to put these ideas into action. A good tool to remember is to counter our natural tendency to saddle ourselves with concerns that go beyond the twenty-four hours of each day.
unmappedHistorical.body: We hear a lot of information at the meetings, and from our sponsors. The knowledge that we gain from listening can then be turned into practical applications to combat this disease. Putting into practice what we learn, can and usually takes a lot of daily practice. Getting through a 24-hour period practicing these newly found tools, in spite of what life can throw at us is the recipe for success. Thus, the phrase just for today is born. We utilize this phrase often, to combat the natural addict thinking. Projecting outside of a 24-hour period, will always lead our thoughts into the realms of doom and gloom, and therefore can put us into a state of hopelessness, and depression again. Just what the disease wants. We must be vigilante about this aspect of our recovery, after all, we can only take positive action today. This doesn’t mean that we can’t plan for tomorrow, but this must be an action that is taken today, not a projection of what tomorrow will be like. We can accomplish this successfully, with the help of the N.A. Program, and our sponsors.
unmappedHistorical.moment: we will keep the focus on the 24 hours at hand, and if we find ourselves projecting into the future, we will take action by calling another addict, or attending a meeting to help get us back in today.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Addicts respond instinctively to honest sharing. The fact that the addict can feel the unconditional love and judge for themselves the qualifications revealed in the stories of recovering addicts, awakens the notion that at last there might be hope.”
unmappedHistorical.body: Something happens to an addict when he listens to another addict share honestly. There is a meeting of the spirits, that has healing potential for both. Only another addict can best understand the pain that we have endured, and the complete loss of self that happens when we are in active addiction. The awakening of our spirits is nurtured at meetings with the message of hope that we receive there. The empathy, and understanding are the vehicle in which these spiritual gifts are met. Once an addict, always an addict, is only one of the negative labels put on us. Many of us throughout the years have been told over, and over from those closest to us that we will never change. They don’t understand us, and never will. The pain and alienation this causes for us runs deep, and it takes a lot of love, caring, and sharing with others like us to heal and mend our broken spirits.
unmappedHistorical.moment: we will listen when we are with other recovering addicts, and try to tap into the healing and love that is offered to us. Just for today we will strengthen our hope that we will never have to go back to the horrors of addiction.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Are we doing our best? Are we staying honest? Are we still growing, or are we slipping back into the old fears and resentments? It is the purpose of the Tenth Step to answer these and similar questions.
unmappedHistorical.body: Life can be difficult. Now that we are not using drugs to mask the pain, and life’s ups and downs, we have a new way of dealing with issues as they arise during the course of a day. The 12 Steps of N.A. are a roadmap to help us avoid all the pitfalls that life can throw at us. This is not to say that we are perfect, and being human we will falter. The 10th Step is a tool that can help us here. We take a daily inventory, and see exactly what is really going on with us. The h.a.l.t.s., are addressed in the 10th Step as well. The importance of this daily habit of taking a look at ourselves gives us the ability to have a choice in the day or in any given situation that arises. We can see clearly, if we are truly doing our best, or are we reverting back to old behaviors, and thinking patterns, that are being fueled by fear, and anger. Today we can choose to use the 10th Step to start the day over, and correct any living mistakes, before they lead to more serious consequences.
unmappedHistorical.moment: we will stop and allow myself the time to take an inventory of my feelings, and emotions, and actions today and see on paper if we are moving in the right direction or straying from the path of recovery.

unmappedHistorical.quote: "As long as the ties that bind us together are stronger than those that would tear us apart, all will be well."
unmappedHistorical.body: Addiction makes us one of a kind, fortunately there are a lot of us. The disease of addiction is what draw us together, but it's recovery in Narcotics Anonymous that keeps us together. The principles in N.A. Is the glue that forms this bond, our common purpose is what brings us together, it makes unity possible. The disease of addiction is what will tear us apart, a recovering addict by themselves is bad company. We keep what we have by sharing it with other suffering addicts, this is our primary purpose. Unity of purpose is what creates unity in action. Addicts individually working the Steps, Traditions, and having a relationship with the God of their own understanding is what keeps the disease from tearing those ties apart. That's why unity is a must, if we are to survive. No individual is more important than the group, and no group is more important than Narcotics Anonymous. Anonymity in the First Tradition makes it impossible for personalities to come before principles. That means that the needs of the group comes before our individual needs, or fears. What's good for the group is usually good for the individual. The meetings is where recovery happens for us, we are drawn together from all walks of life. The Traditions are the safeguards to keep us feeling safe and where we feel like we fit in. That unity depends on how well we follow our Traditions. We practice these principles in dealing with each other and with society at large. This prevents internal and external forces from disuniting us. This makes our recovery possible and the primary purpose to stay primary.
unmappedHistorical.moment: we will not put our individual fears and needs ahead of the group, we need the group to survive.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Those of us who are consciously working and using the twelve Steps to recovery in our lives are seldom bothered by gossip.
unmappedHistorical.body: As addicts, we carry certain tendencies into the program with us. As people with the challenges that starting a new way of life free from drug use, we have many obstacles, and challenges ahead. Our participation with other recovering addicts, and the meetings is imperative in order to stay on the right path. Of course, it can be difficult with all the different personalities that we meet along the way. The support that is given to us through the Fellowship can be undermined by the gossip that so often takes place among our peers. We have many life challenges that we must overcome in order to learn to stay clean through all the good and bad that life on life’s terms can throw at us in a 24-hour period. Having to deal with being gossiped about, or participating in gossiping about someone else can cut us off from the very life line that saved us. What we focus on here in N.A. is ourselves, and getting better, not the faults of others. Remembering why we’re here helps us to keep recovery first. If we are participating in gossip, maybe we should ask ourselves what’s going on with us instead. Taking an inventory, writing a gratitude list, or calling another addict can help us to not be bothered by gossip that we hear in the meetings.
unmappedHistorical.moment: we will focus on ourselves, and not others, in order to not be side tracked from our path. We can be grateful that we are clean, and ready to rise above gossip, and personalities that we encounter.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “We had nothing left to lose. We gave up, quit struggling, surrendered, completely and unconditionally. Then and only then did we begin to recover from the disease of addiction.”
unmappedHistorical.body: The end of the road for many addicts is a miserable pain filled existence. A far cry from actually living a full spiritually principled life, which is what we strive for now. Part of the reason that we must strive to become better human beings today, is directly related to the place we found ourselves at the end of our addictions. To use is to lose, is a quote taken from our book, and with good reason. Without total abstinence from any and all drugs we can no longer strive for the kind of life that will guarantee that we never have to end up there again. Unfortunately, many addicts just don’t stay and work the program in order to stay clean. Unless we can learn to surrender to the program we cannot bring about the changes needed in order to stay here long enough for the miracles to happen. There is no quick fix, as many of us wanted. If there was, most of us would have never gotten to the point in our addiction where everything around us spiraled out of control. After all, we all have looked for that easy way out. When we take the example of those that came before us, we can see living proof that surrendering to the program has a very different outcome compared to surrendering to the disease. It gives us a choice today, where we had no choice, and a program that will help us to recover from the pain and broken life that we endured to get here.
unmappedHistorical.moment: we will surrender to the best of our ability. We will continue to follow the suggestions of the program, and reach out for the help we need in order to keep us from falling back into our old ways of thinking.

unmappedHistorical.quote: "We do, however, remember that God, not us, is responsible for our change. The line between where God does or does not help us is absolutely irrelevant."
unmappedHistorical.body:
Ego tells us that ego doesn't exists, easing God out leaves us with ourselves alone with our disease. The disease speaks to us in a voice that we don't talk back to, our own. Sometimes we don't know who's talking, sometimes we don't know that we don't know. Anonymity also means that we don't take credit for our recovery. Our gray book says, " all glory to God as we understand him is our attitude here."

This state of humility is what we need to interact with others. It is our actions not our feelings that define our recovery. Our Step Ten helps us keep this balance, we take inventory throughout the day to avoid some of our pitfalls. We engage our brains before our mouths, or any other form of communicating with others.

We run down our check list. Are we hungry, angry, lonely, tired, are we taking ourselves too serious, we can count to ten, wait ten seconds, or dismiss the first ten thoughts that come to mind, before we interact. We take time to allow the privilege of thinking before acting or reacting. These tools prevent us from having

To apply the corrective part of Step Ten. We recall our 6th and 7th Step and see where the God of our understanding had forgiven us. We reaffirm our divine partnership with our Higher Power, humility sets in, we become more tolerant and patient with others. Our Steps are designed to keep us from slipping back to our old behaviors and attitudes. It prevents us from creating and recreating more wreckage in our lives. The more we apply the spiritual principles the less we practice our defects. We stop justifying rationalizing, and analyzing. We replace compliance with reliance and let our loving God guide us.

unmappedHistorical.quote: "Our life is a diary wherein we mean to write one story, and quite often write another. It is when we compare the two that we have our humblest hour"
unmappedHistorical.body: In our active addiction we thought our lives were over. We were convinced that we were probably going to die using or die from using. We wrote ourselves off, we were convinced that there was no way out. After coming to Narcotics Anonymous we found hope, we met people, who like us, suffered from the horrors of addiction. In Narcotics Anonymous we stop creating more wreckage, and begin the reparation process. We stop using drugs, we lose the desire to use, and find a new way to live. Our lives start to change, even if things around us don't get better, we get better with the things around us. Narcotics Anonymous not only saved our lives, but gave us a life we never could ever conceive of. We start to change our past, by our actions in the present, we change our future's outcome. The spiritual principles we practice through living the Steps transforms us from the people we use to be, to the people God always meant us to be. If we would've written a list of the things we wanted from Narcotics Anonymous when we first came in, we would've sold ourselves short. We were beginning to live a life beyond our wildest dreams. Only when we forget where we came from, is when we lose our gratitude. Sometimes, as our gray book says, "we get caught up in striving for growth and eliminating our defects, that we forget about our assets." when we are grateful for where we are today, we remain humble.
unmappedHistorical.moment: we will look at our before and after, but most importantly we will focus on our today.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Through the freedom in our new lives we are finally able to see the special qualities that we possess as individuals...”
unmappedHistorical.body:
In Narcotics Anonymous one of the people we will meet, will be ourselves. After hitting our bottoms, we weren’t too happy to see what we have become. Now Abstinent, we feel all our feelings, and most were guilt, shame, and remorse. Most of us didn’t like ourselves, and now we get to face it. Living with ourselves without the use of drugs was even more painful, we no longer had the drugs to numb us. N.A. does not only offer Abstinence from drugs, it also offers Freedom from the obsession to use, and it offers a New Way to Live through the Spiritual Awakening we experience from Living each Step. This Awakening of the Spirit allows us to nurture the person we were meant to be all along. This Process is over time and not overnight, and at times our pain requires Total Surrender.

There’s Freedom contained in each Spiritual Principle. Freedom from active addiction, Freedom from self, Freedom from others, and Freedom from the world at large. We no longer need the masks, we no longer had to be the people others wanted us to be. We finally could be ourselves and be okay with that. We’re a work in Progress. We’re still not the person God knows we could be. We’re still not the person we want to be. We’re the person we are supposed to be right here, right now. With the Help of the God Of Our Understanding, our Sponsors, the Steps, and the Fellowship of N.A. this transformation is possible, Just For Today. We see ourselves realistically, with our liabilities and our Assets. We Surrender to this Process and receive Self-Acceptance, and Acceptance of others. We learn to Live in our own skins, we get glimpses of the people we could one day be. Today there’s Hope.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “All the good ideas and intentions will not help us at all if we fail to put them into action. “
unmappedHistorical.body: We cannot think our way into a new way of living. Talking about making changes doesn’t get it done. How many times have we tried to solve all our problems by thinking our way out? The continued use of drugs, after we saw how they were destroying our lives is the greatest example of how we cannot think ourselves better. This means that we must put action behind our recovery efforts. Going to meetings, working Steps, making phone calls, helping other addicts, and participating in service are all examples of how we can keep living our way into a new way of life. Most of us in our addictions always had the intention to stop using. We would convince ourselves that this would be the last time, or the last run, never to do it again. Of course, we would always fall back into using again, and then tell ourselves that this time would be different. After years of failures to make any significant changes you are left with a choice to try a different way. The N.A. Program not only outlines for us the way to stay clean and learn how to live, it also gives us clear direction on how to put these principles into action in our lives.
unmappedHistorical.moment: we will make today an example of our program in action. We will live clean and participate in the gift of life by doing the footwork we need to do in order to recover.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Being self-supporting is an important part of our new way of life. For the individual, this is usually quite a change.” Grey book
unmappedHistorical.body: Many years of finding ways and means to get more leads us down many different paths when we were using. For some of us who may have been fortunate enough to have enough money to continue a habit uninterrupted by the stumbling; that doing without has brought so many of us. We are used to getting what we want, when we want it. This is the cornerstone of a drug addict. The instant gratification that we found with our drugs is a direct result of living life by this philosophy. Of course, being an addict means that this behavior will take precedence over all other aspects of life. We eventually don’t care about family, loved ones, jobs, friends, children, or society. We are only concerned with getting what we want, and in our case, was more drugs. This usually leaves most of us in a state that makes us feel entitled. This means that if we cannot possibly support this type of lifestyle, then we will find others who will help facilitate this life for us. Whether it’s our parents, or a spouse, we look for people that will help contribute to our destruction a bag at a time, or a pill at a time. After all, if someone close to us tries to get in our way, we generally don’t want that person around us. Life already makes it very difficult to continue in the manner of an active addict, and we certainly wouldn’t want to add to the dilemma by placing ourselves around people that will also make it difficult for us to use. Being selfsupporting in recovery is only brought about by a complete turnaround in our attitudes and our thinking. We no longer feel entitled to, and we no longer feel that the world owes us. This new way of life encourages us to take an active part in life today. And now that we have the tools and the support of addicts in the program, we can carry on without looking to the world to carry us instead.
unmappedHistorical.moment: we can be reassured that as long as we continue in the N.A. way of life, that we never have to be a burden to our loved ones and society as a whole:

unmappedHistorical.quote: “The line between where God does or does not help us is absolutely irrelevant”
unmappedHistorical.body: We as practicing recovering addicts are faced with many choices that we must make in order to continue to grow, and get better. Putting down the drugs and staying clean is for most of us a miracle, that we never were able to do on our own, in the past. So how is it that we can stay abstinent from drugs over days, weeks, months, or years? Learning from those that came before us reaffirms the “coincidences” in our own journey. We can feel Gods love for us the first time that we realize that we haven’t done this on our own this time either. Surely, it must have been God who helped us to clean up and get to the rooms of N.A., because the simple fact that not only were we unable to stay clean on our own, almost all addicts that we talk to in the rooms of N.A. will also have a very similar story. So, what does this mean for us now? Are we to just “let go and let God” do all our work for us? The lines between the effort that we put into our recovery, and the help that God grants us is invisible, and cannot be graphed. However, we must not fall into the trap of thinking that we are now going to be taken care of without doing our footwork that is suggested in the program. Most of us will find that as long as we do the things that are suggested here from our sponsors, the Steps, and other recovering addicts who care for us, then Gods help and presence will be evident in our lives.
unmappedHistorical.moment: we will do our part for our own recovery today. We will put the direction of the program into action, and give 100 percent of ourselves for our own recovery, and leave the rest to God.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “We had been beaten into a corner by our own actions, and we were in the grip of an overwhelming addiction. We had found hope”.
unmappedHistorical.body:
After all the excuses that we had been telling ourselves for all these years during our using, we find ourselves facing a stark truth, that we had been lying to ourselves the entire time, and worse yet, we were believing the lies. Our justifications for our using, and all the actions that lead to the using, were always just whatever means brought us to the end of obtaining and using our drugs. Whomever got hurt or beaten in between were usually just written off as a casualty in the mix. It was obvious that in the beginning we were doing things that we just didn’t like doing, but little by little, we become numb to the actions that at one time in our lives, may have been devastating. These actions escalate as the addiction progresses, and at the same time our denial becomes deeper, and more impossible to penetrate. This is part of the reason why an active addict is nearly impossible to reach, because they have been lying to themselves for so many years, that the truth really has no meaning, and certainly isn’t going to facilitate getting more. Really the hopeless incarceration of ourselves through addiction, is as hopeless a situation that a human being could find themselves in. Our only way out is through the program of N.A., led by addicts who came before us, and have already traveled the path of hopelessness to joyous and free.

Just for today: we will grab onto other recovering addicts that have come before us, and follow the proven path away from the hopeless existence of active addiction.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “We tried limiting our usage to “social” amounts, but our success with this was short- lived or non-existent.”
unmappedHistorical.body: The amount of time we spent trying to control our using as active addicts should be a constant reminder of just how powerless we are over this disease. We may have started as “social” users, but usually, this was at a very young age for many of us. The term “social user” is in and of itself a contradiction of terms, because how can someone be successful socially by partaking in an anti-social activity such as taking drugs. We know too well that any part we may play in partaking in the fabric of society could not be more than just a surface person, with no real deep feelings or emotions. Today, being aware of how futile our attempts at controlling our using reaffirms our surrender to the N.A. Program, and gives powerlessness meaning. After our early stages progressed, we were slowly being taken over by the disease, and the act of using and finding ways and means to get more would also take over more and more of our time. Eventually, this would lead to the final progression of the disease, which found us at the brink of existence, with the sole purpose in life no longer aligned with human wants or needs. We lived to use, and used to live.
unmappedHistorical.moment: we will remember that any attempt to control our using was futile, and short lived. We can admit, and accept our powerlessness based on our past memories of how this disease progressed in our lives in spite of our best efforts.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “It wasn’t until after we came to N.A. that we found out that we had a disease and that recovery was possible for us.”
unmappedHistorical.body: Many of us that get to the rooms of N.A. are here for the simple reason that we cannot continue living the way we were. We can call this our bottom, or maybe it was a part of existing that way, that made us seek out something different. Whatever the reason, we come here with many strange ideas of what we are, what are problem is, and what form help should take for us. How many times did we think that we could eventually think our way out of our dilemma, or that somehow someone could give us that intangible explanation, and solution to our problem. The “miracle” cure that of course required no real work, or sacrifice on our part is what we were after. As many times as we thought we had the answers, is as many times as we found ourselves going deeper down the spiral of addiction. Once here, we are relieved to hear other people, and our literature describe our lives to us. A measure of understanding that we have never experienced before, and a knowledge of this disease that was never divulged to us. We find the meaning of being an addict, and even better we find the proven path to recovery. This is the miracle that addicts speak about here in the rooms of N.A.
unmappedHistorical.moment: we can learn to live with a chronic disease of addiction, by taking responsibility for our recovery. We can be grateful that we have found each other, and support one another in our recovery.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “The most obvious change is the simple fact that we are staying clean”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Sometimes we can forget that in spite of our own negative thinking, and loss of gratitude in our daily lives, that we are usually doing better than we are feeling. When we remain abstinent for another day from drugs, we are that miracle that the literature reminds us of. When we are involved with the hustle and bustle of a busy life, we must remain grounded in the program, and also, we must not forget that we have plenty to be grateful for if we aren’t using. Remembering where we came from, or “keeping it green”, is a good way to be happy with the simple things in life today. After all, we aren’t living to use and use to live anymore. Almost anything that life can throw at us today doesn’t compare to living that life of addiction that we came from. Today with the tools of the program, we can look at life’s challenges as a way to improve ourselves, and our relationships. When we complicate things, we tend to forget that keeping it simple starts with staying clean and being grateful for another day.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will show our gratitude for being clean by looking forward to life’s challenges, and not run away from them.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “We are clean, but by no means perfect and our lives remain unmanageable. We become egotistical from time to time”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Since the addiction has made its way into every area of our lives, it takes quite a bit of change, and time to be able to weed it out of all our behaviors. We start off our changing by tackling the obvious things, like using, steeling, and other things that may have ended us up in jails or institutions. This only brings the problem of addiction to the surface and puts us in a position where we need to either change or die. We are people of advantages, and disadvantages. We have each other as our eyes and ears, because we have a real difficult time seeing the things about ourselves that need changing, and even when we do, we have a tendency to rationalize, and justify instead of accepting them. The “we” part of the N.A. Program has many benefits, and helping each other to make real change in our lives is only one of them. Since we are never truly “cured” of this disease, we will find ourselves struggling with some of the old character traits, such as self-centeredness and ego. We mustn’t lose faith at these times, as our literature tells us. We are only human, and mustn’t put those perfect expectations on ourselves, or we are only setting ourselves up for failure. Recovery is a journey out of the pits of despair, and as any worthwhile journey it will have its pitfalls, and struggles. By staying clean, we choose to live, and continue on that journey instead of falling back into the chains of addiction.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we can take a personal inventory of our own goals, and expectations on ourselves

unmappedHistorical.quote: "We gradually begin to find some order in the universe, and accept that "some power" was supplying us with a conscience we had never had before, and was somehow giving us the power to overcome the compulsion to use".
unmappedHistorical.body: We as addicts may have a difficult time, in keeping track with the evolution we have experienced from before our drug use began. Through our addiction, and now through our recovery we notice many changes taking place. One of the many new-found assets we find is our newly found conscience. Where we were once able to act, or react with malice, or ego we are now not able to get away with it. At least not without knowing the difference today. We are constantly evolving and growing and if we continue to apply the Steps in our lives, we are continually brought to a more conscience contact with our Higher Power. The God of our understanding has been with us all along, and we become more aware of this fact the longer we stay clean. We have a responsibility today to abide by this new conscience we have been given, for it is a gift. We must develop it through the Steps and seek a closer relationship with that Greater Power we find through N.A.
unmappedHistorical.moment: we will work to better understand our Higher Power today through prayer. We will keep in mind today the gift of recovery, and where it has come from in our lives. We will be ready to accept the love that's been there all along

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Many times, our efforts have produced in us feelings of peace and serenity that we have never known before”.
unmappedHistorical.body: When we take our first steps in recovery from addiction, we really don’t know what to expect. Most of us just want to stop hurting and would be happy with that. When we realize that there’s more work to be done, we are given direction, and suggestions by other addicts that have been down this road of recovery for a while. If we choose to follow this path, we will slowly notice that we need to take action on our part, and our actions are met with the help from a Higher Power that we never experienced before. Learning to rely on this power helps us to keep wanting to move forward into this program. After some time, we will build the trust that is talked about in the 2nd Step, and this then puts us in a position to change our lives with endless possibilities ahead. We are no longer controlled by the disease and begin to know peace and serenity.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “The symptoms of addiction include mental states that aren’t normal. When we get clean, these strange habits of mind pass away and we start to learn to live again”.
unmappedHistorical.body: When we were in active addiction, we slowly over years of use develop strange habits. This then becomes what we see as “normal” behavior and thinking. This is fueled partly due to some of our defense mechanisms and learning to hide from our guilt and shame. We learn to suppress our feelings, and instead of dealing with life, ourselves, and others, we slip into a world of strange mannerisms, thoughts, and actions. It takes a while of complete abstinence before we can see a real change. Even though some of the immediate behaviors may stop in the beginning, the thought process behind those behaviors are still there. This and much more is dealt with in our Step work. Being restored to sanity, and coming to believe in a Greater Power, and practicing turning it over all help to not only change the behaviors, but to change the “stinking thinking” behind them.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will practice turning it over to the care of a loving God and look for new positive healthy living habits to make true change in our lives.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Now that we are clean, we have recognized the advantage of getting our own house in order. We can recognize ourselves as the heart of the problem”.
unmappedHistorical.body: The fact that we as addicts can believe wholeheartedly that we are really not the cause of our problems is an example of how cunning and baffling this disease is. We have convinced ourselves, through our own rationalizations for so long, that when we get here, and finally get clean, we still don’t really believe that we are the cause. We still want to point outward, and look to lay blame on others, family, God, society, and just the world in general. Part of the recovery process is learning to take responsibility for our own actions, but this takes time. We must first be able to identify ourselves as having a real disease, that has hijacked us spiritually, and mentally. To be able to identify and accept is all part of our First Step process. Getting to know ourselves through regular meeting attendance and working on getting honest with others is really the practice we need in order to start identifying who we are, and what are real problems are. This is half the battle, and once we can, we can then begin to fix some of the things that are wrong. It must all start with ourselves.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we can identify our problem, and through acceptance, and a reliance on a loving God, we can work on getting our own house in order.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Those of us who stay, do so for the same reasons, to stop using and stay clean”.
unmappedHistorical.body: When we first get to the N.A. Program, we are tired of the pain, and hurting that the drugs have caused us. We just want to stop the pain and stay clean. This holds true for addicts even after we have been here a while. We never want to be returned to the misery of addiction, but we also don’t like the pain that addiction can cause us, even if we are not using drugs. We are all addicts who only get a daily reprieve from this disease, if we are maintaining our recovery program, and attending meetings. We couldn’t do this alone before we got here, and we still can’t. The N.A. Program offers us one main promise, that we never need be returned to the misery of addiction, and in order to receive this, we must continue to come around. Addicts that try and leave N.A. after some time clean, eventually are returned to some of the insanity, and pain that addiction holds for us, if they don’t use all together. For those of us that have had enough and are sick and tired of being sick and tired, we don’t need to follow that path. If we follow this way, we have nothing to fear.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will keep on the recovery path and put recovery first in our lives by applying the Steps.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “The mental part of our addiction comes with our inability to deal with life on its own terms”.
unmappedHistorical.body: The mental part of our addiction is only a part of this disease. We suffer mentally, physically, spiritually, and emotionally from the disease of addiction, and need recovery in all these areas if we are to achieve a true recovery. In order to keep ourselves on track to achieving this, we must relearn all that we thought we knew in the past. If we take a good look at ourselves, and our inventory in our Step process, we will notice that even though we thought we knew how to deal with the ordeal of life, we really didn’t. We suffered from a disease that keeps us from being able to meaningfully interact with others and take part in life. We were more interested during our active addiction in surviving and getting more drugs. Unfortunately, this doesn’t change with just abstinence alone. We must slowly learn, one day at a time, how to deal with others, and life on life’s terms. This means that we need to surrender to the Steps, and look for a Higher Power’s help, along with others in the program. We strive for the mental recovery from the insanity that the disease has put us in, and with a little faith in the program of N.A., and the help of others we meet who are recovering as well, we can be restored to a sane way of thought.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will look to strengthen our faith in the program, and trust that this process work, in order to achieve a restoration of sanity, one day at a time.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “We are able to love the unlovable and discover self-acceptance. We are not likely to create problems in our daily living. We finally realize that we have a choice in the matter of our lives. “
unmappedHistorical.body: Let’s face it, we are not the most loveable people at the end of our addiction. We get clean, and start the process of going to meetings, and being around other addicts like ourselves. We are hopefully, coming out of the lifestyle that kills many of us, and our fractured personalities haven’t even begun to heal. To be accepted in the rooms is one of the most important part of keeping us coming back. How many times in our lives, did we try and fit in, only to be rejected. Most of us have developed this pattern since grade school, or as soon as we started to mingle with other kids our age. We would rebel against the idea of needing anyone, as we self- medicated to hide the pain we felt when we were not accepted. We eventually would hide behind the drugs. Yet disguising that desire through the lie that told us that we didn’t want or need anyone’s help, approval, love, or acceptance. One of the freedoms we experience from living a life without drugs, is the comfort of being accepted in our families, and society as a whole, if we choose to participate constructively. Another freedom we gain from N.A. is being able to make that choice today. Only through the love and acceptance that we get from the Fellowship do we gain the necessary foundation to move through other areas of our life without the fear of making the same mistakes that got us here in the first place.
unmappedHistorical.moment: we will love the addict coming in the door. We will put aside our differences, and welcome them into the program that has given us back our lives

unmappedHistorical.quote: “We agree that there is nothing shameful about being an addict provided we accept our dilemma and honestly take action”.
unmappedHistorical.body: We are not responsible for our disease, but we are responsible for our recovery. This is a reminder that our literature tells us, that we really don’t have any room in our new lives for added guilt and shame for being an addict in the first place. We carry enough of that with us through the doors here and have a Step process in place in order to help us to recover from that. We are of course responsible for our actions today. We cannot go back and change the past. We see countless addicts in this program who have learned to overcome their past by working the program and keeping their attention on the 24 hours in front of them. The first thing we learn after we get clean, is that we do in fact have a choice now, as long as we are willing to follow this simple program. If we choose not to take that choice and revert back to our usual way of doing things, then we will surely end up with the same results that we have encountered in the past, which is a life controlled by the disease of addiction. We can help ourselves to overcome the shame and guilt of our past actions by taking positive Steps each day to improve ourselves, and to get another day’s reprieve from the disease of addiction.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will take an active part in our recovery, so that we can feel good about our lives today instead of feeling ashamed and guilty for who we are

unmappedHistorical.quote: “The fact that those of us who have become addicted come from all levels of society is no guarantee that we will not end our addiction in jail or the graveyard”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Addiction has no prejudices. It will affect anyone, from any race, color, creed, or class of human. We find many different people when we get to N.A., from all walks of life. From doctors, to lawyers, to street junkies, we all have one common problem, addiction. Although, we may think that if we had a good job, like being a doctor or lawyer we would be immune to the effects of this disease. The fact that there are just as many addicted professionals in jails, institutions, and the graveyard as the less affluent addicts proves that this disease is just as devastating to anyone’s life, no matter where we fit in on the social ladder. It has one goal, to bring us down to the bottom, whether that is through institutionalizing us for the rest of our lives, or simply killing us. Although, some of us end up with more “things”, and material goods when we get here, it is the mental and spiritual bankruptcy that ultimately puts us in the same state of despair. We cannot escape the effects of addiction simply because we have more stuff. The flip side of this is also true. No matter who we are when we get here, the program of N.A. will help us to bring ourselves out of the pits of despair that the addiction leaves us in. This program works for anyone regardless of age, race, sex, color, or creed, and saves us from the guaranteed ends of addiction, jails, institutions, or death.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “There is nothing that compares to a new person freely talking about the pain and endless hustle that goes on out there”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Listening to others at our meetings is one of the tools we learn to develop when we get to N.A. The importance of truly listening, to hear what someone is sharing is important for us to achieve that empathy that we have for each other. It also helps to hear the pain of an addict that has just made it here. A brand newcomer may not know much about recovery from addiction, but they do have a message of pain and misery that they come from, and this will help to remind us of where we were when we got here. This is an important piece of our own recovery, because it simply reminds us that we never want to go back to that life of active addiction. We listen to the newcomers, and then we can talk with them after the meeting, exchange phone numbers, and offer help so that they can stay here and receive the benefits of this program as we did. The endless circle of recovery begins with the newcomer and playing our role in the helping of others is how it continues. Relapse is not a requirement here, and if we stay attentive and learn to hear others as we listen, this will help assure that we never have to relapse ourselves. When we can truly feel the newcomers pain, we are the only ones in position to truly help that person.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will practice helping a newcomer, and sharing our experience strength, and hope with them

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Our personal experiences while using differed from member to member. However, as a group we found many common themes in our addiction”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Hearing our literature for the first time or attending one of our N.A. meetings for the first time can be an eye-opening experience. This is when we get to hear our story told through others. All our lives we probably thought that we were the only ones that felt that, did that, said that or experienced that. We were alone. Once we get to N.A., we realize that we are not alone, but we share a common disease, that isolates us all individually, and keeps us that way if we keep using. The lie that we are different begins to melt away when we listen to others share at our meetings, and we can for the first time begin to feel like we are a part of the human race again. It is important to keep focused on our similarities, not our differences so that we can experience this change. This is all part of the recovery from addiction process, and somehow God sees fit to bring us together in order to help each other. A group of people that alone are powerless and isolated, yet together are able to do together what individually we could not. Keeping this in mind as we attend our meetings, and fellowship with others in N.A. will give us a perspective on the power of this program, and the divine intervention that God grants us together.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will be a part of the Fellowship of N.A. by being a part of others life and staying connected with others seeking recovery from addiction.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “One of the most important parts of our new way of life is being part of a group of addicts also seeking recovery”.
unmappedHistorical.body: A very important lesson that we learn when we are in N.A., is that we can’t do this alone. When we were using, we felt that we didn’t need people around. The benefits of a “social” life seemed pale in comparison to our drug of choice, and we put using ahead of being part of anything. We didn’t feel that we needed people. When we stop our using, and begin to find recovery, we find just the opposite is true. Not only do we need each other to stay clean, and to grow, we also need the emotional stability that being around, and part of others’ lives brings. God often works through others, and we are shutting ourselves out from that help if we are not actively participating in others’ lives. Today, we seek out a productive, and social life, and that includes other people. This is an important part of our recovery. When we can admit that we need others help, and be open to others criticism of us, we are practicing humility, and acceptance, two key N.A. principles. The “we” part of the N.A. Program is how we stay clean, and it is also how we learn to integrate into society as a whole.
unmappedHistorical.moment: we will ask God to guide us in our relationships with others, and to help us better ourselves, so that we can be a better part of others’ lives today.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “We may suffer from the fear of insanity and feel we have no escape from using other than an insane and depressed existence”.
unmappedHistorical.body: How many of us end up being institutionalized for life as a result of active addiction? We hear the ends of addiction bring us jails, institutions, and death, and most certainly view death as the worst of these ends. But many of us have a greater fear of ending up in an institution and labeled criminally insane. Once we are put in these places, it is nearly impossible to get out. We can become nothing more than a state funded paycheck, that gets lost in the system. This is just one of the stark realities that addicts face when we are in our active addiction. Along with all the other destruction that this disease can bring, it also can bring a fate worse than death. If we were lucky enough to get to the rooms of N.A., we are offered a solution. A different path that saves us from the fate that addiction has planned for us. We need to be grateful for not having to live with the fear hanging over our heads that we are at the mercy of a disease that unlike our Higher Power, is not loving and caring, and wants nothing more than to have us suffer a miserable existence. Today we share this hope with others who come into the rooms, and offer them a choice at life, and an escape from the fear, and insanity that keeps them chained.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we show our gratitude for our recovery, by sharing the message of hope and promise of freedom with other suffering addicts.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Each day we stay clean by practicing the Steps in our lives, our chances of relapse decrease”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Learning how to live without using drugs takes more than simple abstinence. We slowly begin to learn new habits as part of the N.A. Program. Making meetings regularly, making phone calls, working with a sponsor, and others in the program all help us to begin to see a new outlook on life. For many of us, it will be the first time in our lives that we can view life and others without the negative doom and gloom lenses of the disease. As our mannerisms begin to change and we notice that we look forward to doing things that don’t include using, we are pointed to spiritual principles in our 12 Steps. By working the N.A. Steps with a sponsor, we can identify spiritual principles that are helping us make these changes, as we practice incorporating them in our daily living situations. This is a journey that begins with that first admission of powerlessness and continues for as long as we don’t pick up. If we continually focus on the solutions, and keep our recovery first in our lives, we are taking an active part in preventing the disease from pulling us back in. Relapse does not need to be a part of our new lives, as long as we stay clean, and follow the N.A. way.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will assure ourselves another day clean by making a meeting and practicing these principles in all our affairs.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “We all have to pull together, and in pulling together we learn that we really are a part of something greater than ourselves”.
unmappedHistorical.body: When a group of addicts get together for the purpose of recovery from addiction, we are practicing one of the greatest tools we have in defense of the disease. We no longer are alone and have become a part of a greater fellowship through the N.A. Program. Meeting others at meetings, and fellowshipping with them gives us a mutual solution, to a mutual problem of addiction. We all suffered from this disease in one form or another and have found each other because of the N.A. Program. As we begin to stop being that angry frightened loner, and allow others into our lives, we begin to feel the benefits of living an honest, clean life. This can be frightening for an addict who never wanted to be honest with anyone, and practiced deception, and isolation. The greatest defense against the disease is honest sharing with others, and allowing the healing power of empathy to do for us what we are unable to do for ourselves. A group of recovering addicts have a great power when we work together for a common cause of recovering from the disease of addiction, and helping a newcomer. We can put our personalities, and personal agendas aside, and allow the healing power of God to work through us. Passing along what we have been given through N.A., to the still suffering addict is one of the greatest gifts, and assures that we will not only keep what we have, but that we will gain the spiritual benefits that we so desperately need in order for us to grow.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we can practice putting our own selfish motives aside for the greater good of helping another suffering addict.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “We tried to cover up our inner pain with outside appearances. Any hope of being anything different disappeared”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Getting honest with ourselves about how we are feeling is a difficult task for addicts, and it takes quite a bit of practice when we first get to the N.A. Program. We learn at our first N.A. meetings that the more we can open up honestly to others, the more relief we will experience from ourselves. We tend to hide, and cover up our feelings, as an automatic mechanism so that we can portray being a human being that is just “fine”. Underneath the facade is really that shaky insecure person that our literature tells us about. We can only hide the pain from others and ourselves for so long though, and the more we avoid our true feelings, the longer we stay sick in the disease, and eventually will lose hope. We cannot falter in our programs, and practicing a life of continuing honesty is always the first step in growth for addicts. We cannot afford to be “different” then others today, where once we felt that we were so very different from every other human being, today we celebrate the identification, and empathy we share with other addicts that are just like we are.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will not hide our feelings from others, by getting to a meeting and sharing honestly about where we are, and how we feel.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “If we really believe that a person is wrong, we have no business letting that person have control of our emotions”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Having surrendered to program of N.A. means that we do not have to fight anymore. We no longer need to fight this addiction on our own, and we have admitted powerlessness in order to get here. We must now learn to deal with life, and others without using drugs as an escape from others, and ourselves. In other words, we must learn to function as healthy human beings capable of participating in our own life, and the lives of others. How do we do this? If we continue to run away from our own problems, and defects, then chances are we are continuing to fight with others. Continually needing to prove ourselves right is just another way of feeding our own ego’s, and to feed the narrative that we are just fine, while others are not. We all know where this behavior got us in the past, using drugs. Today, although we may not be using anymore we are still prone to these same egos feeding behaviors, and making ourselves feel better at the expense of others is sure to lead to some of the same pain and misery that using has. We may find ourselves alone, or constantly being avoided, which works in contradiction to what we really need, being around others, and being able to connect with others. Our literature tells us to “give ourselves a break”. This means not only from using drugs, but from the constant fighting with life in general. Today we are in good hands through being connected to the N.A. Program and God.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will surrender, and not fight with others over “petty” stuff, and not allow others to take control of our own emotions.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “By following these principles in our dealings with others in N.A. and society at large, we avoid many problems”.
unmappedHistorical.body: In order to become the productive member of society again, as our literature promises us, we need to continually follow the path of spiritual principles. By keeping our recovery first in our lives, over time, we are able to carry what we learn here in N.A. out into the outside world. As we share in meetings, and listen to others share, we can hear the solutions as well as the problems that addicts have as we slowly integrate back into society in a healthy way. We can learn through our meetings what to do in certain situations, also what not to do. If we follow the positive messages that we hear, we will learn that they all share one common denominator. They all follow spiritual principles. The obvious ones such as honesty, open mindedness, and willingness, but also the ones such as giving, kindness, and empathy for others. We learn that these principles keep our own egos in check, also help to guide us through any difficult situation that may arise in our life. The moment we abandon these principles laid out in the N.A. Program is when we find ourselves in trouble, and it’s usually our own doing. Our ability to make decisions with the help of others in N.A. will help us to avoid some of these problems, but we also develop the ability to learn from our mistakes today. We are no longer doomed to repeat the same mistakes over and over as we were while we were using. Problems we encounter today, are only temporary setbacks as long as we utilize the tools we are given, and continually ask for guidance from God and others.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we can move past a problem by admitting to another addict that we need help and guidance. Today we don’t have all the answers, but we can find the solutions.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Freedom from our destructiveness, covering up the wreckage of the past has been the main stumbling block in relating to others”.
unmappedHistorical.body: We all come to this program with people issues. We as addicts just don’t know how to effectively relate to others. There are many reasons for this, but through our active addiction, we continually compounded this problem by using. While using we are not facing, and in touch with our own true selves. In fact, the opposite, we are running further and further away from ourselves by using. This continuous act repeated for weeks, months, and years will leave us in a dark place that has no real attachment to another human being. Our literature tells us we are left completely isolated from the rest of the world, and any addict who has made it to N.A. can relate to that first hand. Now that we are clean, we need to face all of our past, and first recognize how we were not in touch with ourselves, or our own defects. To first face ourselves, and our defects of character is the first step in being able to relate to others. We need to be free from our own past limitations in order to move forward in a positive way, for our own life, and for being able to participate with the lives of others.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will face our own fears by sharing them with another recovering addict, and admitting we need help

unmappedHistorical.quote: ‘‘It will not make us better persons to judge the faults of another”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Many of us come into the program blaming everything, and everybody for our situation. We never were able to take a look at our drug use, or ourselves as the problem that caused all of our suffering. Putting down the drugs, and getting to a meeting doesn’t change the finger pointing that we find with newcomers. We still want to blame the world and everybody in it for what happened to us. As we begin working on ourselves, and dive into our 12-Step work, we begin to point that finger inward, and identify the real problem, ourselves. However, we still have a tendency to want to “escape” from where the real work lies, and start taking other people’s inventories instead. When we find ourselves being too judgmental, or constantly pointing out the faults of others, it usually is because we are avoiding our own defects, and the work that is required to deal with them. Understanding, and identifying our own faults brings us to a fork in the road. Do we deal with them and ask a loving God, and others in the program for the help and guidance we need, or do we run away from them? Having an honest desire to better ourselves, and to better our lives leaves us with only one answer, and focusing on others is not part of the solutions that we are after.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will keep the focus on ourselves, and face our own problems head on. We won’t procrastinate in our recovery program by judging others.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Our way got us here. Recovery was done through the help of others, the tools they shared with us, and a Higher Power”.
unmappedHistorical.body: When we look back on our journey through our active addiction, and recovery from this disease, we find that the time that we began to turn around from our past life, was when we were beaten enough to start to rely on the help of others. If we were lucky enough to find N.A., and have been demoralized enough to let go of the steering wheel for a while, we can see that this is the point that things began to change for us. Allowing others to help us at our most vulnerable time, and seeing positive changes in our lives, gives us a chance to see that our way of thinking isn’t all we thought it was cracked up to be. In fact, we can safely see that our dilemma in life is a direct result of our thinking. We are then built up in our meetings by feeling accepted in spite of all our faults, and problems. We look to others to show us what has worked for them, and we find that simple tools of the program can make the difference between us staying clean, or returning to a life of misery. If we pick up the tools of writing, fellowshipping, meetings, praying, and reading N.A. literature, we find that we are able to do something that we never were able to do before, get out of our own way, and begins to grow as a human being again. We develop together, and learn that we need each other in order to keep our recovery going. Today we continue working the tools of N.A., so we never have to go back to living that old way of life, and end up where addiction wants us, jails, institutions, and death.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today, we will strengthen our recovery, by working the tools we learned here in the rooms of N.A.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Another stumbling block we should safeguard against is comparing ourselves to others who seem to have gone farther down the road of addiction”.
unmappedHistorical.body: How many times have we said or though, “i never did that”., or “i would never get that bad”. Only to find that we did end up doing that, and we did get that bad. Comparing ourselves to others is dangerous in recovery as well. We cannot find ourselves looking at what others do or “get away with”, and go to our sponsors and say, “so and so does it all the time”. We must learn early on that we are our own person, with our own needs for a personal recovery, and that is where our focus must lie. When we find ourselves looking outward, at others, it is usually because we are neglecting to take that serious look at our own issues, that maybe we are not ready to change yet. Instead of seeking the help and guidance on our issues, we are more than happy to point out the faults of others. Our literature tells us that it does not make us better by pointing out the faults of others. When we are at the point when we seem to be judging and taking other’s inventories, we need to go back to some simple tools that have worked for many of us. Taking time to take a daily inventory in writing helps, and writing down all the positive messages we heard at a meeting is another simple tool. We are here for no one but ourselves. We are not in competition with each other, but are here to use what we learn through our own journeys to reach out and help others.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will keep the focus on ourselves, and our own recovery so that we can carry a clear message of recovery through experience, strength and hope.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “It is difficult to get rid of the notion that we must be great or do great to be o.k.”
unmappedHistorical.body: We are often doing a lot better than we are feeling. Often addicts tend to get over emotional, when our feelings get out of wack. We always strive to achieve an emotional balance, and get off the roller coaster ride that a lot of us experience in early recovery. Our emotions and feelings can often still throw us for a loop every once in a while, and that’s when we need to put our program into action. Not acting out based on our feelings is something we work on our entire lives, and although we all fall short sometimes, we use our shortcomings as a learning tool today, instead of spiraling deeper into an emotional pit of bad decisions, and actions. Feelings come and go, it’s what we do with them when they are here that matters. Not picking up, and not acting out are the first step to a better way. Learning to let go, and sometimes just allow ourselves the time to think things through also gives us an advantage over our addict thinking. Being ok today means that we are not using, and that we are striving for a better life. It also means that we aren’t allowing the disease to creep back into our thinking, and behaviors. We all have dreams and aspirations for ourselves, but focusing on our recovery allows us the ability to put things into a perspective that we otherwise would miss. The program of N.A. offers us a life free from addiction, and the ability to enjoy living a life clean, and this give us hope for our future.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will not act out on feelings and emotions, but accept where we are today, and strive for a better tomorrow.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “We came in sick people who knew very little about how to be happy and enjoy life”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Although we always seemed to think that we knew what was best for us, and for our lives, in spite all evidence to the contrary, it isn’t until we are clean for a while that we see how untrue that was. We as addicts are hard headed, and it takes us following our own thinking until we think ourselves into jails, institutions or dead until we realize that maybe we don’t know everything. Understanding and accepting that our best thinking is what got us to the program in the first place is usually only followed after we have hit bottom, and become willing to try something different. Our idea of living was really an idea of dying a slow and torturous life until we find ourselves in jails, institutions, or dead. Once we are lucky enough to have another chance in N.A., we are ready to take suggestions, and follow direction from those who came before us. We find a whole new outlook on life, and begin to enjoy the simple things, such as being clean, and having the ability to participate instead of hiding away and isolating. Being a part of the N.A. fellowship, and staying on this path of recovery leads to a happiness that we never thought possible before. Today we have a choice to live instead of being controlled by the disease which leads to certain death.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will look for the positive in our lives, and find gratitude for the second chance at life that N.A. offers us.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “What we have in common is what we have all felt: the loneliness, the self- centeredness, the misery, the despair, the pain within, and the empty numbness that sets us apart from others”
unmappedHistorical.body: The empathy that one addict has for another is the greatest healing tool that we have for each other. When we are around other addicts who have “been there” , we are around the people that can help us the most. The understanding of the pain and isolation that we have all felt gives us all the common thread that enables us to help each other, understand each other, and to feel like we belong. This is why the program of N.A. is a “we” program. We together can do what each addict cannot do individually. It also gives us the unique ability to help a newcomer like no one else can. The initial excuse a newcomer gives, that “you don’t know what it’s like”, or “you don’t understand” doesn’t work anymore when that newcomer finds himself around other recovering addicts. Any person who has overcome the total despair that an addict must overcome, along with escaping the jails, institution, or death that addiction had in mind for us, we now have the ability to use the failures of our past to strengthen the ties that bind us together. Our addictive natures will always try and separate us from each other, and we have noticed that an addict that separates himself from those who can help him the most is a sign of relapse. The strength we have together means we must stay together.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will participate in the “we” of the program by reaching out and communicating with other recovering addicts.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “There is the inventory we can pause and make when we run into trouble during the course of the day. Stopping, thinking and remembering that by the grace of God we are clean is a basic”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Each day brings a new set of problems. We as addicts must remember first and foremost that we are powerless over our addictions, and we no longer live with the illusion that we are in control of life on life’s terms. This means we must learn to utilize some of the same tools that have helped us to stay clean, to get through tough times. First and foremost, we are grateful for being clean today. Finding gratitude for the graces that God grants us on a daily basis sets up an attitude of finding a solution for whatever problem life has thrown at us. After all, if we can overcome the obsession and compulsion of addiction, then we certainly, with the help of the program and God, can relearn how to move through the adversities of life without reacting negatively or using. This also takes practice though, and as we develop new living skills through the program, we practice applying what we learn in our meetings to everyday life. The applying of the spiritual principles in all our affairs is our goal, and we achieve this one Step at a time. Today we are not alone. Inviting other recovering addicts into our lives gives us an edge over the disease, which wants us to back into a corner we can’t get out of clean when life throws us a curve ball. We put together a successful life by putting together one successful day clean at a time.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will take time out of our day to give thanks to God for giving us a new chance at life, and to express gratitude daily.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Each day we stay clean by practicing the Steps in our lives, our chances of relapse decrease”.
unmappedHistorical.body: As addicts we mustn’t forget that we are only one drug away from a painful active addiction. We are living a new life based on honesty and are grateful for having another chance at life. Today our living problems are temporary setbacks, that we can learn from and move forward in the solutions. This was unheard of in our addictions, we would be bound to our bad habits without hope of escaping on our own power. Relapse is a choice today, and for any addict who has had enough pain, we choose life instead. As we look inwards in our Step work we find an ability to face problems instead of running away from them. Together we share our experience, strength and hope with each other so that we can continue to enjoy a life free of addiction. Daily practice of the twelve Steps helps us to change. We eventually overcome all the odds each and every day that we don’t pick up a drug. Working a daily program is what ensures our success, and gives us the ability to become the productive members of society. Relapse is not a requirement.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we can continue to have a choice to live by practicing the principles of N.A. in our life today

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Peace of mind was non-existent. The only relief was a comparatively short lived “high”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Achieving balance for addicts is a result of many years of working on ourselves. We were living life based on high highs, and the lowest lows. We didn’t experience a lot of middle ground on almost anything in life, and we really never sought after this. We as addicts come into the program this way too. As our bodies detox from the drugs, we experience even more emotional roller coaster rides emotionally. This is a critical time for newcomers, and utilizing the meetings, sharing, and fellowshipping with other recovering people is crucial to help stable our thoughts. We often acted on feelings in a negative way, and always found ourselves in trouble as a result of this. Today we benefit by sitting on our hands and allowing the feelings to pass without acting on them. This is the beginning of finding a balance for the recovering addict. When we sit and listen at a meeting, make some phone calls to other addicts, and do some writing, instead of acting out we find ourselves at the other side of trouble, and somehow this time we avoided it. Pointing the finger inwards instead of blaming others for our situations is another way that we learn to keep the focus on ourselves. By practicing these simple tools in our new life, slowly we can and do achieve a new balance that is comforting in comparison to seeking the highs and lows.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will seek to have a balance in our lives by inviting God through prayer and meditation into our lives
