unmappedHistorical.quote: “There are certain situations that demand more then we have to give. We should avoid these or seek help if we find ourselves already in such a situation”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Keeping ourselves honest in our daily lives is how we can accurately assess exactly where we are, and what we are able to handle. If we are not living clean, and not being as honest as we can with ourselves and others, then we may find ourselves in situations that we are just unable to deal with. Honestly sharing our fears, and concerns with other recovering addicts will help to get us back in the right direction. We have a tendency to want to either take on more than we can handle, or just the opposite and hide from responsibility. Living with a balance is a new and rewarding idea that requires practice on our part. This is true throughout our recovery process. As newcomers we are told that we should not make major decisions without first talking with our sponsors, and others in the program. The old ideas that we can handle the ordeal of life on our own will haunt us throughout our recovery. This is especially dangerous for us when we are new here. The acting out on such thoughts as a newcomer is almost a guaranteed relapse. Later on, in our journey, we may still become overly confident, and find ourselves getting into situations, that will require help from others, along with some humility, or humiliation to get out of. Keeping an honest daily inventory helps to keep us grounded enough to avoid such situations and can also help us to strengthen our own relationship with ourselves.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we can take an inventory of our daily activities, and seek help and guidance from others in order to keep us out of harm’s way

unmappedHistorical.quote: “If we allow ourselves to stagnate and cling to our old ways of desperation and fear, our chances of real and lasting recovery decrease”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Now that we are clean in the program of N.A. our common effort now is ongoing recovery. We develop new living skills, and a new set of daily patterns to ensure that we continue on this path. This includes a continuing participation in the program of Narcotics Anonymous, and an ongoing inventory of our own behavior patterns. When we listen to those who have struggled with any ongoing recovery, we tend to hear the same things. They almost always stop going to meetings and stop doing one or more of the things that got them to this point in the first place. We must remember that if we do not have this new way of life, all we are left with is our old living patterns. Desperation, and fear were the motivating factors in almost all our thoughts and actions when we were using, and they can easily creep back into our lives today, clean, if we do not keep a vigilante program of recovery first in our lives today. We learn to share with others, when we feel stagnate, and feel that we need a little encouragement to get back on track. Once we get back to actively practicing the program of N.A., we feel the fear and desperation lesson, and a fresh new outlook on life emerges.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today, we will continue on in this quest for recovery, and continually work to improve our lives, and the lives of those around us.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “It seems that being powerless is a huge stumbling block. Whenever a situation arises for us to admit our powerlessness, we first look for ways to exert power against it”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Fighting against the disease of addiction has taken up most of our lives. We were on the path of destruction, at the hands of a spiritual disease that had full control over us. Just breaking that grip of despair is a miracle in and of itself. That took some divine intervention from a loving God. This doesn’t mean that we are cured however, and the sooner we accept and believe that we are truly powerless over the disease of addiction, the sooner we can begin to feel the benefits of the program of N.A. When we are bombarded by life’s challenges we too can have a hard time. Situations, and problems of either our own making, or of circumstances beyond us will occur. When we face life’s challenges today, we must first keep our ego’s in check, by reminding ourselves that we are addicts, and we don’t control everything. We learn to take a Step back and meditate on this before we take actions today. Finding out what we do have the ability to change today about ourselves, and our situations is what we pray for in our serenity prayer. Knowing when to ask for help is one of our greatest tools, and we do these things before we take action. Our first instinct as addicts is to look for the easy way out of problems. We don’t like to do the work and we don’t like change. Over time, we experience enough setbacks, and pain to tell us that our way just doesn’t work, and is almost guaranteed to bring us more pain, and misery. When we feel that we’ve wasted too much of our precious life and want to show gratitude for being alive and free today, we try something different and welcome these positive changes.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will stop looking for the easy way out, and instead take the necessary Steps towards the solution using the principles we learn from the N.A. Program.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Our addiction developed in us an emotional instability. We became very sluggish or glum w/out drugs”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Whatever our living situation was before we started using, it most certainly became worse after. This too is true for our own emotional state. Although addiction doesn’t discriminate against race, creed, religion, or sex it most certainly will affect everyone no matter where they begin emotionally, mentally, physically, and spiritually, the same. It brings all of us that are in its grips down a slippery path with destructive ends. If we had troubles dealing with life before we used, then we have certainly not made that better by putting years of drug induced highs between us and ourselves. After we get clean, we are left with a fractured personality as a result of this, and an emotional mess. On top of our already damaged lives, it becomes evident that we have a lot of work to do in order to get back in touch with ourselves so that we can take inventory and make corrective changes. The miracles we experience here is the newly found joy we experience clean.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we can enjoy learning to live clean one day at a time, just for the moment at times.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “we are encouraged to work the 12 Steps, practice the 12 Traditions, go to meetings, get a sponsor, find a home group and ask for help”.
unmappedHistorical.body: One of the many benefits of our program is that we pass on freely what was given to us. The tools we need to recover. What addict makes it here with a few hours, or days clean and knows what do? If we don’t have some direction from other addicts who want to help us, we are doomed to repeat our old insanity. If we want to participate in our own recovery, and find a new way to live, we must utilize the tools of the program. After practicing these simple tools, over time we come to realize that they are what stands between us and relapse. Our literature reminds us that there are no musts in N.A., however, if we truly want to change and become that productive member of society we will only achieve this by doing some work on our fractured personalities. We have an incurable disease and yet we continually put a day at a time, clean and free, from the disease of addiction.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will practice our recovery program, so we never need be returned to the insanity of addiction, as long as we practice the 12 Steps daily

unmappedHistorical.quote: “We want constantly to remind the newcomer and ourselves that there are plenty of people ready and able to help”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Once we realize that we cannot stay clean on our own, we are forced to look to others in the program for help. We must learn to trust others, as difficult as this may be for some, it’s a matter of life and death for the addict. This requires a new-found surrender, and acceptance first of our own powerlessness over this disease. If we cannot admit powerlessness we will be unable to accept help from others. As a newcomer it is important to cling to those who came before us in this program. This enables us to look for guidance through the program. Eventually, we find that little by little we are more able to have an open mind for new ideas. Surrounding ourselves with other recovering addicts gives us all the ability to do together what we cannot do alone. We must develop new healthy habits if we hope to stay clean and learning from others is the best way to get the right guidance on how to achieve this. We learn to open up in our meetings and invite others into our lives, so we can be available to accept the help. Little by little, we are learning a new set of living skills, that will help us through all of life’s situations, and save our life.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will be available to help others and accept help from people in the program who care for our recovery

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Humility is a part of staying clean, as food and water are to staying alive”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Understanding the humility talked about in our Seventh Step means that we must first understand our need to keep God above our own wants and desires. When we begin to find ourselves getting angry at God for life not going our way we can usually take a look at our own egos and find the answers there. This disease will continually try and work its way back into our thinking and edging God out is the first way it has in order to achieve this. When we begin blaming God for our own shortcomings instead of humbly asking him to remove them, then we have edged God out and have reversed roles. We need to take our own inventory at this point, and re - evaluate our belief in God. As addicts we tend to forget sometimes that God doesn’t work for us. We can feel anger, or resentments at life, and God sometimes also, but these feelings can be worked through in our meetings and talking with other addicts. When we begin to work through some of these destructive aspects of our personalities, we can then begin to work on humility. Of course, this, like all other spiritual principles are not a “once and done” fix. We must continually maintain our spiritual condition on a daily basis in order to ward off the old insanities from creeping back into our thinking. We take comfort today in knowing that we do not have to do it alone today. We have others in the program, and a loving and caring God to help us each day to stay clean, and to work through life on life’s terms.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will humbly ask him to remove our shortcomings and share our struggles with another addict instead of acting out on them.

unmappedHistorical.quote: ” Belief is the beginning. It is helpful to stop at this point to review our thinking in this respect. We should not take the chance that our understanding of a power greater than ourselves is sufficient”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Understanding God, or a Higher Power in the program of Narcotics Anonymous is what we work towards when we begin our Step work. What beliefs and understandings we come into the program obviously didn’t work for us, or we wouldn’t be here. The great part of the program of N.A. is that it is not a religious program. It deals specifically with the building and rebuilding of a relationship between our own individual God and ourselves. We can learn from the group, and we can utilize the group as a Higher Power to lead us to this understanding, but eventually we need to take that Step out on the ledge of a spiritual journey ourselves. Our book tells us that we should feel comfortable with our Higher Power and make sure that this power is loving and caring. Many addicts make the mistake of clinging to old beliefs or jumping into new religious practices only to be carried out the door. We mustn’t forget that we are addicts first, and it is the program of N.A. that has opened the door for this relationship with God to begin with. Without it, we are lost back in addiction seeking nothing more than instant gratification in one form or another and trying to fill the “God box” with anything but God. We want to take heed to our literature and give ourselves the ability to grow spiritually, and this means we must honestly seek our own recovery, so we are better able to have a meaningful relationship with our Higher Power.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will seek a better understanding of our Higher Power through prayer and meditation. We will humbly ask for help today

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Modern drug technology and media attention have made a social anti-hero of the addict. Since many of us were street addicts, we dealt in illicit drugs and lived criminally”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Our literature reminds us that the most natural thing for an addict to do is to use. Each day that we stay clean another miracle happens. After living a life of hiding from the world, and the law, we are labeled by society as criminals, and beyond help. Many of us end up in jails, institutions, or dead. When we first get clean, and stay clean for a while, many of us can feel the miracle happening in our own lives for the first time. This doesn’t mean that society or others around us, such as family members will change the way they look at us. We are here for ourselves, and we don’t change what we do based on the views or opinions of people outside the program. This is a life or death situation for us, and unless we want to be returned to all the negative things that outsiders think or say about us, we don’t concern ourselves with them. Eventually, if we stay clean long enough, and continue to work the program so that we can become productive members of society, we can function in the world and become part of society again. As our recovery progresses it becomes less important what others think of us, and as long as we find ourselves honest with ourselves, and the God of our understanding, we know that we are right where we belong. No longer are we running from ourselves, society or God.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will be part of another miracle when we stay clean, and recover from the disease of addiction

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Eventually, when we sincerely use this program of action in our daily lives, we will be able to face our Higher Power, ourselves, our loved ones, and even the “cold, cruel world”.
unmappedHistorical.body: This program is one of attraction, and the way in which we make our own recovery attractive to other addicts is by living these principles in our daily lives. Besides helping us to stay clean, and to deal with all the adversity of life, it also will give us the ability to help other addicts, by attracting them to be a part of our lives. As we continue to work this program we will notice that the world changes before our eyes to give us a new, fresh outlook on life, with a new enthusiasm for living. This cannot be achieved without first learning to face ourselves, in spite of some of the darkest secrets we may have avoided for many years. Once we work through the 12 Steps of the program we learn that facing these “demons” within, is what gives us the most freedom. Once we learn that we don’t need to be first anymore, we can Step out of our own way and begin to do what’s best for ourselves. We no longer need to live irresponsible, and self-serving lives that leave us alone, and with a feeling of emptiness inside. Today, clean, we work towards spiritual rewards, that will ensure our continued success in life.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we can look the world in the eye and know that we can get through anything with the help of our Higher Power, and the Fellowship of N.A.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Life with these defects may cause perpetual frustration, tension, and relapse.”.
unmappedHistorical.body: For all addicts we struggle with those old feelings, and emotions that we lived with for so long during our addictions. We for so long have lived life full of negativity, and destruction. Our inability to cope with life forced us into a dark existence of hopelessness. After living this kind of life, it is not as easy as just getting clean. How many times did we try and pick up the pieces on our own, get our life in order, only to somehow end up in the same place we came from. We only have to look at our track record to believe it. We will see that over and over we failed because of our inability to deal with the disease. We must learn to deal with the feelings that have plagued us and dictated our lives for years, and only fueled our obsessive and compulsive use of drugs. Once we stay here a while, we come to realize that although we cannot rid ourselves of all the affects that the addiction has done to us, but we can however learn to overcome these feelings and fears through constant work on ourselves and working on our defects of character, through the Steps. We learn a new experience of living life free from these effects of addiction. The freedom comes from learning that we don’t have to continue to allow the fear and our defects dictate our life today.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we can look to the program of N.A. and God to help us deal with the frustrations we may feel dealing with life on life’s terms.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Every clean member of N.A. Could have been rejected by some kind of membership requirement or another. Many of us would not be alive today if we hadn’t found a program which accepted us when we wanted help”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Many newcomers of confused at first, as to what our program has to offer them. We encourage addicts to always stay and accept them into our program, as to not give them any excuses to run out the door. We are here for the addict who wants help with their drug problem and is looking for a new way of life. Any addict who has a desire to stop using can become a member of N.A. We don’t discriminate here, just as the disease doesn’t discriminate against age, race, sex, or religion. Most addicts have experienced a life full of rejection and have felt that they just didn’t fit in to society as a whole. This is part of the disease that isolates us based on all the things we can use to feel different. When we come to the program of N.A., it takes us a while to accept that we are not different, but all share a common disease, and a common cause, the recovery from addiction. When we finally give ourselves a break, and stop using, we can begin to see that we had a disease, and that recovery is then possible for us. When the member decides that they have a desire to stop using, and stay clean, we can also then make the decision to become a member of N.A. This decision rests with the individual, and it is not automatic. We learn to work together for the common cause of staying clean together.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we can make the decision to be a member of N.A., by staying clean and working towards our recovery from addiction.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Our way of living speaks for itself better than our words ever could. People see us on the street and remember us as furtive, frightened loners. They notice the grayness and fear leaving our faces. They see us gradually come alive”.
unmappedHistorical.body: When we first get clean, we will find that our family and friends, and those around us may be skeptical at first of our new-found recovery. After many years of “messing up” our lives, and destroying our relationships, this is normal. We must remember that we are here for ourselves first and cannot get clean for anyone else but ourselves. If we continue to focus our energy, and actions on our own lives, and recovering from the disease of addiction, we eventually adopt a new attitude on life and are better able to have meaningful relationships with others. Our new attitudes, and actions speak for themselves over time. We are here for the purpose of recovery, and to help the newcomer. The principles we learn here not only helps to equip us better to carry the message to the still suffering addict, but it also helps us to repair our broken lives. We are a living example of the program of N.A. The literature tells us that our actions speak louder than our words when it comes to helping a newcomer. We mustn’t forget how we all have a unique ability to pick out all the negative and look for the excuses to leave. Preaching doesn’t work on the newcomer. We keep to sharing our experience, strength, and hope, and apply these principles in all our affairs, to be an attractive to new members of the program, and to our family and loved ones. We have come a long way from that “frightened loner” that we were when we first got here. Today as our spirits awaken we find a new place in the world, and society.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we are grateful for the new life that the N.A. Program has given us, and make ourselves available for the newcomer to give away what was freely given to us

unmappedHistorical.quote: ” We no longer have to be isolated, and in time can feel free to go anywhere, and do almost anything except use”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Listening to others at our meetings will show us that we are no longer alone. The importance of truly listening, to hear what someone is sharing is important for us to achieve that empathy that we have for each other, and to become a part of the na Fellowship. It also helps to hear the pain of an addict that has just made it here. A brand newcomer may not know much about recovery from addiction, but they do have a message of pain and misery that they come from, and this will help to remind us of where we were when we got here. This is an important piece of our own recovery, because it simply reminds us that we never want to go back to that life of active addiction. Now that we are clean, and feel accepted in the N.A. fellowship, we must be vigilante to stay away from play places, play things, play toys and playmates, we often see addicts fall into the trap of overconfidence. When we feel we have the ability to ignore the warnings of others and the literature, we can find ourselves flirting with disaster. The endless circle of recovery begins with the newcomer and playing our role in the helping of others is how it continues. Relapse is not a requirement here, and if we stay attentive to our own recovery, and consistently allow others into our lives we can avoid many of the pitfalls that will help assure that we never have to relapse ourselves.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will not become overconfident with ourselves and keep our egos in check by talking honestly with other recovering addicts and asking for help and guidance.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Incarceration and institutionalization sometimes led us to the realization that the drugs were letting us down”.
unmappedHistorical.body: It’s amazing how many times an addict must be put in a rehab, or a jail before we can figure out that we may have a drug problem. Often, we will blame society, family, the police, or the “system” for our problems, and it takes a miracle before we can see that we are the problem. Unfortunately, many addicts don’t make it here. They’re stubbornness, and unwillingness to face the truth leads them to death at the hands of this disease. Being in jail or a rehab for an active addict will give many of us, the must needed break from our day to day routine of finding ways and means to get more, and sometimes we will have moments of clarity in these situations to see that maybe we should look for another way. We must first overcome the hurdles of the doctors associated with these institutions. Almost immediately, they want to put us on medication, through misdiagnosing us, and not understanding the true nature of addiction. The drug replacement that happens in these places, leads many addicts down a different path of addiction, that just adds to the problem, and keeps us from facing and dealing with ourselves. If we are lucky enough to make it to our first N.A. meeting after being released from jail, or rehab, and we are still clean from all mind and mood changing chemicals, then we are in the best position to succeed, and get what this program has to offer us. It only takes a little bit of time clean, and some good things to start happening for us to want more of this way of life, and to look back at our old way as not an option anymore. We now have a choice to live.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will be grateful for the choice to live that this program that has given to us through a Greater Power than ourselves

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Many of us felt that our lives, due to petty frustrations, minor setbacks and losses, were not getting any better”.
unmappedHistorical.body: We as addicts are easily discouraged when things seem to not be going our way. We tend to always want the answers, and results that we are looking for without the wait, or without putting in the footwork. As we stay clean and start to learn how to deal with life clean, and drug free, we quickly realize that this is not how things work. Anything worth working for, is worth the wait. After years of using drugs, to achieve that instant gratification that the drugs gave us, this is a totally new idea for most of us. We are given another chance through the N.A. Program, which means through the Steps, we are given the ability to put the necessary work in and allow God to do the rest. We are rewarded each day with another day clean, and another chance to live. Unfortunately, many of us get impatient with life. We see many addicts get bitter and angry still when things don’t go their way. This is a result of a lack of surrender, and the inability to let go of the reigns. We do not control the outcome in life, and we don’t control others. The sooner we can admit this and surrender our control, the sooner we are able to obtain the relief that so many of us experience. We find ourselves looking for solutions for our problems today, and when we feel frustrated, and angry, we usually need to take an inventory, and take a look at ourselves, rather than blaming others. Overall, we can feel good about being clean, and as our literature tells us, we are generally doing better than we feel. Through N.A., we learn acceptance, and patience, and are able to live through any setback life may throw at us without using.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will work through our daily problems, and setbacks through the tools the N.A. Program offers us, and with the help of others.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “When we could not stand our old ways no longer, we began to change. All that was required is that we try”.
unmappedHistorical.body: How many years of pain and suffering addicts go through before they will start to look for another way. Many of us find ourselves spending more time looking for a way to successfully use, without all the problems that using has brought us in the past.Unfortunately, this doesn’t work. After making every change that we could try, which includes changing geographical locations, friends, spouses, drugs, and so on, we realize that the same problem exists. When we realize that we are the problem, we can begin to work on the solution. If we are lucky enough to make it to N.A., all we need to do is look around at all the other addicts there who are clean to realize that there is a solution to our dilemma. If we have had enough pain and suffering, and find ourselves in an N.A. meeting, then we are in the best position to succeed. Even after we stay clean for a while, we are still left with all the issues that we have carried around with us for years, but stuffed them deep down inside through constant denial, and drug use. Once the onion peels of denial begin to be pulled away, we realize how much work there is to do. The pain and confusion that our “old ways” of living cause us, gives us the motivation to do the necessary work on ourselves. Through working with others, and a sponsor in N.A., we are able to work through these problems together. If we honestly try, and are consistent in our seeking of recovery, we will notice a change for the better in our actions, and reactions to life. Recovery puts us in a position in life to continually get better and improve ourselves. Today we welcome any change that helps us to keep moving forward in life, and to keep moving away from our past ways.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we want to keep moving forward in our recovery, and will do this through daily work on ourselves, and keeping our recovery first in our lives

unmappedHistorical.label: Historical FSC R&I - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “Recovery is a beautiful chance that many addicts thought had passed them by until they found the Fellowship of N.A. It’s the chance to live again”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Once we have been in our active addictions for many years, it becomes evident to us that we are farther and farther away from our lives before we started using, and also farther away from any chance at a “normal” life. We may have needed help and guidance before we started using on how to be productive, and successful in life, but we become almost beyond any help by the time we reach the end of our using. This is where the N.A. Program comes in to rescue us from our insanity. We not only have a way out through N.A., but it seems to be the only answer that works for us. There is no other remedy or doctor’s prescription, or psychiatrist’s analysis that has any proven, long term success. Jails and institutions have failed us for many years, and continue to label us as emotionally unbalanced, and as a result prescribe more drugs. None of these methods gives us as addicts a chance to live a life drug free, and they most certainly don’t offer any remedy to fix the problems that have plagued us since childhood. Together, in N.A. we can continue to partake in this new life, and we can continue to offer this program to the still suffering addict. If we are part of the N.A. fellowship today, we will always have the support we need to continue on a life free from drugs, and to pursue continued growth and happiness.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will be grateful for this new gift of life that the N.A. fellowship has given us and continue to improve ourselves through the N.A. Program.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “We find freedom from drugs and the obsession to use them: and in time a bit of freedom from that part of ourselves that has been destroyed”.
unmappedHistorical.body: One of the first freedoms we experience as recovering addicts is the freedom from the obsession to use. The length of time may vary from addict to addict, but there is one definite promise that is always fulfilled if we stay here and do the work. That is the relief from that overbearing obsession, and compulsion that had controlled our lives for as long as we can remember. This also gives us the first glimpse at the power of the N.A. Program, and the God that we come to know here. We can believe this at first because we had tried for so many years unsuccessfully to run away from that obsession in one way or another, only to find that we were powerless to stop it on our own. If we build on this belief, and continue through the 12 Steps, and continue on the path of recovery, we slowly are able to let those parts of ourselves go that have helped to destroy us. We find that the real problem has always been us, and unless we face ourselves, and the world around us we will never achieve that happy, joyous promise that the program also always delivers to those who continue in this path and continue to work the program to the best of their ability. We continually seek improvements today so that we are not limited to our old ways, and as time goes on we find that we can continually credit new awakenings and growth to the N.A. Program.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we can reflect on all the many blessings this program has given us, and we choose to build ourselves up through N.A. instead of destroying ourselves.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “We help newcomers, whether they are detoxing or just beginning to learn the principles of N.A. ”.
unmappedHistorical.body: When a newcomer shows up at our meeting, we must keep in mind that this may be the last time this person needs to use. We have a responsibility to talk with that person and listen to their experience so that we can then share our experience with them, making sure to get their phone number, and get them to meetings. Recovery is a gift of God’s grace that was freely given to us, and we learn to share that gift freely with others. Newcomers are always looking for excuses to run back to the drugs. This is the nature of the disease of addiction, and we take great care as to not provide them with any excuse. We must be careful not to put too many expectations on someone new to our program as well, but at the same time we work with them to help eliminate the hurdles that they will continually put in their own path to recovery. Learning to balance helping others without becoming overbearing is an art that we learn here in N.A. It takes an understanding that we acquire over time, by working with others, and seeing others recover. This is also very important for a newcomer. If we reach out to them and offer our experience to help them, get them to meetings, and call them regularly, we can become part of that person’s solution to staying here long enough for the miracle to happen. We keep living just for today so that we can relieve the burden of our past and alleviate the fear of the future and helping another suffering addict can be a great way to get out of our own way.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will reach out to a newcomer, and share with them our experience, strength, and hope so we can offer them a better way of life, through N.A. and the 12 Steps of recovery

unmappedHistorical.quote: “To live is to use the necessities to attain life. To use is to die”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Taking our recovery too lightly can lead to all sorts of stumbling blocks for addicts. When we fail to fully surrender and accept the N.A. Program and our powerlessness to this disease, we have seen time and time again addicts fall back to the horrors of addiction. Keeping in the “solution” of living life today means that we must first accept our powerlessness fully, and also accept and participate in the new way of life outlined in the N.A. Program. Relapse is not must for us, and to safeguard against it, we use the tools of the program and the Fellowship of the others. The short lived “high” that we obtained while using is no longer what we as recovering addicts are after. Today, we are looking to incorporate basic principles set down in the Steps and learn to apply them in our daily lives. This gives our lives more meaning and fulfillment then any short lived high ever could. We become a part of the greater fellowship of addicts all seeking one common goal. We must learn to shatter our illusions of reality or we risk isolation, and the loneliness that is almost always followed by the drugs. We no longer have to “run” the show today, we learn to rely on the program, and a loving God to guide us through life today. Acceptance becomes a way of life, and a Stepping stone to all spiritual growth.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we are keeping our recovery ahead of the pitfalls that life may bring, and we choose to rely on the program to lead us through the good times and difficult times

unmappedHistorical.quote: ” Modern drug technology and media attention have made a social anti-hero of the addict. Since many of us were street addicts, we dealt in illicit drugs and lived criminally”.
unmappedHistorical.body: The newcomers are the most important persons at our meetings. This is a reminder of where we were when we walked through the door, and also, this gives us the opportunity to put our gratitude into action by giving away what was freely given to us, the gift of recovery. It is important for us to remember that society has deemed the addict as derelict, and not part of. We are criminalized, jailed, and put in institutions only to find the doctors there trying to medicate our disease away. As many of us have found out, this doesn’t work. Being totally abstinent from all drugs is a blessing today that we must be grateful for. Remembering all the thousands of addicts that are caught in the system, before they reach N.A. and then medicated with new drug, that will only make the disease grow. There are many blessings of recovery that we can be grateful for and being clean is only the beginning. Keeping in mind not to chase newcomers back out into the society that offers no real help for them is a must. How many addicts are serving life sentences in jail due to their addictions. This is part of the miracle of the N.A. Program, that any addict no matter what society has said about them, or labeled us as, can stay clean, and become productive members of the human race again.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today, we give away what was freely given to us. We have been given a reprieve from the horrors of addiction and have the ability to lend the hand of N.A. to the still suffering addict who is willing to accept it.

unmappedHistorical.quote: ” Being honest is not a natural thing for us to do. We don’t expect to practice total honesty in all things overnight. It is a gradual process in our daily living”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Many addicts would rather swim the length of the atlantic ocean rather then tell the truth. The fact that we as addicts can believe wholeheartedly that we are really not the cause of our problems is an example of how cunning and baffling this disease is, and how dishonest we have been with ourselves through our addiction. We have convinced ourselves, through our own rationalizations for so long, that when we get here, and finally get clean, we still don’t really believe that we are the cause. We still want to point outward, and look to lay blame on others, family, God, society, and just the world in general. Part of the recovery process is learning to get honest with ourselves and others, and to take responsibility for our own actions, but this takes time. We must first be able to identify ourselves as having a real disease, that has hijacked us spiritually, and mentally. To be able to identify and accept is all part of our First Step process. Getting to know ourselves, and practicing honesty through regular meeting attendance, and working on getting honest with others is really the practice we need in order to start identifying who we are, and what our real problems are. This is half the battle, and once we can, we can then begin to fix some of the things that are wrong and begin to see honesty as the beginning of all recovery. It must all start with ourselves.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we can identify our problem, and through acceptance, and a reliance on a loving God, we can be honest about our feelings, thoughts, and actions.This will help put us on the road to healing, and recovery

unmappedHistorical.quote: "Because of our physical sensitivity to drugs we are completely in the grip of a destructive power stronger than ourselves”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Once we realize that we have been in the grips of a destructive power that we cannot defeat we are on our way to recovery. We can no longer kid ourselves into thinking that we can do this on our own. Getting to listen to the stories of other recovering addicts helps us with acceptance of this. When we hear the same story over and over told by many different addicts from all walks of life, we will find a common theme in their stories. That they were unable to defeat this disease of addiction, until they sought help in the program of N.A. This is also a pre cursor to our First Step as well. Unless we fully accept this fact, we are doomed to fail. When we are out of the grip of the disease, and the compulsion and obsession have been lifted, is when we can look back and see just how doomed we were. Recovery is a change of our reactions, thoughts, and attitudes, and when we begin to understand and accept who we really are. Our literature tells us that no addict has ever failed to recover who has surrendered completely to our program. The proven lives of countless addicts who have remained clean and recovering from the disease of addiction is a powerful tool for newcomers. We are highly sensitive to all mood changing and mind-altering chemicals and must take extra care to inform doctors of our condition, as our bodies don’t know the difference between street drugs and prescribed drugs. We are not cured here, in N.A. we get a daily reprieve from the horrors of our past lives.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will accept who we are, and be grateful that we have been given another day free from the grips of addiction

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Obsession is the fixed idea that takes us back to a particular drug, trying to regain the ease and comfort we once knew”.
unmappedHistorical.body: We will hear addicts sharing about keeping it green in our meetings, and this is with good cause. If we forget where we have come from, we are doomed to repeat past mistakes. What keeps us alive and free today is a constant awareness of our disease and the gift of recovery that we have been given. We sometimes we can forget that in spite of our own negative thinking, and loss of gratitude in our daily lives, that we are usually doing better than we are feeling. When we remain abstinent for another day from drugs, we are that miracle that the literature reminds us of. When we are involved with others’ lives today who are also recovering from this disease, we will find it easier to remember who we are., we must remain grounded in the program, and also, we must not forget that we have plenty to be grateful for if we aren’t using. Remembering where we came from, or “keeping it green”, is a good way to be happy with the simple things in life today. The obsession to use drugs has been lifted today, and that is the greatest proof of a Greater Power working to do for us what we could not do for ourselves. Today with the tools of the program, we can look at life’s challenges as a way to improve ourselves, and our relationships. When we complicate things, we tend to forget that keeping it simple starts with staying clean and being grateful for another day.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will take advantage of the benefits of living clean, by being grateful for our recovery, and recognizing that our recovery was a gift granted to us from God.

unmappedHistorical.quote: ” Although our heads told us we would never make it, the people in the Fellowship gave us hope by insisting we could”:
unmappedHistorical.body: One of the things we will hear when we get here is to not think too much. When we start spending time alone in our heads we are giving the disease a forum to attack us. An addict alone is in bad company. Addicts need to be around other addicts in order to feel part of but also to help us to fend off the “stinking thinking”. Hearing our literature for the first time or attending one of our N.A. meetings for the first time can be an eye-opening experience. All our lives we probably thought that we were the only ones that felt the way we do, we felt that. We were alone. Once we get to N.A., we realize that we are not alone, but we share a common disease, that isolates us all individually, and keeps us that way as long as we keep using. The lie that we are different is shattered over time, when we listen to others share at our meetings, and we can for the first time begin to feel like we are a part of the human race again. It is important to keep focused on our similarities, not our differences so that we can experience this change. The proof we get from seeing other addicts that have stayed clean and recovering for lengths of time is sometimes all we need to help us through another day. The hope that this gives us is what we hold onto. This is all part of the recovery from addiction process, and somehow God sees fit to bring us together in order to help each other. A group of people that alone are powerless and isolated, yet together are able to do together what individually we could not. Keeping this in mind as we attend our meetings, and fellowship with others in N.A. will give us a perspective on the power of this program.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will reach out to others in the program to put our minds on the right track today, and to help others who may need help

unmappedHistorical.quote: ” For the first time in many months, we were able to relax when we heard that we couldn’t control our addictions”.
unmappedHistorical.body: The amount of energy addicts spends on focusing on all of the negative things in life, as well as how to control everything can be exhausting. When we first get clean we probably have a mountain to climb ahead of us in order to clear up the wreckage that addiction has done to our lives. This is a clear result of our inability to control the disease of addiction, as well as a host of others. Our attempts at controlling the addiction led us down many dark paths of destruction and dismay, and had we been successful, we would not be looking at this mountain of destruction that we left in our path. Many of us have legal issues to deal with, and fines to pay, and many shattered relationships that may or may not be mended. We begin this process by first taking care of the source of this destruction, ourselves. It is a comfort to know that we can let go of the reigns and allow ourselves the ability to surrender today. We must begin by getting incorporated into the N.A. Program by regularly attending meetings and working with other addicts who have already been through this process. If we get clean, and then try and run around “fixing” everything, we will be in for another brick wall to run into. We keep the focus on a day at a time, and get help from others, so that we don’t try and take the wheel again. We will notice that the things that seemed so impossible before, now seem very possible, with the help of others. We are all in this together, and together we have the power to surrender.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will take comfort in the program of N.A., knowing that we don’t have to do this alone, we can “let go and let God” today.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “However, open mindedness without willingness, will get us nowhere”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Our literature tells us that honesty, open mindedness, and willingness are spiritual principles that get us out of the troubles that dishonesty, closed mindedness and unwillingness got us into. Continuing to live our lives with a closed mind is a sure way to not recover from this disease and will almost guarantee us that we will not make it here. In order to live everyday free from the addiction, we continually work on these principles. We never know when life will throw us a curve ball and must keep ourselves spiritually fit in order to meet the challenges that we can face in a day, and not revert back to our old ways, or worse yet, run back to a drug. It takes quite a bit of practice in order to learn how to face ourselves today, and our true natures. We do this by being honest with ourselves and others about what we are really feeling. This can be done at our meetings, or one on one with other recovering addicts. We follow the path that has been traveled down before us by others in the program. Our past will also come back to haunt us occasionally and must remain honest in order to face our past, and our present in a constructive way. Running from ourselves doesn’t help us today and can lead to relapse. We no longer have the drugs to run to in order to hide from our feelings, and our guilt, so we learn to face ourselves as honestly as we can. We can incorporate the help of the program, and other recovering addicts in order to help us sort through what we’re going through. We also utilize the tools of reading, writing, and praying to keep us in touch with ourselves, and to lead us down a journey to find ourselves each day. Together we learn how to live a new life that we can only achieve if we keep our minds open to new ideas and are willing to do what it takes in order to recover.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we can honestly face ourselves, so we can accept ourselves for where we are. We can work on our shortcomings, and faults by first being honest about who we are.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Before coming to n. A. Most of us tried to clean up or stay clean on our own. Many of us sought treatment or professional help”
unmappedHistorical.body: All of the efforts we put into trying to “clean up “our lives before we got to N.A. were unsuccessful. They were either short lived, or nonexistent. Treatment centers, and rehabs were of no real help to us, and would usually lead us down a deeper hole then when we started. The program of N.A. can do for us addicts what we could not do for ourselves. We know deep down, because of all our past failed attempts to clean up, that without the Fellowship of N.A. we would be in deep trouble. We cannot do it alone. We come together as a group of addicts seeking recovery, and focus on our common themes, that in spite of our different backgrounds, we all have the same underlying problem of addiction. We no longer convince ourselves that we can make it on our own today, and instead each learn to rely on each other and a Higher Power for help and guidance. The surrender to the fact that we could no longer control our using, or manage our lives has led us to N.A. This is another common theme of our addiction. What has separated us from everyone while using has also brought us together in N.A. We have all earned our seat here in Narcotics Anonymous, and we share our experiences and learn from each other. We know today that all the answers we need to live a life free from addiction are found here in N.A. We no longer need to look to doctors, and professionals for answers that they do not have for us.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will focus on our common desire to stay clean and recover from the disease of addiction. We find a new source of strength in the Fellowship and learn to rely on it.

unmappedHistorical.quote: "We quit fighting. We accept our addiction and life the way it is. We became willing to do whatever was necessary to stay clean, even those things we didn't like doing."
unmappedHistorical.body: In our addiction we became self-centered and self-seeking. Always doing what we wanted to get then next high, fix or drink. We put our own needs ahead of all those we care about. We fought our addiction for so long surrender seemed like an impossible dream. Our lives had become unmanageable and we didn't know how to live. In our recovery we learn that we can't control people, places, things and situations so we end up surrendering ourselves. First to the group then to whatever Higher Power we believe in. We learn some simple tools to help us in our daily journey. We go to meetings when our disease tells us to isolate. Meetings make our life tranquil. After we leave a meeting we feel better than when we came. One addict shared when it is there turn to share, right before they say a prayer-"dear God allow me to share to help us and help me feel better! “we call our sponsor or other fellow addicts when we get stuck in our head. We have learned that taking suggestions from our fellow addicts has proven to have extreme value. Becoming willing to follow through with suggestions from others help us keep the serenity that we had desired for years. We learn to write also to help get to know ourselves better and help us grow. Many times, we may not feel like doing these things but we learn feelings are just that........feelings. We let go surrender and make the choice to recover instead of giving in to our disease.
unmappedHistorical.moment: we accept that it is only in this complete surrender that we are able to grow in our recovery.

unmappedHistorical.quote: ” We will eventually hear someone who flat our makes us feel lucky by comparison. We will grow to know gratitude, to see where we came from and how far we have progressed”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Being an addict in recovery by no means makes us perfect human beings. Our self- centered thinking is a natural behavior for an addict, and recovery is only a daily reprieve from this way of life. Thinking of ourselves above, or better than others was a trademark behavior of our addiction, but today this way of thinking has no place in our lives. This is also true of our self-willed behaviors as well. We still want what we want, when we want it, and to go against this natural instinct is just as much of a miracle as it is for us not to use drugs. Comparing ourselves to others while we were using, and also during our recovery is another symptom of the disease of addiction. We always want to feel better than others, so comparing what others are doing to ourselves can be a dangerous behavior. We are to only worry about our own recovery, as we cannot recover for anyone else. No one of us makes consistently good decisions for ourselves in this program, we need each other to help us with this, and this action is based on our Third Step. Learning to let go of the controls and ask for direction can steer us away from making bad decisions in our lives that can bring us pain, and maybe even relapse. When we grab the controls for too long, eventually our own selfish motives come into play, and we will ultimately start to act on these motives. The self-gratifying behaviors will sicken us, and eventually can lead to our picking up. Today, as part of our program we practice turning over the controls to a loving God, and to others, and together we our given the strength to find the peace that comes with letting go.
unmappedHistorical.moment: we can be grateful today for all the gifts the N.A. Program has given us, and keep a positive outlook on a life clean, and free from addiction.

unmappedHistorical.quote: ” We never considered ourselves addicts, although some of us have used, misused and abused drugs for half of our lives or more”.
unmappedHistorical.body: Addiction has no prejudices. It will affect anyone, from any race, color, creed, or class of human. We find many different people when we get to N.A., from all walks of life. From doctors, to lawyers, to street junkies, we all have one common problem, addiction. Although, we may think that if we had a good job, like being a doctor or lawyer we would be immune to the effects of this disease. The fact that there are just as many addicted professionals in jails, institutions, and the graveyard as the less affluent addicts proves that this disease is just as devastating to anyone’s life, no matter where we fit in on the social ladder. It has one goal, to bring us down to the bottom, whether that is through institutionalizing us for the rest of our lives, or simply killing us. Although, some of us end up with more “things”, and material goods when we get here, it is being mentally and spiritually bankrupt that ultimately puts us in the same state of despair. We cannot escape the effects of addiction simply because we have more stuff. The flip side of this is also true. No matter who we are when we get here, the program of N.A. will help us to bring ourselves out of the pits of despair that the addiction leaves us in. This program works for anyone regardless of age, race, sex, color, or creed, and saves us from the guaranteed ends of addiction, jails, institutions, or death.
unmappedHistorical.moment: today we will remember that if we have stayed clean today, from all mind or mood changing chemicals, that the miracle of the N.A. Program is working in our lives, and we can be grateful that we are no longer under the grips of addiction.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “In N.A. we have feelings we never dreamed of having. We are able to entertain ourselves today. We do things beyond our wildest imagining.”
unmappedHistorical.body: As addicts, we used drugs to get out of ourselves, we didn’t feel comfortable in our own skins, in the Process we stood away from others as well. At the end of our bottoms, the isolation and desperation seemed too much for any human being to handle. For most of us, this is what it took to want to seek a Solution. We still weren’t sure that N.A. was for us, we just wanted to stop hurting. Arriving at Narcotics Anonymous we were given suggestions. As we learned to follow these subtle commands, our Perspectives started to change. We found out that we didn’t have to use anymore, and that was a great revelation. We joined others in their Journeys, and they shared their Recovery with us. They showed us the way that was shown to them, when they first came around. One addict helping another proved to be what was missing in our Lives all along. As others helped us, it helped them as well. As we helped others, our own Recovery was enforced. As we got introduced to the God Of Our Understanding, and took the Steps with a Sponsor, we also started to feel comfortable in our own skins. We experienced Compassion and Empathy toward others. We learned by working with others, we got out of ourselves. The more we gave of ourselves, the more of ourselves we received. Working the Steps and Practicing Spiritual Principles in our Lives, we began to Change. We started to become the person we always wanted to be. We grew to Love Freedom, and our Lives began to be something we wanted to experience. We experienced Love of self and others. Some of our dreams became possibilities, now that we weren’t trapped in the disease of addiction.
unmappedHistorical.moment: We can build Healthy Relationships, with God, Ourselves, Others and with the World at Large. Living Happy, Joyous and Free becomes a Reality.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “It would seem that the path to spiritual recovery involves spiritual principles. Spiritual indifference will surely lead to relapse.”
unmappedHistorical.body: Not living spiritual principles makes us miserable people. Constantly blaming the world for our own pain. We cut ourselves off from God and the gifts of recovery. We may be physically clean but spiritually dirty. We are now in the problem and not the solution. In order to reach our spiritual aim, the practice of willingness will play a key part in letting go of our defects of character. Our solution is a spiritual one and if we drift off and relapse we might not make it back.
unmappedHistorical.moment: Utilizing these spiritual principles we are ready to have sanity restored to us and we are growing in our recovery.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “After establishing our new desire to live clean in the Fellowship and acquainting ourselves with the tools which have helped other suffering addicts to recover, we can then proceed with the business of living.”
unmappedHistorical.body:
We made the choice to stay abstinent just for today, because using drugs was too painful and was killing us. Once the obsession with using had been lifted, we decide if we want to live this way of life.

It took some of us a while to find out what this program is about. We were finally beaten and could admit that our way of doing things wasn’t going to work and keep us clean, then we started to open up for suggestions. We get to know and trust in the actions of addicts that have gone before us and who have learnt to live clean. We learnt about surrender by the examples of others and that whatever we were thinking and feeling, our first priority was to surrender to the tools of our program.

By getting acquainted with the tools of recovery we found our lives became easier and began to become more responsible in the society we live in. These tools have proved to work for many others, all we need is the desire to use these them. It does not mean we will master them right away, however, where there is a will there is a way.

We need the steps in order to change, to move away from our past and begin to live and become the people God would have us be.

In the moment we continue to live this way of life, putting our recovery first and share it with those that want it.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “One of our biggest stumbling blocks seems to be in unrealized expectations of ourselves and others. Relationships are a terribly painful area.”
unmappedHistorical.body:
Our unrealistic expectations in romantic relationships often caused pain, fear, and anger. This self-obsession caused us to withdraw into isolation and loneliness. We brought the damage from the last relationship into the next relationship with even more unrealistic expectations. We as addicts are reminded that alone we are in bad company. Loneliness is not the way of a new life. We feel like running but we don’t. We call our sponsor and they tell us to keep coming, accept our feelings, and share our pain. They guide us to a solution through the Steps and Traditions. They love us unconditionally. We pray and lay our pain in the hands of our Higher Power, and ask for help and guidance. Now we are in the solution.

In this moment, we will allow others to help us to love ourselves so we can love others in a healthy relationship.

unmappedHistorical.quote: Some of us found getting clean a battle. The program is simple. No one ever said it was easy....
unmappedHistorical.body:
Getting clean was a daily fight for us with lots of ups and downs. Its hard dealing with mental and physical issues as well as emotional. When we begin to see that will power alone wasn’t going to pull us through anymore. We tried countless other remedies, councillors, psychiatrists, hospitals, lovers, new towns, new jobs. Everything we tried failed. We quit for a day, a week, or a month perhaps, but sooner or later we took that first pill, fix, drink, or toke and we were gone again worse than ever.

Untill we surrender there is something about addicts... we like to complicate a simple program. In times of trial, we are faced with a dubious ultimatum we must either change or go back to using. Before we surrender we have all kinds of excuses and are great at rationalizing and justifying why we can’t do the things necissary for our recovery. When we could stand our old ways no longer we began to change. Only under the relentless attack of pain and suffering did we begin to make a way. When the pain of staying the same outweighs the pain of doing something different, change is inevitable

When we finally opened our eyes to see the simplicity of the program we were expecting an easy process. We were wrong. Nothing good comes easy, and rarely are easy things good. Using was easy and stopping was hard. We used daily, if we want to recover it is going to take a daily program. With the help of addicts, there might be a chance... thanks be to God there is a process we must follow. It takes time and acceptance to figure it all out but life always does. In the middle of a true crisis, it is always a relief to know that God will never tempt us beyond what we can bear. He will always make a way out. We saw the gifts of recovery and kept fighting. Now we see why the fight is worth the pain
unmappedHistorical.moment: After we surrender many of us ask ourselves “why didnt we surrender sooner” we must get out of our self... in order to understand the beauty of the simplicity of NA.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “We usually react angrily as recovering addicts if anyone tells us what to do”
unmappedHistorical.body: Many of us came in as angry, frightened individuals. We were hot headed and defensive, quick to defend our views and actions. This was a character defect that kept us from surrender. We had very little trust in the addicts in the room. Advice or direction from anyone, especially those close to us, such as a sponsor, was not always taken the best. We had been controlled our whole lives, by our own feelings or others, causing us to become resentful at even the mere hint of someone trying to control us. Throughout our recovery we had been given many suggestions on what we need to do to stay clean. Often we thought that they were wrong, that they didn’t know what they were talking about. We are close minded and self-centered. We do not realize that we know little about the program and that someone telling us what to do actually cares for our wellbring. Slowly, as we grow up in recovery, we become more trusting, understanding, and emotionally stable. Over time we learn to take suggestions and see how, without those suggestions, we can’t recover. We begin to trust that others care for us and want to help. We learned that asking for help & listening to suggestions is not as hard as we once thought. There is no longer a reason to become angry over it.
unmappedHistorical.moment: Being clean is abnormal to us, and we must learn how to live a different way. Being able to let go of our need to control when told what to do is a blessing from our higher power.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “When we finally became desperate enough to seek help we once again sought out the company of our fellow addicts”
unmappedHistorical.body:
Desperation is an all too familiar feeling to us. We were hopeless our lives had fallen apart we thought we had nowhere to turn that noone could understand what was happening and why we used. Some of us as relapseing addicts struggled with commitment issues and reservations. The line once again takes on a whole new meaning. We fought it, cried about it, and feared it non stop.. we were in a dark cycle. Using felt good for a little bit then we felt the emptyness the guilt, fear, and hopelessness we became addicted to a cycle that did us no good but was hard to break away. we hit rock bottom and needed something different in our lives to lift us up.

When we came thru the doors of NA it seemed like everyone knew our feelings about using and our desperation to get better. It started out awkward and uncomfortable trying to trust another person enough to ask for help or support. We were so used to building a wall to protect ourselfs. Reaching out to another addict felt hard and foriegn. We were leaving behind isolation and the fear of being alone and judged. When we finally did reach out we suddenly felt part of something bigger than ourselfs. We realized our way wasnt working and we needed others to show us how to live.

We found a new and loving group that doesnt judge and accepts us for who we are. We sought the help of fellow addicts in NA they were the ones that can understand us. Noone else would understand what we are going through like another addict. When things get complicated in our lives we learned to call our sponsor or someone in NA who can give us insight on how to get through the hard times. We feel the ESH abd want it for ourselfs. We started to make changes and strive for recovery. We found help and discovered our ability to share our personal experience can help other addicts.

When we came into the rooms we were greeted with a hug and a genuine desire to get to know us and people that want to be there for us.... its scary and uncomfortable at first but slowly we find love trust and loyalty. In battling the issues previously stated..... it really boils down to the company we keep. Do we wish to further a fresh mentality, the desire to recover and change, by our fellowship with other addicts? Or do we wish to stay the same, by continueing the same path, with the same people, in the same pain? The choice is ours....
unmappedHistorical.moment: We realize when we seek help it brings back a part of us we had lost... when we are clean we are able to live free at last.

unmappedHistorical.quote: "There is one truth which helps guide us. True spiritual principles are never in conflict: they always compliment each other."
unmappedHistorical.body:
We came into NA not being able to be honest with our selves or others. We lied to ourselves for so long we believed our selves. After awhile we learned we can't recover if we keep living dirty. Without truth our program is phony and without meaning and purpose. Where there is truth there are no lies.

Many of us fought surrender and have to come to a point where there are no more excuses . We learn to do things the way our higher power wants us to. Treating people the way we would like to be treated. We begin to understand we can't feed our ego and be humble at the same time. We let our higher power guide us through life on God's terms not ours.
unmappedHistorical.moment: we know where there is light there cannot be darkness. When we are honest we feel God's spirit is with us. When God is with us, we cannot fail. Life becomes simple as we begin to understand true spiritually principles will never contradict one other.

unmappedHistorical.quote: "Just as we went to any length to get drugs, so must we go to any lengths to learn to get clean. "
unmappedHistorical.body: Our drug searching took over our days. It was a constant obsession. We spent all of our energy feeling stressed over how we would find our next fix. We gave all we had to using dope, so why would we think we can sell ourselves short by giving only part of ourselves to recovery? We went through many painstaking ways, we dealt with difficult relationships and went through trials and tribulations. But we did not give up. Our searching drew us away from many things in in life that we cared about. In desperation some of us felt there was nothing left but suicide. We hated the disease and where it took us, we committed crimes just to exist and that was our reality. We found it easier to change our perception of reality than the reality we perceived. We have to put getting clean ahead of everything else in our lives. If we put half the effort into staying clean as we did into finding means and ways to use, all will be well. We need our recovery to be bulletproof. We must put all our energy into working the steps, using meetings and people, and the program to help guide us. We need to seek out people clean and in recovery. We learned to spend energy on positive things in life; work, school, kids, family, hobbies and nature. We do whatever it takes to stay clean. We must in order to grow and stay in recovery. Getting clean is a full-contact process where we must face our fears, insecurities, guilt, and shame if we truly want to recover.
unmappedHistorical.moment: recovery is easy compared to the work we put into finding drugs.

unmappedHistorical.quote: "We came to hate ourselves for wasting the talents with which we had been endowed and for the trouble we were causing our families and others."
unmappedHistorical.body:
For a person living with an addict, for their families and their kids they're always fearing an outburst and never trusting what the addict says. We only could think about what we needed and not how it affected the people around us. We manipulated and stole from those closest to us. We became a burden on our families, often creating financial difficulties and emotional pain. Our addiction led us to become people we never wished to be. However, none of us had realized what we were becoming. We became people who were constantly letting down loved ones and ourselves. We would often wake up hating ourselves each morning and night. Most of us were just sick of being sick and tired and wanted a new way to live without having to use drugs as a way to do so. We had never thought of ourselves as angry people, but when it came to anything getting in the way of our addiction, it would lead to a constant defense and often a rage directed at those who least deserved it.

We had given up on our dreams and everything that was important to us. We wasted away what talents we had on drugs that we could have used for good instead of the troubles we caused family and others with our using. In one point or another we've been praised on the great talents and skills God bestowed on us, only to allow it to escape our grasp as if it were sand in our hands. Many have asked ourselves "Will we ever be able to harness our talents in a positive way?" Many of us came into NA with talents we thought were wasted. We may have known we had talents but didn't know how to use them. When we reflected on the time wasted, along with our talents, resentments would fester and build like cancer until we became our own worst enemy.

Some of us asked..."Will we truly be able to make amends and be forgiven?" Only when we surrendered to our higher power and made amends to ourselves were we allowing the healing process to begin within. We turned towards our family and loved ones for the wrong doing of our hands. We learned to ask ourselves "can we forgive ourselves?" Life should be happy and stress free, but living in addiction is stressful.
unmappedHistorical.moment: NA gave us a place to find our talents once again. We learned how to harness our God given talents. We learned to use the creative freedom NA has to bring out our talents and help us carry our message.

unmappedHistorical.quote: "By telling our own story someone else is bound to be suffering from a similar problem and our experience tells them how to deal with it.... what works for one , might work for another."
unmappedHistorical.body: When we share our experience it will hopefully help the still suffering addict. In this selfless program we seek to guide one another to find a new way to not only live... but live better more fulfilling and prosperous lives. By telling our own story we allow our disease no shadow to hide in... and addiction dies in the light of honesty. We enable other addicts the solutions and tools they may be seeking. Letting another gain insight from something outside themselves helps us see the beauty of one addict helping another. We thought we knew it all. Anonymity is half of our name but the principal behind it is were our freedom begins. When we get here it is easy for us to only look at the differences.We all came into the rooms the same way. Many of us coming into recovery were uncertain, scared and fearful of the unknown. Drugs had made our lives unmanageable as we continued to come back and come back clean we all hear something that is not far from our own experience. It is freeing to only share our ESH and leave the rest in God's hands. When we share about our recovery both the good and the bad we become able to be part of the program. We see others that find similarities in our stories and learn again that we are never alone... and never on our own in our struggles. We suggest we attend meetings, sit and listen, and learn how the system works. This sounds like support in a simple form... listening and giving suggestions. It is through this unity that we are bound together to ensure that none who enter and want to stay slip though the cracks.
unmappedHistorical.moment: When we share honestly we help each other feel less unique. We draw our strength from each other by sharing our past lives and remembering what it was like. No one can argue with another when they share their experience instead of counseling.

unmappedHistorical.quote: " Living clean for a period of time provides valuable experience working the program through many life changes".
unmappedHistorical.body: As we stay in the program for a while, we may notice that some of the things that we do for our recovery maintenance have evolved over time and changed. It is important to remember that we are given only a daily reprieve from the disease of addiction and are never "cured". The staples of our program, which include the 12 steps, writing, meetings, prayer, and fellowship with other recovering addicts is just as powerful a tool against relapse now as when we first came into the program. What changes is our lives, and our thinking. That is part of the recovery promise that our literature tells us. As a direct result of working the program to the best of our ability, for a period of time, recovery takes on a new meaning. Today we are able to grow emotionally, and spiritually, instead of staying stuck as we did for so long during active addiction. This is true for all addicts who choose to continue to grow in the program. We can provide valuable experience for newcomers, and old timers alike, if we continue to work the tools of the program and continue to live just for today. Over time our ability to deal with life clean, has taken on a whole new meaning for us. We can look forward to dealing with life s challenges today instead of running away from them. Listening to other addicts share these experiences at meetings, about how they get through these challenges clean by utilizing the NA program, and all the tools they put into practice in order to get through problems, gives us hope that we too can get through our own problems clean.
unmappedHistorical.moment: Today we can share our experiences of working through life s problems with other addicts by sharing solutions at meetings, and how this program has helped us to come out the other side clean.

unmappedHistorical.quote: " Many of us did not come to our fellowship with an sincere desire to stay clean. That came after the fog had lifted and after we realized that staying clean was possible".
unmappedHistorical.body: Many addicts come here from all walks of life, and all different backgrounds. Once we make it to an NA meeting, we will find this out after a short period of time by listening to all the other addicts in the rooms share their experiences and stories. We may have gotten here through jails, or from an institution, or from the street, but the important thing is that we made it here alive. Many of our fellow active addicts aren't so lucky, and find themselves still out there living in misery, or perhaps locked up for long periods of time, or even dead. It doesn't really matter how we found ourselves here, and clean, or whether we decided at the time to change our life, once we are here, we have a new chance at life, which we never had before we made it here. If we follow suggestions of fellow addicts who have been here before us, and work this simple program of Narcotics Anonymous, we will develop the desire to continue on this path, and an honest desire to stay clean from all drugs, and mind or mood changing chemicals. It may take some of us longer than others, but if we stick and stay, we can be here for the miracle to happen. We will realize that staying clean is a real possibility, and with that realization, we have a newfound hope in life to begin to participate in a meaningful, and productive life, free from the grips of addiction.
unmappedHistorical.moment: Today we will renew our commitment to our recovery by attending an NA meeting, and by reaching out to another addict to share and be part of the miracle of recovery from addiction together.
