unmappedHistorical.quote: “ We seek solutions rather than dilemmas. Productive means being clean, creative and loving today”.
unmappedHistorical.body: In order to continue to be a productive member of society, we as addicts need to keep our priorities in order. First must be our own recovery, we must never forget that we are all addicts, and are powerless over this disease of addiction. We must fit our lives to the program, and not the other way around, as so many addicts who fail try to do. Staying clean is always our number one priority, and not using no matter what a simple way is to remember that. We have tools today to help us get through anything that we may come across in life, and getting to the other side of situations without using, damaging others, or ourselves is what the tools of the NA program guide us in. It takes practice. Being successful in life, and our relations with others takes work. We didn’t come to NA possessing the necessary tool set to get us through life, or we wouldn’t have needed to come here in the first place. We wouldn’t have been running to buy drugs daily to escape life instead. Learning the art of solution finding through the drudges of life on life’s terms is where we practice these principles and all that we learn from our program and the steps. Taking what we learn here at our meetings and applying it to all aspects of our lives gives us renewed energies to pursue the necessary actions that lead to solutions today. Our past habits, and survival tactics will keep us stuck, and will not help us today, and unless we are willing to change, we will find ourselves angry, and frustrated at life, where we need not be. Remember this is a “ WE” program and we keep in constant contact with other recovering addicts as to not isolate ourselves. Getting to meetings regularly and sticking to what works keeps us in the solution and gets us out of the problems.
unmappedHistorical.moment: Today we will talk to others about finding the solution to problems that may be getting us down. We will not allow ourselves to fall into anger and depression, and instead put our energies towards taking the actions necessary to stay in the solution.

unmappedHistorical.quote: "There is no area of our lives that the disease does not affect. The truth is that fear is present in every area of our lives."
unmappedHistorical.body: Our disease affects everything we do in our lives, including our decision making. We may never know how much the disease of addiction has affected our lives. It has affected our family, our jobs, marriages, recreation, finances, and most of all our spirituality. Spiritually we were empty, our families torn apart, our homes broken or nonexistent, and relationships based off of unhealthy needs for attachment or using someone for something they had. In short, it had affected our whole lives. We are restrained by addiction. We are subject to it as a slave is subject to his master. The disease is always alive; it does not go away. When it creeps in, we may not be aware of it because we are caught in the moment. When it takes a hold of us, we tend to be less able to understand which way to go until we start making mistakes with our using. One of our character defects shows the more unaware we are of drifting into isolation. We grow farther away from the program and closer to relapse. We thought when we stopped using, our problem was cured. But the truth was, we did not know ourselves without the drugs. We lived in fear. We found that these things just got worse and didn't seem to get better for fear of the unknown we held. We feared how people might react. As we recover, we see how fear has been a constant struggle for us to overcome. We were more comfortable staying in the pain we knew than doing something different. We learned all we have to change is everything. "We have nothing to fear but fear itself." We learned to overcome things that baffled us before. By putting one foot in front of the other, we learned how we could get through any fears we had and get through them clean. Through NA we learned how to face our fears instead of running. Once we become open-minded, we can fully surrender and overcome the fear; placing faith and trust in the program and a higher power replaces that fear.
unmappedHistorical.moment: with the help of God, we find it is possible to live a new way of life.

unmappedHistorical.quote: ‘‘In order to survive, we must set aside the differences we live by and become part of a greater whole.’’
unmappedHistorical.body:
Narcotics Anonymous, at first, seems like a room full of people who are different. The program of NA taught us that isolation is one of our biggest enemies. Living in our active addiction, we relied on our primal instincts to feed our necessity for our next high. Often, we were selfish and thought of ourselves first. We came from a place of fear and isolation that was ruled by selfish and self-centered behavior.

Our differences become part of the group, allowing us to come together and assist each other. The importance of no big i s or little u s is the importance of NA. By becoming a part of something bigger than ourselves, we are allowing ourselves to recover together. The group is always stronger than the individual. By identifying with another addict, they become part of us, and us a part of them. When we try to be more understanding of other s feelings, we can all get along.

We were once frightened by the idea of loving others, for we did not love ourselves. We learned to live again by unifying with others. As we become part of NA, our stories meld into the NA story. We become NA. And everywhere we go, we have a home. Only with unity and camaraderie can we achieve a higher understanding and purpose.
unmappedHistorical.moment: being a part of NA as a greater whole; heightens our base of recovery and uplifts us into the ultimate freedom that we were striving for in our active addiction.

unmappedHistorical.quote: "We must puncture our egos and realize that we have much more work to do."
unmappedHistorical.body: When we were using, we never listened to anyone else's opinion on our using because we were closed-minded and in denial. As active addicts, we were big-headed egomaniacs, always thinking of ourselves first and ensuring we got what we wanted. We thought we had everything figured out, but we had never been more wrong. It's important that we realize there is much more to life than the way we've been living. We need to understand that living life on our terms will never work for us. Never thinking of how our actions may affect others. Ego gets in our way of growth if we let it. We must get out of our self-centeredness and realize we can't do this alone. We let go of our pride and hear others when they offer suggestions that can help us. We come to realize we are not in control and turn our lives over to our higher power for guidance and open our minds to allow growth. There is so much work we need to work on but to remember the principles of NA, "easy does it" and "one day at a time." We don't usually carry a pen around to deflate our egos, but when we do it starts with the 12 steps of Narcotics Anonymous. By working the steps with a sponsor helps build growth. In order to work these steps, we have to develop the principle of humility. We must humble ourselves, remain teachable, and get to work in order to learn and grow as we move forward. Humility is accepting our place in the present. We will never be perfect and being humble helps us remember we are not God. Not more than, not less than...life as it is...that is how it works. We must realize that our recovery process is a long journey. Not just a 30-day treatment place, but an everyday thing. A lifelong process not just a short process. We must do all we can to ensure we let go of ego, so we are not Edging God Out.
unmappedHistorical.moment: we must always remember we need to be beacons, not only for ourselves but for other addicts also.

unmappedHistorical.quote: "Here we found Hope. If the Narcotics Anonymous program worked for them, it might work for us."
unmappedHistorical.body:
What is the Narcotics Anonymous Program?

We could not quit using by ourselves. After countless times trying, we finally gave up and decided to give something new a try, the NA program. We came in hopeless and beaten. The disease of addiction ran our lives and we couldn't see any way out of our destructiveness. Many of us were in despair and felt hopeless. Our lives had hit rock bottom, and we had nothing. Then, coming into the rooms of NA, we found a shimmer of hope. Where we were once alone, we now had found strength in numbers. We all had found something special when we walked into these rooms. We see people smiling and laughing, something many of us forgot how to do. We wonder where this has been in our lives, and after attending a few meetings, we found hope that we could have what they have. Hope is the light at the end of the tunnel.

We found hope when we surrendered and put ourselves in God's hands and in God's will. Early on, we watched others in the rooms...seeing others recover from addiction, and live new lives. We found other addicts that we could relate to who had gotten out of the mess and carried a message. If the NA program worked for them, then it might work for others. We learned quickly that hope is contagious, and we were ready for a new disease. In Narcotics Anonymous, we are loved until we can love ourselves. We hope that, "An addict, any addict, can stop using, lose the desire to use, and find a new way of life."
unmappedHistorical.moment: Hope is a four-letter word, and so is love. In the fellowship, we hope to see people stick around long enough to be able to be loved.

unmappedHistorical.quote: "After we accept that we created our own hell and that there is a God that wants to help us, we begin to make progress in solving our problems".
unmappedHistorical.body: One of the biggest hurdles for addicts is to recognize that we are our own worst enemy. We hear many times over, in many different ways in our literature that reaffirms this. " An addict alone is in bad company", rings true for us, as much as we may be in denial that we are indeed the cause of our own problems. Creating our own hell is what happens when we allow our ego and thoughts to rule our life and are closed off to the rest of the world, and any help. This is exactly where the disease wants us, isolated, and ego’d up. This way when we believe that we are actually in control of our drug addiction, it is actually the other way around. Drugs have taken our will and taken over our life, ahead of all else. Our family’s, loved ones, and friends all can see this, but unfortunately it takes more than the pleading of loved ones to break through the wall of denial that the disease puts us behind. Being completely powerless to this disease means that we are unable to break through that denial on our own. It takes the help of God, and other recovering addicts to help us break through, and once we do, to keep us from running back. We can then begin to learn how to solve problems, instead of creating new ones. The belief in a power greater than us is where our power comes from now, and if we strengthen this belief together, we begin to see that the miracle that this program promises us, that no addict need die from the horrors of addiction is true for all of us.
unmappedHistorical.moment: Today we will look at the good in our lives and focus on solving problems with the help of God and others in the program. We no longer have to be our own worst enemy.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “By recognizing the defects in our characters, and letting go of them spiritually, we were ready to have sanity restored to us.
unmappedHistorical.body: Many of us hold onto the belief when we get to the program of NA, that we can straighten out our lives, if only we can stay clean, and put the drugs down. It doesn't take long before we realize that drugs were only the tip of the iceberg. We have a tendency to hold onto our old beliefs, and way of thinking, even though we may be clean. This is where we all begin our recovery process, and slowly the realization that we have many lives, and living problems that we were hiding by using drugs. Our first realization that we need help, and that the program of Narcotics Anonymous has the help we need, gives us hope that we can do this. The proof is in the many addicts who have come before us, and have been practicing these principles, and in doing so have stayed clean, and improved their lives. Understanding that our old ways of going about life will not serve us well today, and will keep us clinging to fear, and desperation. Many addicts who are unwilling to let go our past behaviors, and thinking will find it hard to stay clean. We must begin to slowly let go of our past, in order to make room for new habits, and as a result of this, and new way of thinking of life, ourselves, and others, gives us a new life that offers happiness, and joy. We learn to rely on our Higher Power for strength to help us to let go, through our step work, and through talking with, and fellowshipping with others in the meetings. Staying on the road of recovery is a constant cycle of letting go and moving on. We learn that we are opening the door for Gods help when we are able to do this, and this helps to strengthen our belief, and offers us some of the sanity talked about in our literature. Today we can overcome the fear of letting go and letting God.
unmappedHistorical.moment: Today we look forward to allowing Gods help into our lives. We can let go of the wheel today, and practice turning our will and life over to His care.

unmappedHistorical.quote: " we will eventually hear someone who flat out makes us feel lucky by comparison. We will grow to know gratitude, to see where we came from and how far we have progressed. "
unmappedHistorical.body: Many of us play the victim. We came into the room self-centered, self-seeking individuals. We sometimes struggled with hearing other people's stories. Sometimes it made us question whether we were addicts too... we kept coming back and eventually heard others rather than ourselves. We might think WOW, maybe our lives weren't that bad. We hear of others pain caused by the disease of addiction. We can no longer play the victim. We will hear a person in a meeting that we can compare with and feel a connection. We see how far others have come in their recovery, and realize, we can do this. After hearing others stories it gave us hope that we too could recover from addiction. Once we change our attitude away from being alone in our misery, we learn to accept life as it is. We learn that life happens to all of us. We began to live rather than just existing. What a gift that is. In recovery, we realize it's not how much or what we did. We are all addicts. We all have different stories. We continue to grow until we are blessed with being able to give back.
unmappedHistorical.moment: By sharing our past we help others come to the reality of how close we were to death. We all have the choice to recover.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “The same power that has helped us deal with our obsession will be the guide and source of courage when we ask for it.”
unmappedHistorical.body: We came to Narcotics Anonymous broken. Spiritually bankrupt. When we were using our vision of Hope was slim. That little bit of trust is vital when we are desperate for courage. We were constantly obsessed with the idea of ways and means to get more this is one of the core symptoms of the disease of addiction. Fear is the power that helped with our obsession to use, the fear to lose everything that we worked for everything we gained in our lives. Trusting our higher power is one of the first obstacles we face in the program. But as we go to more meetings and listen to others share we realize that a higher power is what will save us. We are so thankful that we have been given the power to let go of our past. As long as we are centered in our higher power and not in ourselves we are able to find the courage to share at meetings. Courage is not of our own but rather a power greater than us. Courage is a very useful spiritual principle, the more we rely on our higher power to give it to us in our daily lives, the easier it becomes to find it. Each day our courage of doing the next right thing makes us become a better person. Before we knew it we were able to share and reach out with the courage. We learned that being open minded willing and honest with ourselves and others there is a better way to live. We feel welcome and most importantly we see freedom from addiction. We ask for help in another profound moment of surrender. We are not alone. We start to see that the power is always with us this power is our strength and with courage we continue through the steps on our new journey. Our higher power is truly our own. Every member has a different outlook and that is powerful. That is magical. No longer haunted by our past we feel a sense of freedom that has been given to us freely. What we were once so desperate to find-our higher power shows us that we had it all along.
unmappedHistorical.moment: Our higher powers will for us is always a lot better than our own. When we try to live on our own will bad things will happen. When in doubt always pray.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “We admitted that we used drugs, but many of us did not think we had a problem.”
unmappedHistorical.body: Many of us came into the rooms of NA openly admitting we used drugs. We were often proud of our insane behaviors. We couldn’t see through the haze that drugs had built in our minds. Denial ran rampant in every aspect of our lives. Denial opened the door for our disease to lie to us and tell us we wanted the bad things back in our lives. Many addicts relapse because denial tells us we can use successfully no matter how we felt. So many addicts have told themselves, “I can control myself” or “I can quit whenever I want.” These statements are a product of naïve pride. These are only boasts leading addicts back to an unmanageable and powerless life of desperation. These misguided words are just the byproduct of a previously failed attempt. Many of us thought our past would always haunt us. We can’t change our past but we can change what we do from this point on.
unmappedHistorical.moment: We admit we do have a problem that’s not curable but can be arrested at any point. We will allow the Gift Of Desperation to sink in. We surrender saying we are done just for today.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “We can make amends by our actions. They don't always have to be verbal.”
unmappedHistorical.body: How many times did we say we are sorry? We said it time after time only to repeat the same behavior later. We can make our amends by staying clean and learning how to be more productive members of society. Sometimes it is easier to say we are sorry, and think that this is over. There are times where verbal amends are impossible or unwanted. The beauty of living amends is that we don’t just say words; the old saying talk is cheap makes sense here. It seemed we wanted to save our face by apologizing rather than save our ass by changing. Action needs to be applied here. Without changing our behaviors, we will slip back into dangerous ways. Our actions show if we change or not. We can begin making amends through action even if we are not on step 9 yet... we can start acting differently, not using. NA provides a way for us to quit just saying we are going to change, and instead we learn how to be the change. Being spiritually reborn through our new way of living and communication with others – God as we understand Him leads us to a new level of surrender this fills our lives with purpose and meaning. Now we have a chance to learn how to live and let others live. It required some level of willingness but with this attitude we may feel this new happiness, joy and freedom. When such an amend needs to be made, an opportunity will arise to take action. By helping a newcomer or doing some volunteer work or donating to charity. We can make our living amends by caring for a sick parent or loved one, paying forward a kindness that was done for us or simply by staying clean. The one things amends should never be though are installment payments on false guilt or false shame. We can remove ourselves from fear and take the actions necessary. Whatever the action needed, depends on the situation and our patience. We get to the exact nature, admit our wrongs out loud and move into the serenity that the program offers us.
unmappedHistorical.moment: This is God's thing. Others see our lives change and that helps them see we do recover.
unmappedHistorical.note: Preserved without assigning a calendar date. The source document states its dates are historical writing dates.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “As we grow, we become more aware of the key to willingness. “
unmappedHistorical.body: Willingness is the quality or state of being prepared to do something; Readiness. Willingness is the foundation for any addict who has the desire to stop using. Many of us came into NA scared of our own shadow. We had no idea how to live. Pain is one of our keys to willingness. We wanted the pain to stop, but many had been hurt time after time, when we tried anything new. We needed hope. In recovery, we need to become uncomfortable in order to grow. Once our desire to stay clean out ways our desire to use , then and only then, will our willingness to live a better way of life have meaning ,strength and motivation. We see addiction in others but it’s their journey to find themselves before it’s too late. We keep an eye on them and share our experience, strength and hope whenever the opportunity arises. Our willingness to accept others where they are with an open-mind allows for growth within us to not be judge-mental. We've learned that we can't change others. As we grow and are willing to ask others how to be more accepting. We learn how to calm down and be positive communicaters. We can only lead by example. NA provides us that hope which changes our lives. It begins with the willingness to change everything and to surrender every day from Day 1!! These are the 9 suggestions: 1. avoid people, places and things we used with or at 2. come early, stay late 3. get and use a Sponsor, 4. don't use and go to meetings 5. go to 90 meetings in 90 days 6. get a Home Group 7. use the phone 8. keep coming back it works 9. get involved in service. With willingness, it allows us to be open-minded to actively listen & listen to learn. Hope came when we found others that were like us and had found a way to stay clean. We finally understood it is possible for drug addicts to get and stay clean. NA provided us that hope which changed our lives. As we continued to grow the things that once scared us no longer were as scary. Opening up and getting honest and vulnerable with our Sponsors became easier. We come to understand if we don't get humble we will continue to be humiliated.
unmappedHistorical.moment: Willingness to live by spiritual principals is a cleansing of my soul.
unmappedHistorical.note: Preserved without assigning a calendar date. The source document states its dates are historical writing dates.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: "Recovery is a beautiful chance that many addicts thought had passed them by until they found the fellowship of N.A."
unmappedHistorical.body: We came in broken and beaten by our disease. Many of us didn't want to live or felt that we would ever get the chance to live. Life was a monotonous routine of finding ways and means to use. Some of us early in recovery still have days with strong desires to use. We learn to rely on NA meetings to help us recover from our addiction. Our desire to stay in recovery and grow is strong as we have found a new freedom from active addiction and a much better way to live. Recovery and the chance to live again has been a beautiful process. We learn that recovery is not a destination but a journey that has ups and downs. We fully enjoy the ups while being clean, and the downs become a learning experience we can share with our fellow addicts. In active addiction, we may have talked about our dreams and ambitions. Inside some of us thought they never would happen. We have let ourselves down time and time again. When we tried we failed over and over again. We had no clue how to live. After learning to live the NA way we have found we are slower to anger and more understanding of those around us. Our family life has become something we can thank our Higher Power for. They are no longer the source of constant fighting. We are given the chance to build relationships we thought long lost. Recovery is a brand new life that is totally different than our life in active addiction. It changes our behaviors and thoughts to new ways....and a new focus... We are grateful for the gift of recovery, getting out of our old way of life that included the use of drugs. We don't want this beautiful chance to pass us by. After awhile we learned not only how to survive but to thrive. We are given the chance to live what we thought had passed us by. We remember that it is a process, a journey not a destination.
unmappedHistorical.moment: We realize what a beautiful chance to live we have been given. We realize our gift of recovery is fragile. We will protect it with our lives because without it we will surely die.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “The newcomer is the lifeblood of NA and when one comes to us seeking help we welcome them with open arms.” (Pg. 97 Ln.30 –
unmappedHistorical.body: The Twelve Traditions: Tradition Three As we walked through the doors on Narcotics Anonymous, we felt out of place. We were nervous and a little scared. We, as addicts, come in scared of being vulnerable. For many, showing vulnerability could get us manipulated into all sorts of nonsense. We all come in as newcomers. When one comes to us seeking help with their struggles, we help with open arms. Welcoming newcomers is one of the best ways that we can let them know we care. Members who have been in NA for a long time make us feel welcome. Our service is best exemplified in the act of one addict helping another. They welcome us with hugs and the love an NA group has. There is a sense of relief, and we feel right at home. By making newcomers feel welcome, the ice is broken, and hopefully, they can see we truly care. Assisting them and pointing them towards help, the newcomer is the most important person in NA. We can all share our storied and the way we stay clean. It also gives us the ability to give someone in need the same help we needed at some point.
unmappedHistorical.moment: We need to stay a newcomer to remain teachable and stay clean. We never know when we might need a hug, the message of NA, or the experience of another addict or newcomer to save our own lives.
unmappedHistorical.note: Preserved without assigning a calendar date. The source document states its dates are historical writing dates.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “Just as we went to any length to get drugs, so must we go to any lengths to learn to get clean.”
unmappedHistorical.body: How many of us knew how to get clean when we first get to NA? There was nothing we wouldn't do to get high. So why do we make excuses that keep us from putting our recovery first? We knew how to use drugs, that was for sure. When we place our focus and energy on getting clean we have less energy for the negativity of addiction to influence our behaviors and thoughts. Our using didn't take a day off so we need to do all we can to keep from using if we want to stay clean. We caution you we can’t take shortcuts. If we forget, our last use, we are doomed to repeat it. Not only is addiction a 24/7 disease, but recovery is a 24/7 solution. If we take a moment away from remembering recovery must come first. We may return to the misery of using once again. So we must be willing to do whatever it takes to get clean.
unmappedHistorical.moment: For us combating addiction needs to be fought with the same spiritual force that we used with, we surrender and try to gain an understanding of spiritual principles. These are the tools we use to let go of our self -obsession. If we put the same effort into getting clean, as we did into using, we will succeed.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “As we began to learn how to change our perception of reality, we, as newcomers, were encouraged to avoid making any major decisions on our own.”
unmappedHistorical.body: Almost all decisions we made on our own in active addiction led to disaster. Some of us, as newcomers, wanted to change everything right away. For example; a new house, a new job, a new relationship, going to college or getting our family back. We find new situations everyday where our judgement is back and forth and to the extremes. We are trying to renew our vision of recovery to act more sanely. But first we had to learn how to stay clean. Perception is the ability to see, hear, or become aware of something through the senses, a way of regarding, understanding, or interpreting something; a mental impression. Before we came to NA the only way we knew to change our perception of reality was using drugs. Our whole perception of life had to be shattered if we were to recover. We had made a mess of our lives. What harm would it do to learn to trust someone else with our major decisions? If we want to learn a new way of life we have to learn to accept directions. We need others to guide and teach us how to live differently. With guidance from recovering addicts, our sponsor and our Higher Power we learn to make decisions, not act on a thought without looking at the consequences that may arise. We need to learn to put our recovery first. If we don’t have our priorities in order, we can lose everything in a relapse. We hear members suggest not making any major decisions on our own because our thinking is still distorted by addiction. Forming a relationship with reality takes time and so does learning to live the Twelve Steps.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: "There is one truth which helps guide us. True spiritual principles are never in conflict; they always complement each other. "
unmappedHistorical.body: Our second step tells us, “through open minded effort we act our way into right thinking letting our Higher Power find us rather than searching for God with only our minds” GB pg 64 L 24-26 We find that when we do this, we rid ourselves of the personalities, prejudices and self-centeredness that can destroy not only ourselves, but our groups and the people closely associated with us. Conflict is friction and pain caused by selfishness. As addicts we were nothing but selfish. When we let go of selfishness and let a Higher Power guide us, we come to realize we are stronger as a group and unstoppable when working together. We are told we will not have to fight for nonexistent virtues anymore. Why fight when spiritual principles are never in conflict? When we Surrender and see we can let go of whatever gets in the way of serenity we can grow together. Our Steps help us grow and our Traditions help us to Surrender the things that cause conflict within our Group. NA helps us Surrender our egos so that we can find the truth rather than continuing to fight for nonexistent virtues. When we first came to NA we were confused and tired persons. We were tired of ourselves, of our old ideas and sick thoughts. Here in NA we've meet people who learned how to solve their problems. They told us that we need to use spiritual principles. Our thinking is distorted by addiction so self-centeredness penetrates in all our decisions. - If we are open-minded & honest with ourselves we will have no problem developing a loving relationship with God, family and friends. We need to hear others messages of hope. The more we improve our conscious contact with God, through prayer and meditation, the more often we pause when doubtful and say “God, WE DONT KNOW WHAT TO DO PLEASE SHOW US WHICH WAY TO GO?” When we finally get our own selfish motives out of the way, and pray for guidance we begin to find peace. We begin to feel a calm joy. We begin to experience awareness and an empathy with other people that would never be possible using drugs.
unmappedHistorical.moment: We practice spiritual principles and we allow the light to shine upon them.
unmappedHistorical.note: Preserved without assigning a calendar date. The source document states its dates are historical writing dates.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: Though we still face human pain, life finally begins to get meaningful. Clean living is possible when we rely on a Higher Power daily to provide us with spiritual progress, establishing us in useful living.
unmappedHistorical.body: NA doesn't say it will take the pain away. At times we found ourselves in confusion. Without drugs we thought life was pretty hard because drugs were our source of relief for a long time. Emotions were hiding inside us distorting our view of life, and they are now on the surface and we have to meet them. We felt the consequences of not accepting responsibility for our lives. Many of us were running around purposeless before we found NA. We began to see pain can be a great motivator. Pain no longer has the strangle hold it once had on us. We found a purpose, first in learning how to live for ourselves without masking our hurt with drugs. We later find a purpose in sharing our gift of recovery with others. Recovery is a continuing process; going through the Steps with our Sponsor we discover new revelations about ourselves and others. NA gives us a way to first survive the pain, and eventually thrive through the pain. We now have a new chance to live on a spiritual basis. This is our chance to get a daily reprieve from our insanity. Now, we’ve got a new source of strength – a Higher Power. The NA program can restore us to the state where our lives become meaningful. With help of our HP, and our friends in recovery, we can face life on its own terms. We learn to try to be useful to God and other human beings. We no longer need to be a burden to ourselves or others. Helping others can get us out of our sick heads, and restore our relationship with God. This is how we can become a part of humanity. It is something that we had forgotten for a long time. Some days we grow, sometimes we stay the same and sometimes we regress. Daily reliance on our HP helps us to be in the here and now and take some baby steps accepting life as it comes.
unmappedHistorical.note: Preserved without assigning a calendar date. The source document states its dates are historical writing dates.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “Our purpose is to be rid of guilt—not wallow in it! We must be done with the past, not cling to it.”
unmappedHistorical.body: By writing our Fourth Step inventory we examine the events and situations that have caused us guilt and shame. We allowed ourselves to be in the mode of guilt for so many years during our active addiction. It is easy to begin our recovery by looking at all the horrible things we have done and say, " poor me!" We didn't come to NA because we are perfect beings. Lots of what we did in the past was not pretty. We destroyed our lives as well as anyone else's life that got in the way of our tornado of destruction. The purpose of our 4 Step is not to confess or to show how bad we have been. We do th this so that we can see the past for what it truly is and so we can move forward in recovery without the limitations of our past guilt. Otherwise we will continue to think others are at fault. We need to become aware of the harm we are bringing to others for us to grow. Old thinking is what got us here. Now it is time to move towards our future leaving guilt and shame behind. We don’t have to be fully done with our past to prepare for our future in recovery. Too many times, as addicts, we lived a life of partying. The only difference now is that sometimes we throw a different kind of party, a pity party. We do not let the negativity that has been placed upon us by the world, disempower us. We can’t live in our past. We now have a new life without the use of drugs.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “We try to avoid asking for specific things. It’s hard because we are so sure we know what is right for us. We know now that if we pray to do God’s will, we will receive what’s best for us.”
unmappedHistorical.source: Gray Book pg 58 lines 12-15 How It Works (Step 11)
unmappedHistorical.body: We come into NA self-centered, self-obsessed individuals. We were separated from life completely. Praying for certain things can raise our self-centeredness and allow the disease to control us again. Our self-obsession may cause problems in our lives that we have no idea how to live with. We may have the insanity of not being able to quiet our mind or sleep. There is no doubt in our mind that our best thinking got us here, and that it can keep us here too. At times, we do not know what is best. It is easy to say that we can understand God’s will when everything is going well. It also can be really hard at times to see the will of a loving God in our lives when a relative or friend dies or any situation that we are faced with life on life’s terms. We admit that we don't have all the answers. NA helps us learn to calm the mind and seek the God consciousness that meditation gives. Many of us have faced difficult life events while clean. Sometimes we only can pray and try to accept how things are going. Some things we can change and some things we can’t, but have to accept. Sometimes, we only need to seek what is the best thing we can do, just surrender and let go. If we ask for specific things we may be put on pause by our Greater Power because it was self-will. We learn to not ask for specific things but only God’s will for us, and the power to carry that out. Prayer for Gods will is a sign of our surrender. By the time we have gotten here we have acquired some faith. Faith and trust is built when we live our Steps. We may struggle at times to Surrender, but it helps us know how to believe God’s will for us is the best. We no longer want our will anymore. We now truly understand what it is to serve a loving, caring God. We serve this God rather than depending on our own ways.
unmappedHistorical.note: Preserved without assigning a calendar date. The source document states its dates are historical writing dates.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “We can always find people who have difficulties similar to our own and do succeed.”
unmappedHistorical.body: When we came to the Fellowship of Narcotics Anonymous, we found other recovering addicts who had overcome similar adversities and difficulties. Our lives looked like a mess. Many of us had health problems, debts, and conflicts. This seemed like the only way of life we knew. We had no idea how to live clean. We learned that we should stay clean no matter what happens in our own life. We began to Surrender to the program of NA. We found that we should ask for help, and allow others to help us. We may learn to allow others to help us by asking for the help of addicts who have had some experience in similar situations. We may then learn that we should take responsibility and get into action seeking solutions. In NA people share with us freely their ESH. They can offer us their help, time and care. They are leading us by example, and when we are ready we do the same. We are able to draw on the experience of others which helps us recognize our need to be willing to let our defects go. Many of these defects had helped us survive the world which we once knew. Seeing and hearing about changes in others with similar experiences helps us to become willing. This is the way it works, because the therapeutic value of one addict helping another is without parallel; this is a powerful process that continues throughout our recovery. We become aware of our actions and behaviors that we previously hadn’t noticed had a negative impact. By seeing this we are able to get out of ourselves. We are able see the world clearer and how changing our actions and behaviors affects the world around us. We learn how to be of use to others which helps us learn how to become a part of society.
unmappedHistorical.note: Preserved without assigning a calendar date. The source document states its dates are historical writing dates.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “We don’t have to be religious. All that is required is a willingness to believe.”
unmappedHistorical.body: Religious dogmas seemed not to work for us. Some of us came into NA with resentments against organized religion. We had been hurt by humans that said they were carrying out God's directions. Internally, we were spiritually broken. If we have desire without willingness, the program is less likely to work for us. We don't have to believe in God to begin to recover, we just need the willingness to believe that the program can help us stay clean. Willingness to believe helps us walk through the threshold to get past our fears. It is a key that opens once closed doors to our freedom. Without it we may work our way back to insanity. We needed something other than religion to help us learn how to live differently. NA gave us a spiritual not religious program to learn how to practically apply spiritual principles in our lives. Spiritual principles work no matter what. When our desire to stay clean is more than our desire to use we have come to believe a power greater than ourselves can transform our faith into actions. This is the only way. Practicing surrender and acceptance make it possible to become willing to let go and change. What works for us are actions and experience of other addicts who went down the road of recovery before us. These actions may seem hard sometimes but we should try anyway. We had seen other addicts made it and we decided that it can work for us. Every day the vision of loving and caring God should be a main theme for us. Accepting a concept of a loving God was new to us, it was suggested to place old ideas on a shelf and focus on aspects of a loving caring God instead – one which had gotten us here and provided those who came before us with recovery. If we have an issue with the word God we can come to understand it to stand for Grow up Or Die, Good Orderly Direction or the Gift Of Desperation.
unmappedHistorical.moment: We must become willing to trust the process.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “The progression of the disease is an ongoing process, even during abstinence, no matter how long.”
unmappedHistorical.body: Time doesn't cure our disease. At any given moment if we forget that we struggle from the disease of addiction we can be setting ourselves up to return to a lifestyle of active addiction. We have heard some say clean time doesn't equal recovery. Mere abstinence is not nearly enough. . If we get caught up in just abstinence and not living the program we are setting ourselves up for failure. No matter where we go if we don't remain vigilant to living the principles of NA we will not recover. Our disease may use our sub-conscience to whisper cunning things into our ears and minds. Though we think we have learned enough to stay clean our disease is still there. Our disease can still keep growing in the background even when we are not using. One moment of weakness can be all it takes for us to lose everything and return to the unmanageability and the insanity of active addiction. Relapse is not a requirement. We don’t have to jump into the rabbit holes anymore that caused us so much drama in our lives. Complete surrender is the only way for us to receive freedom from active addiction. One of the greatest forms of surrender is to not indulge in our toxic emotions. We quit reacting like children. No longer do we deny our personal responsibilities. We do this is by living a thorough and honest program every day. The lie is dead. We do recover in the rooms of Narcotics Anonymous. It is only with a daily reprieve and constant awareness that we are truly set free. The tools of NA are our daily medication to heal us.
unmappedHistorical.moment: We have a daily reprieve, only with our daily practice of surrender. Active addiction condemned us to death but NA has provided a way for us to have temporary relief in each moment we surrender.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “Often we found that the higher our drugs took us, the lower they brought us.”
unmappedHistorical.body: We used drugs to take us higher than we thought we could ever get on our own. As we tried to escape life we dreamed of finding a higher sense of freedom from the pain and our emotions. We continued looking for the right medication, fix, or the magic elixir that would solve our ultimate problem….ourselves. In active addiction, we used drugs to avoid life on life's terms. We convinced ourselves that we could turn to drugs and act out on our character defects whenever coping with life was difficult. This led us to a continuous cycle of insanity where we felt highs and lows. Though the highs felt great and the lows were very difficult we came to find that drugs only offered us a temporary high, and at the end of the day, we were left with nothing. We tried everything and the different drugs we used slowly escalated with time. No combination was successful for us. Some of us ended up in jail, hospitals or rehabs. The higher we got on drugs the lower they brought us. We compromised all our moral values for the next fix. We lived on the animal level. We used to live and lived to use. Often doing things we never considered an option in our non-addiction driven life. Some of us prostituted ourselves just to get that next fix. All of us at some point sold ourselves in one way shape or form. We demoralized ourselves repeatedly. We were running from ourselves trying to escape life and reach that ultimate euphoria that we found the first time we used, but the more we used the quicker our addiction overtook us and took us to places we never wanted to go, doing things we never thought we would ever do. We thought the shame and guilt we felt over these activities would kill us. We know today that any drug we do that is mind or mood altering will take us back to the roller coaster of insanity. We found that life is truly a beautiful chance that may have passed us by if we had not found the rooms of Narcotics Anonymous. Through the spiritual principles of N.A. we are able to begin dealing with the trash of our past and rebuild a new life better than anything we had ever dreamed. Once we searched for the magic elixir that would fix us and in NA we found that it was this simple spiritual not religious program known as Narcotics Anonymous that would solve our problems and offer us a new life. In recovery, we find that our best day using will not outweigh our worst day clean. Although life may get us down, we have the choice to recover “just for today.”
unmappedHistorical.moment: We have found that by not seeking our own selfish desires we are able to find a life that goes beyond what we thought was possible through Narcotics Anonymous.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: Addiction is chronic, progressive and fatal. The cycle can be broken by not taking that first fix, pill, drink, or toke. Like other incurable diseases, addiction can be arrested. we agree that there is nothing shameful about being an addict provided we accept our dilemma and honestly take action.
unmappedHistorical.body:
Addiction may be chronic, progressive and fatal but there is a solution! Many of us have found if we don't pick up after our first surrender and accept our addiction for what it is we have not found it necessary to use again. How many of us lived in the shame of being an addict? We didn't understand that being an addict is not shameful. Not getting into action and refusing to be responsible for our recovery is letting our disease out of captivity.

The 12 Steps and 12 Traditions give us a way to be free from our diseased thinking. We have heard that our disease is progressive even when we are not using. What does this mean? Our disease doesn't take days off. It learns how to attack our spirits in different ways. If our disease is not arrested we will surely die. The death begins with an emotional death where we can't deal with our emotions, then it progresses to a spiritual death where we lose contact with our spirit. If this progression is not stopped soon, we will continue on the path to a mental death where the obsession to use kicks in. Normally, by this time, much has been lost. This is the last step before the beginning of our physical death. As long as we don't put the drugs in our bodies we have a chance.

We must admit that we have a disease. We must become willing to accept all that we did or have to do to get better one day at a time. We must also accept the fact that there will be times when our disease will resurface. Through prayer, sponsorship, stepwork, literature, sharing and application of the principles it always passed, if we don't put any of these into action we will revert back to our sickest behavior or use. Addiction can only be arrested when we become Honest, Open-minded, and Willing. If we overlook one of these indispensable principles, the H.O.W. of the program will not work.We have to convince ourselves daily that we need to turn our will and our life over to NA and God or our lives will become miserable again.
unmappedHistorical.moment: No longer are we trapped in the hell of obsession but rather we are freed to live life on life's terms and begin enjoying life again! We want freedom. Clean, we see that the greatest freedom we can achieve is acceptance of God's will.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “If you want to change your life--risk sharing! It is by taking risks we have almost lost our lives, by asking for help in the same way, we can change.”
unmappedHistorical.body: Distrust of others is just a symptom of the disease of addiction. We came to NA and tried to keep ourselves in control but it didn't work. We freely allow ourselves to suffer from the risks we've so blindly taken. We struggle to accept that without taking the risk of asking for help, we may never fully recover. We are blinded and unwise in our addiction. As we used drugs we constantly risked losing all our health, welfare and our very own life. It seems like we trusted in drugs and their power to help us almost until the end. Just to stay clean is not enough for the type of addicts we are. As we learn to share and care we get some chances to better life through changing our behaviour. It is only when we become willing to change that we grow. In recovery we need to become open and willing to allow others that have gone before us to show us the way. We've been told to try to share what we are going through and see what will happen. Surprisingly, The NA Fellowship didn't reject us but wanted to help. We realized that we can be vulnerable; we can ask for help, we can share our problems and achievements. We can be humans. When we share something with others we begin to admit that this thing really exists in our life. In surrender we are willing to live without pretense or defense, we ask for help when needed as living a life of honesty requires telling the truth about every little thing, our own pain, fears, and joys. For many of us these are new feelings. This is an opportunity to participate in the healing and growth we experience through the Steps. As we risk being open to others we let them be part of our lives and to become part of their life as well.
unmappedHistorical.moment: NA helps us face our fears we grow through the pain not in spite of it. We learned to face reality and live life on God's terms. We overcome them through prayer, meditation and acting differently.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “On the outside world, a lot of the rules that apply will not work with our new life in the Fellowship. Expressing our need for help at the time of crisis seems like a logical thing to do, but we are sometimes illogical.”
unmappedHistorical.body: We had some messed up rules in active addiction. Some of us thought we had a code we lived by. Many of us saw the insanity we created. Being illogical is a form of insanity we need to be rid of. Something inside us cries that people will reject us if they know how we feel or think. In coming to NA we found humility was not normally part of our code. By applying the principle of honesty we can make one clean day when it seemed impossible before. We may feel we can’t apply all of the principles but applying honesty keeps us clean for that moment. When we put some distance between ourselves and our obsessive thinking we allow the grace of a Higher Power to work in our lives. Our thinking got us here when we find ourselves with life problems we know our best option is to acknowledge them and remember that today “I am not alone”. Our NA friends accept us as we are. Though it may not feel secure to cry for help in the outside world, we know that there is one place we are welcome no matter what - and it is NA. We have a Higher Power to sort the problems out: we have a sponsor and Home Group members from whose experiences we can learn.
unmappedHistorical.moment: We will find a new way to live; asking for help is one of the ways to do it.
unmappedHistorical.note: Preserved without assigning a calendar date. The source document states its dates are historical writing dates.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “We come to understand that our recoveries are a gift from a Power greater than ourselves. There is a spirit that is guiding all living things.”
unmappedHistorical.body: We struggled with a Higher Power for a long time. It was something that we allowed ourselves to rebel against; to act out, to channel our rage against. We are reminded our best thinking got us to the rooms of NA. In active addiction we often took credit for things we didn't do. We also denied our responsibilities regarding things we did. We were led here to show us there is hope and a way to live our lives without drugs; we just have to want it and put in the work. When we come to understand that there is truly a loving caring God that is watching out for us, we can surrender and begin to recover. In the Fellowship of Narcotics Anonymous, we found a spiritual not religious program we could trust. There are so many pieces, parts and people in our recovery that we have “stumbled” on and we know that’s not by accident or a coincidence. This led us to a Higher Power and surrendered to Guidance in the 12 steps. In our first Step we are taught to surrender our egos. Redefining a Higher Power as a force that is good which has allowed us to lighten up about being guided.Pain and difficulties teach us there are no short cuts and that anything worth having requires surrender which brings out our true character and knowing who we are. We are taught humility and how to be a part of rather than a part from. If we could do this on our own, we would have. the first time that I have accepted the help of those around me and the wisdom from something larger. Recovery feels like the greatest gift that we have received. It allows us to get out of our own way. The spirituality that we have always felt now has a home within us and within a community and doesn’t require definition- it just is. The fact that we are surrounded by love from our Higher Power and you all, just is. Our Higher Power knows what is best for us. This frees us up from having to know everything; be good at everything; have all the answers.
unmappedHistorical.moment: We come to understand we can't take any credit for our gift of recovery. We learn we must rely on a Power Greater than ourselves to restore us to sanity.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “Belief is the beginning.​ It is helpful to stop at this point to review our thinking in this respect. “
unmappedHistorical.body: We were not the most trusting when we came into these rooms. Many of us came here believing only in drugs and they had now betrayed us. At times we felt like everyone and everything was against us. We didn't believe we could be like others or worthy of the blessings others already had. Now we needed to find something different to believe in. We found if we don't surrender, we can't recover. Addicts tend to want to know all the answers. It is humbling to admit we don't have all the answers and to learn to rely on a Power Greater than ourselves to guide us instead of our own sheer willpower. We tried doing things our way many times only to find our way doesn't work, willingness to accept this simple suggestion wasn’t so easy. Many of us came into NA either with resentments against God or misunderstandings we didn't know how to deal with. It may seem hard when things don't go our way. We may be angry at our HP or think that there is no God at all. We may equate God with material blessings other people have and we don't have; or we can fall into other delusions. We are blessed to have sponsors and other recovering addicts to provide guidance and direction. Often, they tell us to give ourselves a break. Conscious contact can be established and we can find God in other people. Belief grows as we get to know our fellows and see how a Higher Power has worked in their lives. The Steps provide a framework to begin to establish a relationship with a loving Higher Power. Facing reality and getting gut level honest is something many of us don't want to do. However, the Surrender necessary to actually recover from our disease requires us to get vulnerable. By opening up we get to know ourselves more and more. We peel the layers away as we bloom into a blossoming flower.
unmappedHistorical.moment: We do believe we can stay clean today. We just surrender and continue our journey.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “The ego of the addict must be busted for him to have a chance at recovery.”
unmappedHistorical.body: We come into NA thinking we have all the answers. In all reality, our thinking got us to the rooms of NA. We found until it was our choice to recover, recovery didn't happen. We often have a case of self will run riot as we come to recovery, this does not work. Busting ego is as painful as living life without drugs. We had to be beaten to a pulp and humbled inside, knowing we can't use successfully at all. Many of us found life was still super painful. At times, we saw no hope and had thoughts of killing ourselves. So, we went to a meeting or found another addict and honestly shared some stuff we had inside. While this may not have provided immediate relief, it is the action we took just for today. We hoped to feel ourselves free one day. Some of us had to feel the pain of the ego over and over again before we could understand the source of our pain. A chance for recovery? Sometimes it's hard to say what does it mean? Life without fear and pain? Our way got us here and the way out we have found is one of surrender. By getting humble we learn how to quit pissing all over today. We learn we don't have to hide from our past. We can face it and recover. We also don't have to fantasize about our future. We begin to understand that what we do today creates our future. We learn how to live in the moments. At first, we should recognize our ego, what part we played in the events, and recurring patterns only then can our ego be busted. To see that we are our problem is a huge step forward. For some of us this is the first form of honesty. It is this self-honesty that helps humble ourselves so we can grow. We learn how to face life as it happens. We come to understand our powerlessness and unmanageability is about much more than just simple drug use. Our perception of our feelings and our actions need to be changed. Without surrender recovery isn't possible. We must come to understand that if we are not the problem there is no solution.
unmappedHistorical.moment: Making a decision to allow our Higher Power work in our lives, and moving forward with the steps provides us a pathway to recovery. We just stop using for today whatever cost it takes and face the day. PS: E.G.O.= Edging God Out

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “We are granted the serenity to accept the things we cannot change, and thus lose our quickness to anger and sensitivity to criticism.”
unmappedHistorical.body: Happiness and anger were two of the most powerful emotions we tended to have in active addiction. When we don't get our way, we throw a temper tantrum and strike out at others that get in our way. It was our way of avoiding facing life. We sought answers in things that shoved others away rather than bringing them closer. In our active addiction we were self-focused and often lived our lives either as if we were victims tossed about by the waves of the world we inhabited or in a constant fight with the tides of life. Addicts tend to obsess over things we can't change, instead of focusing on what we can change. We seek to blame others for us not accepting our own personal responsibilities. After years of drug use, we hardly knew what serenity was. A definition of serenity is a state of being calm, peaceful or untroubled most of us did not come in to the rooms brimming with serenity. Being granted serenity means we have already been given it. We just have to recognize it. Serenity is a gift. It is not something we can fight for or pay for. When we have enough acceptance and courage it comes. No matter how long we stay clean problems will occur and we need to admit them. Only after that can we get to acceptance and agree with reality as it is without holding any reservations. As we ask for help and overcome our self-centeredness new possibilities arise. Once we invited our Higher Power into our lives, we found through the grace of a loving God that we have a choice to use the tools of prayer and meditation to give us the space to take a step back and not just live as a human reaction. We find ourselves able to be open to possibilities we may not see in our limited view. As we learn to live with serenity in our lives we no longer have to react to our emotions and can surrender to God and begin to change and grow in our recovery. We learned through working the steps what we could do to better achieve this state of mind. What a freedom the steps offered us! this freedom is so valuable to us. removing the obsession and compulsion from our lives gives us the strength to carry on to the next level of recovery. We do recover though and this means we learn we are responsible for not only our lives but also our recovery. We learn how to love the unlovable as many called us unlovable for years. We learn how to forgive the unforgivable because we see how others forgave us. We lose our self-centered, self-seeking ways and in the process rid ourselves of our ego. Everyone who experienced it can remember this moment. Now we have something to strive for. There is a saying Clean and Serene. It shows up that there is another part of recovery - emotional stability. Without it complete abstinence becomes a burden and we can lose everything in relapse.
unmappedHistorical.moment: In NA we learn how to build bridges rather than walls. We learn how to connect with other addicts and by doing so we learn how to

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Trusting others doesn't come naturally to us, but we must learn to trust because an addict alone is in bad company.”
unmappedHistorical.body: We came to NA not trusting ourselves; left alone our addictive personalities grew. The only thing many of us were sure of was that we had made a mess of our lives. In addiction we had developed a deep mistrust of everyone and everything, often finding ourselves acting out of desperation and fear. We had a loser's point of view that kept us always looking at the negativity of life rather than seeking solutions. This caused us to think everyone was out to get us. In NA we found there were addicts just like us that had been hurt. Our past was not filled with love and trust. It was mostly fear and obsession. For most of us trusting others isn't natural. When we came to N.A. as the result of being powerless, we started to realize that it wasn't a good idea to completely trust ourselves. Trust is a new idea for most of us. It was a hard learned experience yet as addicts we had to surrender so that we could recover. We found comfort in being alone, because that is what we were used to in the past. Being alone was dangerous; it put us in danger of slipping up and telling ourselves that “one won’t harm us”. Distrust is a bi-product of our disease, practicing Spiritual Principle's allows us to take that first step. Trust begins with faith. In recovery we surrendered and found that we must trust a Higher Power and at first, we had to find a constant that we visualized as a Higher Power that helped us with our focus. This started to make sense. It would be insane to continue all by ourselves, yet it was also scary to let people in to let them know what was going on inside of us. We needed to be surrounded by others in recovery, likeminded people, so that we can bounce ideas off of them and to get other options.... our ways don’t work anymore for us. Those addicts though learned how to let others be human beings instead of expecting perfection from everyone. We learned how to accept our responsibilities by seeing the part we have had in every situation in our lives rather than blaming others. Without trusting other addicts to help us to recover we stay alone...an addict alone is in bad company as the last addict we used with was ourselves. We found other addicts that care for us and will be there for us. We found a Sponsor that was able to guide us by sharing their Experience, Strength and Hope and how they went through similar experiences. By seeing others’ actions and care we began to learn to trust. Learning to live the spiritual principles of NA is the foundation of our recovery. Trusting others is a process we develop over time; we were untrustworthy so why would we trust others. We develop this trust as our faith grows. We lose the belief that the world was out to get us and see that trusting others is a strength, not a weakness. In N.A. we learn to rely on the guidance and experience of other members, our sponsors and a loving God. We came to find out that people are here to help us, not to judge us. With this we are well on our way to a day clean. A day clean is a day won.
unmappedHistorical.moment: By opening up we start to feel a part of each other’s lives and we don't have to live in isolation ever again. “Spirituality as a way of life for an addict seems a total contradiction. Many feel that they have found what they were searching for in drugs through spirituality.”

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “We addicts have no choice but to help one another. In helping others our own recovery is aided. We don't criticize them better we love them better.”
unmappedHistorical.body: In the beginning we might have mistakenly thought that recovery was an intellectual practice, like choice, theory, or a mindset. we thought if we studied the literature harder, contributed more to the conversation in the rooms,” fake it till we make” it that recovery would descend upon us by osmosis. We learned knowledge alone doesn't equal recovery. After all, how many of us were quick to tell others "I know" over and over again. We have to learn how to live the program of NA for us to actually recover. As addicts we are well trained in saying cool words and not living them. This is dishonest to others and ourselves, we have to practice what we preach. When we are dishonest we run the risk of relapse. Our disease is so cunning that we can feel temporary satisfaction from the attention and admiration of others in the meetings. Good deeds speak for themselves better than words. If we want to reach others with our message we have to be a living example of it. As stated in our Gray Book, “The message is meaningless unless we live it”. Gray Book Page 60 lines 1-2 As addicts, our perception of love was twisted, addiction is a love disorder. Love is contradictory to addiction. In learning how to love we practice it through actions. So why not to start with the next addict in the room? Love is an action word. It brings connection and communication while our disease is patiently waiting to separate and kill us thru isolation. We have to live our principles if we want to stay clean, happy and alive. When first coming to NA, the love and acceptance found in the rooms kept many of us coming back. It was that love that provided a basis of understanding a Loving Higher Power which was necessary for surrender, recovery and continued growth of a relationship with a loving Higher Power. We had lived so long in a life filled without love we longed for a new life. We had found it with that first hug as we learned to live this new life of recovery. We carry the message as we show empathy and caring as we greet the new comer and show the love of the Fellowship, this is the NA way of spirituality. Any addict can be struggling even if they have substantial clean time. In allowing people in the program to love us, we are able to continue to grow and blossom into the people our Higher Power created us to be. It's an ongoing process and we get to participate by giving back what was so freely given to us, the love of the program. When we look back on our own experience we have been shown nothing but love, compassion and empathy this is why we never give up anyone and keep practicing what we have been shown into our daily lives.
unmappedHistorical.moment: Recovery is a program of action. It is not an appliance that works for us-we work for it! We cannot think our way into right acting-we must act our way into right thinking.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “Belief became the most important thing for us to work on. We have some type of belief and unless we examine it and seek to improve it, it may be insufficient to give us recovery.”
unmappedHistorical.body: When we first came to Narcotics Anonymous many of us had little or no belief in a power greater than ourselves. Some of us being atheists and agnostics always wanted some proof about this God thing. Without belief we stand and face a door that will be forever closed. Closed doors will not help us to recover. Some of us had something we believed in before we got to NA. Clearly what we believed in didn't help keep us from the insanity of our using. We had sought relief in drugs our whole lives. We sought quick fixes instead of solutions that take time and surrender. Our thinking and belief system almost killed us. The only thing we, as addicts, could believe is that life was unfair. In turn, we treated others unfairly. It was a dog-eat-dog world, and we would do anything to be top dog. Treatment for our spiritual malady must be spiritual in nature, developing a relationship with a God of our understanding and asking for help is the start. From there the work is expanding that understanding and relationship and allowing it to express in our lives –faith. We found out in the Second Step that we needed to come to believe that a power greater than ourselves could restore us to sanity. We needed to examine how we used that belief in a Greater Power so that it could grow and help us through the insanity the disease of addiction creates in our lives. Many of us found that it wasn't our Greater Power that had let us down but our understanding of how our Greater Power works in our lives. Some of us had a problem with the word God when we got here. We were told that if we had a problem with the word God that it could mean Good Orderly Direction or Gift of Desperation. In Narcotics Anonymous our concept of God comes not from dogma but from what works for us. Recovery showed us a different truth. recovery showed us that we could rely on others. we could believe in good will. we could trust God and the fellowship. “Life” and “love” were Spiritual Principles, but belief is what made these things possible! Surrendering our will helps us to be able to deal with life on it's terms. It helps us to accept being human. It helps us become a part of the human race rather than running and hiding from it. We found what we had been seeking all along. A way out of the pain and misery we were creating by not accepting our own personal responsibilities.
unmappedHistorical.moment: As humans we will have opportunities for growth placed before us, these may challenge us but we have the original experience of our surrender to know that our Higher Power is taking care of us even when we cannot see.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “Just as we went to any length to get drugs, so must we go to any lengths to learn to get clean.”
unmappedHistorical.body: Addicts are no strangers to the concept of supply and demand. We are programmed to want. Wanting more was a part of our survival skills. We were willing to go to any lengths to slowly kill ourselves, even if only for a few moments of relief. Most of us have some type of story of the insanity we lived in our active addiction. Our lives were consumed with the getting and using and finding ways and means to get more. We worked very hard to get our drugs. We found we never tired of this insanity. We lived in it for so long that many of us can't believe change is possible. We tried to quit for several years. We'd heard it was possible yet were able to get drugs at all costs anyway. Now when we’re clean for a while and struggling with life issues; often suffering from instability and constant feelings of inferiority. At times recovery seems unreachable. We try and fail, try and fail. People said try one more time; in desperation we do. That's it. We would be dead without recovery so we try what people suggest, more or less. We went to any length to get drugs. Finding that same stubbornness to stay clean is important; why do we think we can recover simply by osmosis. Recovery is action; it is a way of life. Sometimes it’s just a white knuckled grip on recovery and sometimes it’s just repeating the serenity prayer. NO MATTER WHAT WE HAVE TO DO, WE CAN STAY CLEAN JUST FOR TODAY. We stay present to our commitments, continue our practice to value what happens when we wrestle with discomfort that arises rather than running away through distraction. We want to feel like we could never be tired of the gifts that recovery brings, the opportunities, the self-acceptance.
unmappedHistorical.moment: By taking suggestions we grow and each Step helps us grow more and more. The layers of insanity peel away as we recover. NA teaches us how to live a different way.
