unmappedHistorical.quote: “We come to this program from homes and apartments, offices and schools, treatment centers and jails, parks and gutters. We come from many different places, but they all share loneliness, pain, and fear. Somehow addiction draws us together in Narcotics Anonymous.”
unmappedHistorical.body: Loneliness, fear and pain of addiction were what brought us in NA. If you are an addict then you know what it is like to feel alone. You know what it is like to feel like no one else understands you. We all have felt the sorrow of being an addict. We often hear the saying in recovery: “We didn’t get here on a winning streak”. No saying has ever rung more true. We come exhausted, we come distrustful and ashamed-we come from the places we have come to fear the most. We all know the pain of living either with or without drugs. It is not the worst case at all. We are surrounded by people like us, so they can understand us. Being among recovering clean addicts kills loneliness. Anonymity brings us all together. We quit looking at the differences and start looking at our similarities We recognize the diversity of experiences in both our addiction and also our recovery. The 12 Steps provide a blueprint for the development of our personal relationship with a Higher Power which provides the way out. Our Higher Power is what keeps us connected to each other in NA. We can feel the love in the rooms of NA. We each have our own Higher Power to guide us as our spirits awaken. We put God into our lives so each of us feels connected. This acceptance enables us to feel connected. We must remember that our diversity requires us to be inclusive, which means accepting life and everyone as they are. Acceptance is a spiritual practice that sets us free from anger, resentment and judgement. What some of us get that choose to learn how to live the NA way is we find a new way to live. We find a way to be a part of rather than apart from. Where our disease once separated us from everyone and everything around us, it now brings us together in recovery. We get to experience one another's sorrows, joys and life experiences. We get to live. We still feel pain from time to time and it will be so. Applying of NA principles can ease this pain while other people are still around to support us. They share with us how they were able to make it thru fears of this yet unknown clean life. They can even spend some time with us when our fear of living is too overwhelming. The World is less scary place when we know that there is place where people are waiting for us. Excitement of new actions can replace the pain, more or less. NA is our life and our life is NA.
unmappedHistorical.moment: What a gift it is to know that no matter where we came from we have a place and that is here in Narcotics Anonymous.

unmappedHistorical.quote: Learning to live without drugs is complicated by the fact that it is so hard for many of us to accept our disease.
unmappedHistorical.body: The obsession and compulsion to use drove us to the bitter ends - jails, institutions and death. It was easy to get high and feel nothing. Our literature indicates that the people around us noticed that we were addicts way before we did, we were stuck in a state of denial. Admitting we had a disease we had to arrest was unthinkable. In turn, admitting that we had to start feeling without our numbing medication. Pain, guilt sorrow and embarrassment, were just a few of the things hard to face in admitting we had this disease. In order to live without drugs to numb our pain of the real world and live on its own terms we had to come to this conclusion. Unlike drugs which offered instant gratification, recovery through the Steps takes time, patience and faith. It can be overwhelming to discover that we are the problem, not the drugs. This is where A DAY AT A TIME can be invaluable. While it feels impossible to accept WE CAN NEVER USE AGAIN. WE CAN PRACTICE NOT USING A DAY AT A TIME. Once we accept our powerlessness, we are able to move forward in our recovery and live clean. We thought if we stopped using drugs our problems would go away. While total abstinence opens our minds so we are able to hear the message if we stop there we sell ourselves short. NA provides much more than just simple abstinence from drugs. NA provides a proven path to recovery that all of us can use if we choose to get out of the way and Surrender. Acceptance comes from freedom. The freedom we seek comes as we learn how to stay clean, listening, taking suggestions and working the Steps. We can have no freedom if We don't love ourselves. That love for ourselves comes from writing and working the Steps. Having to work for freedom does not come easy.
unmappedHistorical.moment: accepting the disease and quitting using drugs can be difficult but if we keep coming back and live one day at a time living with our disease gets easier. We find others like us that help us understand, we never have to live alone again.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “We had to keep other people from knowing about our pain. We isolated ourselves, and lived in prisons built out of our own loneliness.”
unmappedHistorical.body: Many of us felt no one understood us. We were afraid what people would think of us. Our disease makes us apart from rather than a part of. We used to hide the sorrow and pain that we felt inside rather than express ourselves openly. Our self centered nature keeps us from getting close to others. We used so we could hide our tears and sorrow rather than let people see how empty our Lives had become. We pushed life away. We tend to do this so other people think we are strong rather than letting others know our pain inside. Sometimes the loss or death of someone close and dear to our hearts helps us to recognize our need for others. Inside we are thinking to ourselves how are we going to continue to manage our lives without the help of that person. NA helps us to see we are not alone. We open up to others about our pain. Because we open up, the magic of empathy is shared. NA provides us a way to become a part of a special group of addicts that can relate to the pain we felt inside. We find the only thing we have to change is everything.
unmappedHistorical.moment: we no longer have to hide from ourselves or others, we are set free.

unmappedHistorical.quote: "One thing you can't hide, is when you're crippled inside."
unmappedHistorical.body: We covered up our depression and sadness using dope. We were reduced to mere animal levels. Some of us were great at hiding our pain until it got too much for us to bear. We reached a point where we felt our lives were being ripped apart from us. We no longer could cover up our depression and sadness. We find we can get clean inside yet we still can't hide our emotions. It is hard for us to walk our path when we laid it so fast. We can only pray we find the G.ift O.f D.esperation.
unmappedHistorical.moment: we will be grateful we have found there is hope without dope. ___ "Spirituality and sharing is the essence of our recovery."

unmappedHistorical.quote: “The situations that seem hardest to maintain our honesty have produced the most rewarding results.”
unmappedHistorical.body: Most of us didn’t have any honesty when we came into Narcotics Anonymous. In active addiction, many of us hid behind a wall of lies and wore masks to suit whatever situations we were in, in order to survive. We clung to this dishonesty as a means of making it by, and were so attached to this habit of lying, that we often found it hard to open up and get honest even after finding NA. We said we were honest, but we truly didn’t know who we were or why we did some of the things that we did. We always struggled with hard situations in our lives, things that made it hard for us not to use. Our ego doesn’t like being called out on things that make us appear less than others. Making it through these situations without using gave us a feeling of accomplishment. We eventually learned to build our honesty. Honesty is a spiritual principle that we thought that we knew all about until we were able to get humble and see the growth that we needed. Every action has an equal and opposite reaction. If we lie, the reactions and responses will be tainted and inapplicable to our true condition. We open up a little at a time to others and we find that the situations that were hardest to get honest with provided a sense of relief and bore the greatest prizes in the end. Once we experienced the freedom and tranquility that could, and did, overcome us when being honest, we began to make a habit of it. We let it grow by practicing daily. We continue this honesty through vigilance in our program and fervently practicing spiritual principles and working steps with a sponsor. Rigorous honesty yields the best results, because it provides us with the opportunities necessary to learn and grow.
unmappedHistorical.moment: By continuing to maintain honesty in the most difficult situations we come to gain freedom.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Just as we went to any length to get drugs, so must we go to any lengths to learn to get clean.”
unmappedHistorical.body: Recovery and Relapse We were willing to do things we never thought we would just to use. We were imprisoned by this all encompassing need, and were driven to go to any length to get it. We put off being responsible in our lives just to find that next fix. It seemed natural and easy for us to set everything aside and make the world stop and wait while we sought out the drugs. Everything else about life could wait and was secondary. In active addiction nothing was ever as important as getting that next fix. Why does it seem like such a struggle in the opposite way in order to stay clean? Putting everything down for the drugs seemed easy. We want to stay clean so much! Perhaps even more than we wanted the drugs… It makes no sense to us that staying clean, although we want it so badly, seems to be such a struggle forward for us. We went to great lengths to find ways and means to use. Why do we feel recovery is going to come without the same effort? It seems painful to stay clean. Such a grind! We might ask ourselves, why is that? The difficult part for some of us is finding the desire to do so and letting go of our past. We must let go of the past so we can move forward, but we must not forget about the past so we can learn and grow from it. We must get honest so we can see it wasn’t the drugs but our diseased thinking we had that kept us sick that made our lives unmanageable. If we can do this, we can finally see and experience life free from the prison we were placed in while using drugs. We hear it works if you work it. If we put half of that effort towards getting clean, we have a great chance at success. It never mattered how dangerous or impractical it seemed. Today, as we get clean and find Narcotics Anonymous, we have to go the same distances we would go in our using to free ourselves from the enslavement of our addiction.
unmappedHistorical.moment: We learn by facing our fear of asking others for help, we will recover if we put the work into it.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “We as addicts, suffer from a problem deeper than the drugs we took.”
unmappedHistorical.body: Many of us, as addicts, felt that drugs were the issues in our lives, creating all the chaos and problems. We came in and thought, if we quit using drugs our problems would go away. The drugs were only the symptom of a bigger problem. But it wasn’t until coming into the program that we realized that our problem runs far deeper than that. We have a living problem. We found that our disease has roots in every area of our lives. Our issues, in many cases, were our own selves. Through finding a sponsor and working the steps, we got to know ourselves better. We grew as we learned to mend the issues that faced us. We had to address our own broken pieces and darkness in order to fix the mess and chaos that consumed us. We learned that old habits die hard. Yet, there is our message saying that, “An addict, any addict, can stop using drugs; lose the desire to use again; and find a new way to live.” Our whole lives changed as we continue to recover. Working the steps help a us figure out what we need to work on. We start to recognize our character defects, and through constant vigilance we reassess these dark points of ourselves and use spiritual principles to guide us through.
unmappedHistorical.moment: By learning to live life on life’s terms the drugs aren’t necessary any more.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “We were freed to live and enjoy life just for today without the old ghosts of our addiction haunting us in the morning of every new day.”
unmappedHistorical.body: Why Are We Here What it feels like to wake up and have to use? In active addiction, many of us felt slaves to our use. We were haunted constantly by these lingering thoughts and feelings. That is what addicts live with until we stop using. We couldn’t stop using even when we wanted to. It was as if we carried with us the burden of being an addict every day.it isn’t until we face our past head on and come to terms with it, that we can truly be freed and move forward. Being freed from that pain as well as our other ghosts we didn’t want to face is truly something many of us never believed would change. The events of our past haunted us on a daily basis. We often used to deal with the reality of the past. We used to avoid feelings. Coming to Narcotics Anonymous we are set free from this prison in our minds. We learn that facing these ghosts helps us grow. At the start of every 24 hours, we can build our confidence, our self-esteem, and our desire to change, and our will power to carry out the message of NA. We learn we must go or grow and growing is so much better than having to live with the horrors of addiction on a daily basis once again. We work the steps in order to stay away from this dark shroud that surrounded us daily. The regular use of spiritual principles and reaching out to others are also important weapons to keep these demons away. We know we never have to use against our own will ever again.
unmappedHistorical.moment: addiction will still haunt us, but with constant vigilance, we learn how to live just for today and keep our once dark mindset at bay.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: "Our lives become so much simpler, when we get to know ourselves."
unmappedHistorical.body: Who were we before. during, and after using? Many of us find a void where self “was” or is. In recovery, we get to learn who we are, and we get to accept who we were. During active addiction, many of us hardly knew who we were, and we were uncomfortable with ourselves.By finding the rooms of Narcotics Anonymous, we slowly begin to remove the masks that we wore for so long. We come to find, through working steps with our sponsor/working the spiritual principles, who we truly are and what makes us up. By doing this, we find so many silly obstacles simply disappear or stop being problematic. By discovering the person we truly are, life just seems to simplify. Knowing ourselves, in our times that we are suffering, can lead us down the right path if we know and are aware of premeditated reservations. We stay teachable, and in turn we grow. Our lives were filled with chaos and pain before coming to NA. we had no clue how to deal with our emotions. Once we get honest with ourselves we no longer feel the need to make excuses or blame others for our actions. We get honest, and by getting honest, we begin to see out true selves.
unmappedHistorical.moment: We quit fighting. We have surrendered all our excuses so that we can recover.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “Every addict is a prisoner in their own mind, condemned to slow execution by their own sense of guilt.”
unmappedHistorical.body: We do recover Let’s face it, we did not come to Narcotics Anonymous because we were living clean. As addicts, we tried to escape the pain that seemed to trap and engulf us. We suffer from mental emotions and feelings that become a daily battle. Many of us thought that those around us or situations we faced were the cause of our pain and torment. It wasn’t until coming to NA that we came to realize it was our own selves we were trying to escape. We were killing ourselves slowly by traveling down a path that was self-seeking, self-centered, and self-obsessed. We did things we surely were not proud of. We need to be aware of our inner thoughts so we are not slowly making reservations for failure. We came to NA to find a new way of life. When we still repeat these patterns while not using, it can be confusing. We learn recovery is a 24/7 battle of surrendering our will over and over again. Through learning and practicing the spiritual principles/working the steps, we begin to slowly remove the bars and escape the dark prisons we had made for ourselves. By not only doing our best, but doing higher power’s best, we are allowed to be free from our own sense of guilt. We no longer have to suffer from the slow execution of our thoughts and are free to a new and better way of life.
unmappedHistorical.moment: It is only through continual vigilance and practice that we remain free and clean today

unmappedHistorical.quote: "Some of the most common excuses for using are loneliness, self-pity, and closed-mindedness. Past thinking patterns known as "stinkin' thinking'" have proven lethal."
unmappedHistorical.body: As addicts we looked for every excuse we could to keep living in our insanity. We were our own worst enemy, our thinking kept leading us to using, institutions, deaths, and jails. Old habits die hard... as addicts we must come to understand that every day is a battle. In war, one must know their enemy. Our enemies as recovering addicts are the patterns and defects that keep us sick. loneliness, self-pity, and closed-mindedness are some of the most common excuses for continued use. We have found that when nothing changes; Nothing changes. We always were our own victim of the disease. Our thinking led us to the action and meaning of dereliction. Our past thinking took us to our pity pot which we filled up daily with our negative thoughts. It may have taken someone to tell us to get off our pity pot for us to realize what we were doing. We searched for answers and found none, because we needed to change our whole mindset. In NA, we found addicts who thought the same way as we had, and had changed their whole perspective on life. We could not stay clean with out the the love of the fellowship, because we always felt alone. NA has helped us understand we are responsible for our recovery. We went from thinking only of our self to individuals that cared for others and are able to share that care with others. We found we couldn't finally live life in recovery until we took suggestions and changeded our closed-mindedness.
unmappedHistorical.moment: We are Grateful that NA has helped us remove all the excuses. We finally understand that if we are not the problem, we can't be part of the solution.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “After we accept that we create our own hell and that there is a God that wants to help us, we begin to make progress in solving our problems”
unmappedHistorical.body: Our way always leads to destruction. Even in our darkest of days, there is still a loving and caring God that wants to help guide us. The question is: “What level of hell are you on?” We asked ourselves, “how did we get here?” As addicts, we made reasons for our lives as we walked through hell. In active addiction, we were stuck in a cage of misery; blaming everyone and everything for our pain but ourselves. In our minds, it couldn’t possibly be us that is the problem causing all this horror to ourselves. We had to come to the reality that we were the problem and our own undoing. We, as addicts, have the uncanny ability to get ourselves into things that we cannot get out of alone. We find that we are our own captors, imprisoning ourselves and being our own judge, jury, and executioner. We created our own hell but our higher power helped us progress in our lives. God, as defined by the program, is nothing more and nothing less than the ability to make the impossible possible. The only way for us to live rightly is by surrendering and trusting that God has a plan for us. It was the light from god as we understood him showing us that there is a way out. No one else is responsible we learn. Problem solving starts with a change of pwerspecative. We learn the excused must go if we want to grow. By working the steps, we find we finally are able to release ourselves from the grim fate we once faced. We then come to realize there is a power greater than ourstlves that we can learn to reach out to for help guiding us.
unmappedHistorical.moment: We are Grateful that we now understand that if we aren’t the problem there is no solution.
unmappedHistorical.note: Preserved without assigning a calendar date. The source document states its dates are historical writing dates.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “Recovery as found in Narcotics Anonymous must come from within and no one can get clean for anyone else.”
unmappedHistorical.body: How many people saw us suffering and wanted to help us. In active addiction, we were our own undoing. We were the ones that kept ourselves sick no one else made us. It didn’t matter how much others wanted us to change until we wanted to change ourselves. We decide how much we choose to suffer. Some of us came for family and stayed to get clean for ourselves. We have found that recovery is a personal choice the same as admitting being an addict had to come from the addict themselves. We are only responsible for ourselves. Our willingness to change our lives and live clean becomes a new strength. In our recovery we are responsible for working the program, practicing spiritual principles, and setting ourselves free from the prisons of our own making. Where before we felt worthless, we learned in the process of the steps our own importance. One of the greatest aspects of being in recovery is feeling a sense of belonging. Being empowered with that new way of life we find the fellowship of Narcotics Anonymous. When it comes to recovery, we must look within where our true problem lies, because without looking within, we are just getting clean for others. Recovery is what you make it, and you get out of it what you put into it. We learned that we had created most of our problems by our actions. We get to have freedom today. Today, with our personal freedom, we realize we have goodness and this goodness has to be given away in order to keep it. Through helping each other we find self-worth. Seeing each other get clean gives hope. Finding a new way of life is something we can share with others freely and joyously.
unmappedHistorical.moment: We must get clean for ourselves or we will surely die.
unmappedHistorical.note: Preserved without assigning a calendar date. The source document states its dates are historical writing dates.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “Trusting others doesn’t come naturally to us, but we must learn to trust because an addict alone is in bad company.”
unmappedHistorical.body: In active addiction many of us had a sense of distrust of anyone but ourselves. We were alone in this world and felt abandoned by everyone. We had a hard time trusting others as we lived on a survival instinct. Attempting to cope, many of us sought to withdraw and isolate with some of our fellow peers. Being alone only gives us more time to be in our own heads. It brings us to dwell on the shit that has happened or hasn’t happened. We were spiritually and emotionally void, numb. We went on living one day at a time, not knowing how to deal with problems as they arose. We felt that no one could understand us the isolation started to drive a rift between us and the ones we loved. It gave us all this doubt not knowing who we can really depend on. It just seemed that we took one step forward and two steps back. Can we ever trust anyone? The people we have trusted have only let us down, lied to us, stolen from us and abused us. After coming to Narcotics Anonymous, we found that trust was a core principle in the program. With new surroundings, trust will develop slowly but surely. We get a chance to build solid relationships based on trust. We had to find other people in Narcotics Anonymous that we could trust to share our struggles within everyday life. We realize that not everyone is in the same place in their recovery, and some are sicker than others. We finally found a sounding board to help us in our difficult times and help us make good spiritual decisions. By working steps with our sponsor and continuing to practice spiritual principles, we develop this trust in another, so we no longer rely solely on ourselves.
unmappedHistorical.moment: Used, abused, and finally broken, we sought help as our once need for emotional support was met with the full-blown reality of active addiction. Now in recovery, we know: “an addict alone is in bad company.”

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “Responsibility is a key word here.”
unmappedHistorical.body: When we came into the rooms, many of us had the tendency of facing life on our own terms. In recovery we are faced with real life problems and situations. We have responsibilities to finish our step work. The weight, at times, can weigh us down so much that we feel like flipping out. Many times, it depends on how we handle the situations as they arise in our daily lives. We cannot count the number of times that we had to take responsibility for owning how selfish, hurtful, and manipulative we were. The people, places, and things that we have been through have made it possible to take responsibility and foster ownership in our daily lives. Life on life’s terms has a lot to do with one spiritual principle in particular… Responsibility. Responsibility is a big part of whether we get well or stay sick. Responsibility has to be the forefront of our mind. Responsibility is a term many newcomers run from. How can we truly be free when we have commitments? Being free cant mean submitting our wills can it? It can… In Narcotics Anonymous we learn how to be respectful, responsible, and productive members of society. When we are responsible, our responsibilities include: recovery, steps, meetings, calling our sponsors, helping the newcomers, service works, and most of all our higher powers. There are so many responsibilities in our lives. We get bills, savings, cars, gas, etc. All these things coincide with our daily program.
unmappedHistorical.moment: Start taking responsibility … Stop avoiding accountability… Stop dying and start living. God help us!

unmappedHistorical.quote: Spiritual Vigilance is required to apply our Twelve Traditions and to bring up at times the ties which bind us together.
unmappedHistorical.body: How do we stick together if we don’t talk about the things that protect us from ourselves. For years we hid behind the masks which we utilized to hide fears, feelings, and the unknown. All we knew was pain, chaos, and instability. Relationships where foreign and the few we managed to scrape together where built upon our own selfish desires. We learn to respect each other through getting out of our self-centered, egotistical ways. As addicts we are master manipulators. Even some of us with multiple years clean have the ability too skillfully rationalize and use strong personalities to detour individuals from their own voice. We must stay vigilant to stick to our principles and keep our opinions out of service. The ties that bind us are stronger when we are honest and loving with each other. Anonymity teaches us to respect each other and every addict is equal and valuable. Our members continue to grow as we talk about our traditions and get to understand how they work through experience. We must be persistent in demonstrating unity. After all personal recovery depends on our unity. “Our program could not encompass so many types of addicts from differing backgrounds if not for the spiritual nature of our groups” (Gray Book p157). Our traditions protect that spiritual nature.
unmappedHistorical.moment: We learn to use the spiritual nature of our Traditions to love ourselves and others.
unmappedHistorical.note: Preserved without assigning a calendar date. The source document states its dates are historical writing dates.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “As practicing addicts, our will and our lives we’re controlled by drugs.”
unmappedHistorical.body: We may not have seen it at the time, but, for most of us, using consumed our whole being. In active use, we were only concerned with one thing. The getting, using, and finding ways and means to get more. We used to survive. We lived to use and used to live. We woke up, used, and did all we could to continue using. No matter how much we used, we could never fill the hunger we had for drugs. It was all we knew. Eventually, we just wanted some temporary relief from our inability to live life on life’s terms. What was our real struggle? The real struggle was admitting that we are powerless over our addiction. Unlike our problem with drugs controlling our lives, powerlessness is something we face daily. We had to stop using drugs and start using the steps of the program in order to recover. A daily first step helps us achieve what we thought was impossible. We learn how to live without drugs.
unmappedHistorical.moment: In active use, we couldn’t imagine going one second without being loaded. In recovery, we have found more than we could ever imagine.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “We come to understand that our recoveries are a gift from a Power greater than ourselves. There is a spirit that is guiding all living things.”
unmappedHistorical.body: We struggled with a Higher Power for a long time. It was something that we allowed ourselves to rebel against; to act out, to channel our rage against. We are reminded our best thinking got us to the rooms of NA. In active addiction we often took credit for things we didn't do. We also denied our responsibilities regarding things we did. We were led here to show us there is hope and a way to live our lives without drugs; we just have to want it and put in the work. When we come to understand that there is truly a loving caring God that is watching out for us, we can surrender and begin to recover. In the Fellowship of Narcotics Anonymous, we found a spiritual not religious program we could trust. There are so many pieces, parts and people in our recovery that we have “stumbled” on and we know that’s not by accident or a coincidence. This led us to a Higher Power and surrendered to Guidance in the 12 steps. In our first Step we are taught to surrender our egos. Redefining a Higher Power as a force that is good which has allowed us to lighten up about being guided. Pain and difficulties teach us there are no short cuts and that anything worth having requires surrender which brings out our true character and knowing who we are. We are taught humility and how to be a part of rather than a part from. If we could do this on our own, we would have. the first time that I have accepted the help of those around me and the wisdom from something larger. Recovery feels like the greatest gift that we have received. It allows us to get out of our own way. The spirituality that we have always felt now has a home within us and within a community and doesn’t require definition- it just is. The fact that we are surrounded by love from our Higher Power and you all, just is. Our Higher Power knows what is best for us. This frees us up from having to know everything; be good at everything; have all the answers.
unmappedHistorical.moment: We come to understand we can't take any credit for our gift of recovery. We learn we must rely on a Power Greater than ourselves to restore us to sanity.
unmappedHistorical.note: Preserved without assigning a calendar date. The source document states its dates are historical writing dates.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: Quality and not quantity is the most important aspect of abstinence. Emotional sobriety in reality is our goal, not mere physical abstinence.
unmappedHistorical.body: When we first came to the rooms, many of us felt like we didn't have skin at all we were overly sensitive. Was it good in the beginning to finally be clean in comparison to what felt like a life in hell? What felt like an unending road that always led to the same pain and misery. When it is pain it is soooo extremely painful. When it is joy it is sooooo incredibly joyful. Addiction is a 4-sided disease: physical, mental, spiritual and emotional. It means we've got sickness of feelings as well. Our emotions can be distorted by the addictive perception of reality. We are sensitive people, and we should learn how to deal with that if we want to stay clean and recover. When we first came around, stringing together any clean time was a miracle as we began the process of the steps we found that recovery encompassed more than just not using. With the guidance of our sponsors we approached the steps as a pathway of recovery. As time goes on, as we work the Steps and develop relationships with our Higher Power, our "skin" grows. Over time how it feels to have gained even more than "simply" being clean? The "gifts" that come with time in recovery: family, true friendship, respect both self and from others, and not looking over our shoulders all the time... Quality can be hard to compare over time. We will still find ourselves in ups and downs but now we've got friends to help us - recovering addicts in NA. We pray, we share, we care, we change our behavior and we turn all of our lives to the care of our Higher Power. This is not a one-time deal; we make it daily.
unmappedHistorical.moment: We can emotionally grow and mature thru abstinence and applying principles in our lives. This ongoing process that happens just for today.
unmappedHistorical.note: Preserved without assigning a calendar date. The source document states its dates are historical writing dates.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “The ego of the addict must be busted for him to have a chance at recovery.”
unmappedHistorical.body: We come into NA thinking we have all the answers. In all reality, our thinking got us to the rooms of NA. We found until it was our choice to recover, recovery didn't happen. We often have a case of self will run riot as we come to recovery, this does not work. Busting ego is as painful as living life without drugs. We had to be beaten to a pulp and humbled inside, knowing we can't use successfully at all. Many of us found life was still super painful. At times, we saw no hope and had thoughts of killing ourselves. So, we went to a meeting or found another addict and honestly shared some stuff we had inside. While this may not have provided immediate relief, it is the action we took just for today. We hoped to feel ourselves free one day. Some of us had to feel the pain of the ego over and over again before we could understand the source of our pain. A chance for recovery? Sometimes it's hard to say what does it mean? Life without fear and pain? Our way got us here and the way out we have found is one of surrender. By getting humble we learn how to quit pissing all over today. We learn we don't have to hide from our past. We can face it and recover. We also don't have to fantasize about our future. We begin to understand that what we do today creates our future. We learn how to live in the moments. At first, we should recognize our ego, what part we played in the events, and recurring patterns only then can our ego be busted. To see that we are our problem is a huge step forward. For some of us this is the first form of honesty. It is this self-honesty that helps humble ourselves so we can grow. We learn how to face life as it happens. We come to understand our powerlessness and unmanageability is about much more than just simple drug use. Our perception of our feelings and our actions need to be changed. Without surrender recovery isn't possible. We must come to understand that if we are not the problem there is no solution.
unmappedHistorical.moment: Making a decision to allow our Higher Power work in our lives, and moving forward with the steps provides us a pathway to recovery. We just stop using for today whatever cost it takes and face the day. PS: E.G.O.= Edging God Out
unmappedHistorical.note: Preserved without assigning a calendar date. The source document states its dates are historical writing dates.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: We are granted the serenity to accept the things we cannot change, and thus lose our quickness to anger and sensitivity to criticism.
unmappedHistorical.body: Happiness and anger were two of the most powerful emotions we tended to have in active addiction. When we don't get our way, we throw a temper tantrum and strike out at others that get in our way. It was our way of avoiding facing life. We sought answers in things that shoved others away rather than bringing them closer. In our active addiction we were self-focused and often lived our lives either as if we were victims tossed about by the waves of the world we inhabited or in a constant fight with the tides of life. Addicts tend to obsess over things we can't change, instead of focusing on what we can change. We seek to blame others for us not accepting our own personal responsibilities. After years of drug use, we hardly knew what serenity was. A definition of serenity is a state of being calm, peaceful or untroubled most of us did not come in to the rooms brimming with serenity. Being granted serenity means we have already been given it. We just have to recognize it. Serenity is a gift. It is not something we can fight for or pay for. When we have enough acceptance and courage it comes. No matter how long we stay clean problems will occur and we need to admit them. Only after that can we get to acceptance and agree with reality as it is without holding any reservations. As we ask for help and overcome our self-centeredness new possibilities arise. Once we invited our Higher Power into our lives, we found through the grace of a loving God that we have a choice to use the tools of prayer and meditation to give us the space to take a step back and not just live as a human reaction. We find ourselves able to be open to possibilities we may not see in our limited view. As we learn to live with serenity in our lives we no longer have to react to our emotions and can surrender to God and begin to change and grow in our recovery. We learned through working the steps what we could do to better achieve this state of mind. What a freedom the steps offered us! this freedom is so valuable to us. removing the obsession and compulsion from our lives gives us the strength to carry on to the next level of recovery. We do recover though and this means we learn we are responsible for not only our lives but also our recovery. We learn how to love the unlovable as many called us unlovable for years. We learn how to forgive the unforgivable because we see how others forgave us. We lose our self-centered, self-seeking ways and in the process rid ourselves of our ego. Everyone who experienced it can remember this moment. Now we have something to strive for. There is a saying Clean and Serene. It shows up that there is another part of recovery - emotional stability. Without it complete abstinence becomes a burden and we can lose everything in relapse
unmappedHistorical.moment: In NA we learn how to build bridges rather than walls. We learn how to connect with other addicts and by doing so we learn how to connect with the human race. We no longer need to terrorize everyone else because of fear of getting close to others.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: “Trusting others doesn't come naturally to us, but we must learn to trust because an addict alone is in bad company.”
unmappedHistorical.body: We came to NA not trusting ourselves; left alone our addictive personalities grew. The only thing many of us were sure of was that we had made a mess of our lives. In addiction we had developed a deep mistrust of everyone and everything, often finding ourselves acting out of desperation and fear. We had a loser's point of view that kept us always looking at the negativity of life rather than seeking solutions. This caused us to think everyone was out to get us. In NA we found there were addicts just like us that had been hurt. Our past was not filled with love and trust. It was mostly fear and obsession. For most of us trusting others isn't natural. When we came to N.A. as the result of being powerless, we started to realize that it wasn't a good idea to completely trust ourselves. Trust is a new idea for most of us. It was a hard learned experience yet as addicts we had to surrender so that we could recover. We found comfort in being alone, because that is what we were used to in the past. Being alone was dangerous, it put us in danger of slipping up and telling ourselves that “one won’t harm us”. Distrust is a bi-product of our disease, practicing Spiritual Principle's allows us to take that first step. Trust begins with faith. In recovery we surrendered and found that we must trust a Higher Power and at first, we had to find a constant that we visualized as a Higher Power that helped us with our focus. This started to make sense. It would be insane to continue all by ourselves, yet it was also scary to let people in to let them know what was going on inside of us. We needed to be surrounded by others in recovery, likeminded people, so that we can bounce ideas off of them and to get other options.... our ways don’t work anymore for us. Those addicts though learned how to let others be human beings instead of expecting perfection from everyone. We learned how to accept our responsibilities by seeing the part we have had in every situation in our lives rather than blaming others. Without trusting other addicts to help us to recover we stay alone...an addict alone is in bad company as the last addict we used with was ourselves. We found other addicts that care for us and will be there for us.We found a Sponsor that was able to guide us by sharing their Experience, Strength and Hope and how they went through similar experiences. By seeing others’ actions and care we began to learn to trust. Learning to live the spiritual principles of NA is the foundation of our recovery. Trusting others is a process we develop over time; we were untrustworthy so why would we trust others. We develop this trust as our faith grows. We lose the belief that the world was out to get us and see that trusting others is a strength, not a weakness. In N.A. we learn to rely on the guidance and experience of other members, our sponsors and a loving God. We came to find out that people are here to help us, not to judge us. With this we are well on our way to a day clean. A day clean is a day won.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Spirituality as a way of life for an addict seems a total contradiction. Many feel that they have found what they were searching for in drugs through spirituality.”
unmappedHistorical.body:
After years of destruction of ourselves and others, we were in great need of something that could help us to deal with life. When we first come to Narcotics Anonymous, there may be many things that seem foreign or uncomfortable. Many of us came here with our spirit broken. It seems like we had a huge void inside and desperately tried to fill it with drugs. Although it worked for a while, finally we found ourselves completely exhausted and helpless. Our body is allergic to drugs. Our mind can be driven by the obsession to use.

Our new NA friends offered us a solution to our problem, it was: (Gray Book Page IV last paragraph) “Based on our collective experience, we believe that every addict, including the ''potential" addict, suffers from an incurable disease of body, mind and spirit. We were in the grip of a hopeless dilemma. The solution of which is spiritual in nature. Therefore, this book will deal in great part with spiritual matters.”

When we first came to NA, we may not have been very trusting. After a time, we saw positive results in other lives which they attributed to living the Twelve Steps. We came to believe the answer to our problems was spiritual in its nature. Many of us had a very complicated relationship with “God”, and could not reconcile that with a loving entity as was suggested by our sponsors and home group. Spirituality doesn’t imply a particular religion or theology it simply means there is a power greater than ourselves. Understanding this allowed us to believe that there is every reason to hope.

Addiction is a disease of body, mind and spirit when we have all three in line, recovery can then take place; if one of these ingredients is missing, our recovery will suffer. When we started to practice a new way of life, we began to see results. When we apply spiritual principles in our daily lives it helps us to deal with many aspects of our disease such as self-centeredness, manipulation and false pride.
unmappedHistorical.moment: Being spiritual isn’t limited to only prayer and meditation. We have to practice spirituality in our daily lives to experience growth and recovery.
unmappedHistorical.note: Preserved without assigning a calendar date. The source document states its dates are historical writing dates.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: We addicts have no choice but to help one another. In helping others our own recovery is aided. We don't criticize them better we love them better.
unmappedHistorical.body: In the beginning we might have mistakenly thought that recovery was an intellectual practice, like choice, theory, or a mindset. we thought if we studied the literature harder, contributed more to the conversation in the rooms,” fake it till we make” it that recovery would descend upon us by osmosis. We learned knowledge alone doesn't equal recovery. After all, how many of us were quick to tell others "I know" over and over again. We have to learn how to live the program of NA for us to actually recover. As addicts we are well trained in saying cool words and not living them. This is dishonest to others and ourselves, we have to practice what we preach. When we are dishonest we run the risk of relapse. Our disease is so cunning that we can feel temporary satisfaction from the attention and admiration of others in the meetings. Good deeds speak for themselves better than words. If we want to reach others with our message we have to be a living example of it. As stated in our Gray Book, “The message is meaningless unless we live it”. Gray Book Page 60 lines 1-2 As addicts, our perception of love was twisted, addiction is a love disorder. Love is contradictory to addiction. In learning how to love we practice it through actions. So why not to start with the next addict in the room? Love is an action word. It brings connection and communication while our disease is patiently waiting to separate and kill us thru isolation. We have to live our principles if we want to stay clean, happy and alive. When first coming to NA, the love and acceptance found in the rooms kept many of us coming back. It was that love that provided a basis of understanding a Loving Higher Power which was necessary for surrender, recovery and continued growth of a relationship with a loving Higher Power. We had lived so long in a life filled without love we longed for a new life. We had found it with that first hug as we learned to live this new life of recovery. We carry the message as we show empathy and caring as we greet the new comer and show the love of the Fellowship, this is the NA way of spirituality. Any addict can be struggling even if they have substantial clean time. In allowing people in the program to love us, we are able to continue to grow and blossom into the people our Higher Power created us to be. It's an ongoing process and we get to participate by giving back what was so freely given to us, the love of the program. When we look back on our own experience we have been shown nothing but love, compassion and empathy this is why we never give up anyone and keep practicing what we have been shown into our daily lives.
unmappedHistorical.moment: Recovery is a program of action. It is not an appliance that works for us-we work for it! We cannot think our way into right acting-we must act our way into right thinking.

unmappedHistorical.quote: Belief became the most important thing for us to work on. We have some type of belief and unless we examine it and seek to improve it, it may be insufficient to give us recovery.
unmappedHistorical.body: When we first came to Narcotics Anonymous many of us had little or no belief in a power greater than ourselves. Some of us being atheists and agnostics always wanted some proof about this God thing. Without belief we stand and face a door that will be forever closed. Closed doors will not help us to recover. Some of us had something we believed in before we got to NA. Clearly what we believed in didn't help keep us from the insanity of our using. We had sought relief in drugs our whole lives. We sought quick fixes instead of solutions that take time and surrender. Our thinking and belief system almost killed us. The only thing we, as addicts, could believe is that life was unfair. In turn, we treated others unfairly. It was a dog-eat-dog world, and we would do anything to be top dog. Treatment for our spiritual malady must be spiritual in nature, developing a relationship with a God of our understanding and asking for help is the start. From there the work is expanding that understanding and relationship and allowing it to express in our lives –faith. We found out in the Second Step that we needed to come to believe that a power greater than ourselves could restore us to sanity. We needed to examine how we used that belief in a Greater Power so that it could grow and help us through the insanity the disease of addiction creates in our lives. Many of us found that it wasn't our Greater Power that had let us down but our understanding of how our Greater Power works in our lives. Some of us had a problem with the word God when we got here. We were told that if we had a problem with the word God that it could mean Good Orderly Direction or Gift of Desperation. In Narcotics Anonymous our concept of God comes not from dogma but from what works for us. Recovery showed us a different truth. recovery showed us that we could rely on others. we could believe in good will. we could trust God and the fellowship. “Life” and “love” were Spiritual Principles, but belief is what made these things possible! Surrendering our will helps us to be able to deal with life on it's terms. It helps us to accept being human. It helps us become a part of the human race rather than running and hiding from it. We found what we had been seeking all along. A way out of the pain and misery we were creating by not accepting our own personal responsibilities.
unmappedHistorical.moment: As humans we will have opportunities for growth placed before us, these may challenge us but we have the original experience of our

unmappedHistorical.quote: surrender to know that our Higher Power is taking care of us even when we cannot see. Honesty, open-mindedness, and willingness to try, work hand in hand. The lack of one of these principles in our programs can kill us. Living a personal program without these principles, will make recovery difficult and painful for us when it should be beautifully simple.
unmappedHistorical.body: Many of us came into NA having no clue how to be honest with ourselves, let alone anyone else. We were stuck in the lie of denial regarding our disease and the part it plays in our lives. Our best ideas got us here, many of us searched for solutions outside of ourselves only to end up back where we started or worse. This just added to our mistrust and fear. Trying to get clean without Honesty, Open mindedness and Willingness to try is like trying to climb a ladder with missing rungs. The first thing we are to do when we get to Narcotics Anonymous is to get clean. This is a program of complete abstinence from any mind-changing or mood-altering substance. Lack of honesty in this area can kill us. To be dishonest seems like a natural habit for every addict. We wanted to control and manipulate in order to fill the spiritual void. We were so self-centered that we couldn't see past our own reflections. This kept us sick and stuck in denial. We separated ourselves from the rest of humanity, we found ourselves in jails, institutions and loneliness. This lack of honesty kept us from experiencing true open mindedness where we could listen and hear others and be open to a Greater Power. We need to be open-minded to this new way of life and willing to do whatever is necessary to get clean, stay clean and recover. Thankfully our first Step helps us break through the wall of denial to a place where we could quit making excuses for everything in our lives. We were directed to the tools of the steps to find this solution. When we surrendered, we found the faith to follow simple direction. This required honesty with ourselves, which was necessary before we could be honest with others. Then we were able to consider being open to a loving Higher Power and then take the steps in front of us. After getting suggestions, we had to learn to be willing to try something different than what we were used to. This willingness to try helped us grow as we carried out the actions others suggested to us to help us recover. We could finally see the truth for what it was and it set us free. In NA we were met by those who shared similar experiences who said they had a way out, and their lives demonstrated this to be true. This new way of life is free; the only payment is to get rid of our old ways of living. We must be willing enough to try it. When we get some results, we are able to say it works in our lives. Sometimes our close-mindedness returns and we are unwilling to try new ways or change anything. This is the time to pray, call our sponsor and share.
unmappedHistorical.moment: Honesty, Open-mindedness and Willingness to try are the HOW of the program. We found that without living the H.O.W. of the program, recovery is impossible. These spiritual principles are indispensable when it comes to recovering from the disease of addiction. These principles are the foundation of our recovery and must be lived daily to succeed.

unmappedHistorical.quote: “We begin by simply admitting to the possibility of a power greater than ourselves. From the very beginning, we discover that power in our lives, and that Power lives in the Fellowship.”
unmappedHistorical.body: As addicts we came into the program running on and running from self-will. Up until entering Narcotics Anonymous we were our own advocates, self-righteous, self-reliant but most of all scared. it is very common for us in active addiction to be fearful when trusting others, especially a Power Greater Than Ourselves. It seemed for so long we’ve had to rely on ourselves predominantly in the area of the using and needing to get more. We can come to an understanding that there is a power greater than us and we don't have to understand everything, because we are not God. This simple admission of a power greater than ourselves can be very difficult for some of us. There is a difference in belief vs coming to believe; believing is a choice, coming to believe is when we discover reality allows us nothing else. We have many different views when we first come to NA. Some were raised with a God that was vengeful and punishing and they had resentments against that idea. Others had a belief in a god that was limited and judgmental. Some addicts had a relationship with a God of their own understanding, but were missing knowing how to apply the spiritual principles of our program. Seeing the reality of a loving God working in the lives of those met in NA and we came to believe this Higher Power could work for us too. This helped some of us with the belief that the Narcotics Anonymous program can accommodate our atheism in our leap of faith. No matter what we thought when we came to NA we eventually learned how to surrender. Part of this surrender is understanding we don't have all the answers. Wow what is old becomes new. In Step one we admitted we were powerless over our addiction and our lives BECAME unmanageable. Once we surrender that is when the magic happens. How could this be? “It cannot be me, myself, and I”. We can write our own conception of a Higher Power; however, it doesn't mean that God will always fit our requirements. We have to learn about Higher Power thru our own experience. We can choose Spiritual Principles as a form of our Higher Power. We are to test it in our own lives and see if it really works. And it works - it really does. So, we place our understanding of Higher Power on the solid ground of our own experience and not others. When we practice honesty, we see how it changes us inside - this is the work of loving Higher Power. We practice open-mindedness by listening carefully to members at meetings and openly sharing where we are at. And it works - we learn something new, both about the world and ourselves. Eventually, when practicing willingness to try - it is sort of like the tie that binds it all together. We allow a Higher Power take care of us - because it can be better for us to act, not to overthink everything. We recognize the possibility of a Higher Power in our recovery, many found it in the group for the most part. The fact that others can recover using the tools of the program gives us hope. Hope is found in the second step. That hope goes into our prayers and communication with our Higher Power. Our Higher Power gives us grace to live life as a human, making mistakes. Recovery shows the evidence of obsession taken away through our Higher Power. We read literature, we visit various groups and ask members of these groups what works for them. We pray every day that we are doing the right thing and try to have faith in our higher power that we will be ok.
unmappedHistorical.moment: Each of us develops ideas over time by seeing how this power greater than ourselves helps us deal with life on God's term's rather than on our own. The

unmappedHistorical.quote: Just as we went to any length to get drugs, so must we go to any lengths to learn to get clean.
unmappedHistorical.body: Addicts are no strangers to the concept of supply and demand. We are programmed to want. Wanting more was a part of our survival skills. We were willing to go to any lengths to slowly kill ourselves, even if only for a few moments of relief. Most of us have some type of story of the insanity we lived in our active addiction. Our lives were consumed with the getting and using and finding ways and means to get more. We worked very hard to get our drugs. We found we never tired of this insanity. We lived in it for so long that many of us can't believe change is possible. We tried to quit for several years. We'd heard it was possible yet were able to get drugs at all costs anyway. Now when we’re clean for a while and struggling with life issues; often suffering from instability and constant feelings of inferiority. At times recovery seems unreachable. We try and fail, try and fail. People said try one more time; in desperation we do. That's it. We would be dead without recovery so we try what people suggest, more or less. We went to any length to get drugs. Finding that same stubbornness to stay clean is important; why do we think we can recover simply by osmosis. Recovery is action; it is a way of life. Sometimes it’s just a white knuckled grip on recovery and sometimes it’s just repeating the serenity prayer. NO MATTER WHAT WE HAVE TO DO, WE CAN STAY CLEAN JUST FOR TODAY. We stay present to our commitments, continue our practice to value what happens when we wrestle with discomfort that arises rather than running away through distraction. We want to feel like we could never be tired of the gifts that recovery brings, the opportunities, the self-acceptance.
unmappedHistorical.moment: By taking suggestions we grow and each Step helps us grow more and more. The layers of insanity peel away as we recover. NA teaches us how to live a different way.

unmappedHistorical.label: Grateful Wake Up Group - calendar placement not confidently resolved
unmappedHistorical.quote: "We seek solutions rather than dilemmas. Productive means being clean, creative and loving today."​
unmappedHistorical.body: As addicts we are experts in destruction. Many of us were so used to living in the dramatic world we created and felt uncomfortable when considering a lifetime of peace and contentment. Some of us buried our heads in the sand, like an ostrich, when it came to the problems we had. We acted as if our problems would solve themselves. Drama in our lives served many purposes. Some seek affection through sympathy to avoid feeling, use upset to cause excitement and distraction from our issues. In active addiction we were surrounded by dilemmas. It was front page news to everyone else except us. We were running on 100 forms of fear, we were the victim and the search party. We destroyed our bodies on a daily basis when putting drugs in. Being liars, thieves and schemers, we put ourselves in a viscous cycle, creating destructive patterns. Our spirits were destroyed and broken by our self-centered disease. Chaos ruled the days before we found NA program that helped us get out of the chaos. It seemed like all we knew was how to destroy our lives one use at a time. It was much easier and instantly gratifying to seek dilemmas rather than solutions, but this tends to make our lives unmanageable. Being a productive member of society doesn't require us to work a typical 9-5 shift, live in a fancy home, drive a new car, etc. Being productive means putting our recovery first, living a life we feel is worth living, and living for today on life's terms. It is so easy to get caught up in the materialistic, comparing, and control-focused mindset, but to live a productive life means to focus on seeking solutions for our dilemmas as they arise and from there become a more productive member of society. In NA, we found a way out of the insanity inside our heads. We can choose to not take part in this, instead relying on our Higher Power creating a space within ourselves to connect in the stillness and know They will meet our needs. In this way, we can become an asset and lead a more balanced life. The solutions we seek are sometimes difficult to see at first. We go through the Grey Book looking for answers to our questions and find that prayer and meditation may be our biggest source of solutions. These solutions are the key to getting and staying clean. We started to understand that we don't recover overnight so we needed to give ourselves a break and "take it easy". We learned that being productive meant we went from one task to the next just like we lived clean from one moment to the next. NA provides us an opportunity to become productive members of society. We start to do so surrendering all mind-changing chemicals and then maintain total abstinence on a daily basis. We can join a Home Group and practice creative freedom of NA in carrying our message. Part of our message is love and care. Care is a form of love, love-based actions. Sharing is caring. There are so many ways to do it we just have to surrender to the program moment by moment and life will have a new meaning.
unmappedHistorical.moment: We found creative solutions to the problems that once troubled us so much. We also learned how to love ourselves, and how to love others. What a gift it is to be able to live happy, joyous, free, and clean today!

unmappedHistorical.quote: “We come to this program from homes and apartments, offices and schools, treatment centers and jails, parks and gutters. We come from many different places, but they all share loneliness, pain, and fear. Somehow addiction draws us together in Narcotics Anonymous.”
unmappedHistorical.body: Loneliness, fear and pain of addiction were what brought us in NA. If you are an addict then you know what it is like to feel alone. You know what it is like to feel like no one else understands you. We all have felt the sorrow of being an addict. We often hear the saying in recovery: “We didn’t get here on a winning streak”. No saying has ever rung more true. We come exhausted, we come distrustful and ashamed-we come from the places we have come to fear the most. We all know the pain of living either with or without drugs. It is not the worst case at all. We are surrounded by people like us, so they can understand us. Being among recovering clean addicts kills loneliness. Anonymity brings us all together. We quit looking at the differences and start looking at our similarities We recognize the diversity of experiences in both our addiction and also our recovery. The 12 Steps provide a blueprint for the development of our personal relationship with a Higher Power which provides the way out. Our Higher Power is what keeps us connected to each other in NA. We can feel the love in the rooms of NA. We each have our own Higher Power to guide us as our spirits awaken. We put God into our lives so each of us feels connected. This acceptance enables us to feel connected. We must remember that our diversity requires us to be inclusive, which means accepting life and everyone as they are. Acceptance is a spiritual practice that sets us free from anger, resentment and judgement. What some of us get that choose to learn how to live the NA way is we find a new way to live. We find a way to be a part of rather than apart from. Where our disease once separated us from everyone and everything around us, it now brings us together in recovery. We get to experience one another's sorrows, joys and life experiences. We get to live. We still feel pain from time to time and it will be so. Applying of NA principles can ease this pain while other people are still around to support us. They share with us how they were able to make it thru fears of this yet unknown clean life. They can even spend some time with us when our fear of living is too overwhelming. The World is less scary place when we know that there is place where people are waiting for us. Excitement of new actions can replace the pain, more or less. NA is our life and our life is NA.
unmappedHistorical.moment: What a gift it is to know that no matter where we came from we have a place and that is here in Narcotics Anonymous.

unmappedHistorical.quote: "Obviously, our way did not work. In utter desperation, we looked for another way."
unmappedHistorical.body:
When we come into the rooms we are stuck in old patterns. The disease of addiction is one that lies to us over and over. Most of us came into the rooms helpless and lost. We had no idea how to live. Many of us learned the true feeling of desperation before we came to NA. Some of us cried realizing we had to use no matter if we wanted to quit. We had to act on our compulsion. This desperation was how we made our way into NA. Some of us who didn't seek any changes, died or were locked up in institutions. We didn't know where to go, what to do. Although we kept trying to force our will on to people, places and things in our lives. Our way still wasn't working for us. We didn't know it at the time, but we were spiritually bankrupt. We had lost our connection to our HP. In our active addiction we were out of control and our lives were unmanageable. For many of us, we lost everything, but most of all we lost ourselves in the darkness. Many times, once addicts stop using drugs to cope with life their lives get better just from stopping using. This is a dangerous place for an addict as we can get cocky and start thinking "I got this". We forget that our best thinking got us into the rooms of NA. When we forget that this is a we program and not a me program we are doomed to repeat the insanity of our addiction. The obsession may show up in different ways than the drugs but it will return. The compulsion also returns if we start living for self rather than surrendering our will and learning to live differently. We began to realize that we needed to find a new way to live. We found that way in Narcotics Anonymous.

Luckily at some point we saw a glimmer of hope thru other addicts sharing. We should make a choice: to choose ourselves over drugs and begin to recover. We may face desperation again and again, in recovery. Sometimes life seems unbearable, sometimes we make our life unbearable. Losing our spiritual principles is what often brings us to this point. However, it's not the end of the world yet. We can always come back to principles and the help of Fellowship. There is something solid about them, something we tried and realized that it worked. We learn to rely on this instead of feelings only. No matter how difficult a situation is, using drugs can only make things worse and never better. We believe if, we make one more clean day and we use principles instead of drugs it will be a successful day. Once we entered the rooms of NA we were told the only thing that would work for us was to reestablish our spiritual connection with our Higher Power and once this connection was reconciled that things would start happening in our lives. We learn that the Steps are the way for us to change our lives. We find there is no substitute for surrender. We grow and grow if we let the Steps nurture us to health with the members of NA watering us daily to help us grow.
unmappedHistorical.moment: Today we are free to stop before we react, look at a situation from another perspective and act in the best interest of all those involved. We search out the new, now because we constantly have to pull ourselves out of those old habits.

unmappedHistorical.quote: "We find ourselves helping others and securing help for our own problems. We redefine ourselves. We become feeling people, capable of responding appropriately to our environment."
unmappedHistorical.body: We came into NA messed up. We had problems on top of problems and most of us just wanted the pain to stop. When we sought help from other sources, we ran into many different people who were totally misinformed about our disease. They at first seemed to have solutions but their solutions only took us so far. The things that troubled us were much deeper than we ever realized. Our ego kept us from seeing the truth. *"Being clean we will eventually have to learn to cope with success. Success scares us because in the past it preceded failure. We could not afford to feel good because we remembered the pain of disappointment. It was better, we concluded, to keep moving on and holding back. Actually this made a great deal of sense when we were using. Now, it makes no sense at all. "* After sticking around awhile we found out that not accepting personal responsibility was what was mainly causing us our problems. After stopping using, the fog was lifted enough for us to start seeking solutions. We begin to discover we are all related, by our experiences of suffering, walking similar paths, “needing something different” seeking the solution to our suffering in this program. We discover that the therapeutic value of helping EACH OTHER, helps all involved in this process. We are accepted in NA; told to keep coming back, we experience meaningful love without strings, we begin to discover who we are complete with short comings and assets, we are eager to share this process with others. We found freedom from ourselves, in being able to share our thoughts and feelings with other addicts. The empathy we received bolstered our ability to reach out to other addicts & society at large. The path we followed allowed us to rejoin society in ways we were not capable of during our active addiction. The Steps free us from our self-made prisons and allow us to do the healing work we were never capable of in the past. Once we learn to ask for help, we naturally start to help others. We become a helpful part of our community and do things that help all those around us. By taking a second to read a situation, we can respond to any situation with what's best for all involved. Once we found other addicts that had found recovery from the disease of addiction, the path we needed to take became obvious and we were able to stop focusing all our energy on our version of reality. We are often Amazed at how far we have come when we are able to share our Experience Strength and Hope with someone else about how our reactions to difficult situations today is way different than when we were using or in early recovery. This is made possible by working the Steps and incorporating spiritual principles in our lives.
unmappedHistorical.moment: Many of us have gone from hopeless dope fiends to hopeful human beings. NA makes this possible; for self-centered, self-seeking individuals to grow and become a part of others' lives and find ourselves too. *Gray Book page 84 lines 23-29

unmappedHistorical.quote: "The situations that seem hardest to maintain our honesty have produced the most rewarding results. When we are honest in really difficult situations, the feelings of happiness and serenity are overwhelming."
unmappedHistorical.body:
Let's face it most of us came in here as liars. We thought that living was using drugs. Some may have been honest on the outside, but all of us had denial about our disease. Honesty for some came as a huge challenge, it was like a foreign language. The phrase cash register honesty was seen as an insult. It was almost like hearing someone call us a liar. Those of us that were in such denial had a difficult time seeing ourselves for the person we were. We had numbed ourselves to a point where we had either no feelings or extreme feelings in every situation. Many of us thought if we stopped using everything would get better. Some things were changed just by getting abstinent, but true recovery at a deeper level eluded us due to our lack of being able to see reality for what it was. Getting honest with ourselves was a huge step in the right direction. We were finally beaten to where we were able to accept help. Before we get to that point honesty will be difficult.

We told ourselves we can do this alone. We couldn't see that we needed the WE of the program of NA to help us live. If we were lucky we had a strong sponsor that helped to break down our walls on denial and dishonesty. This was but one of the gifts from our coming to the rooms, not continuing to run from who we were and are.

unmappedHistorical.quote: "we were looking for something new in life, possibly a way to be accepted."
unmappedHistorical.body:
When we first entered the rooms of NA a lot of us were looking for immediate acceptance by family members that we had driven away by our drug use. Some of us were looking for acceptance of where we were. Most of us came into the rooms of NA painfully shy, and untrusting of others. WE didn't start using drugs because we were happy. We were seeking something. Some were seeking to stop the pain. Others were seeking to fit in with a world they felt separate from. Some just wanted to try drugs and ended up finding out they were addicts. No matter how we got here, every single one of us was searching for something different.

NA provides a way for us to finally take an honest look at the problem.... ourselves. We were asked "what is your part?" in situations where we started complaining. As we grow, we may not get the immediate acceptance or trust of others in our communities that we have grown and that may fill us with a "what's the point" attitude. The point is we are better people today then we were in active addiction and eventually our actions will speak for themselves.

We thought since we were attending meetings that we were well. For the first time in many of our lives we had found people that wouldn't accept the blame game. Those people understood us better than we understood ourselves. We often asked "how is that possible?" We finally felt we belonged with other
