unmappedHistorical.quote: "Recovery as experienced through our Twelve Steps is our goal, not mere physical abstinence." basic Text
unmappedHistorical.body: Narcotics Anonymous is a proven and complete program of recovery. This program addresses the disease of addiction and its symptoms in all their complexities. This IP is the shared experience of addicts who have found recovery from ALL drugs without seeking outside help in the form of chemical solutions to our spiritual problem. The foundation of the Narcotics Anonymous Program is complete and total abstinence from all mood-changing, mind-altering drugs. Step 0 There is a Step 0 and we can't recover until we are off drugs. Our Surrender has to be complete when it comes to Total Abstinence. WE MAKE THE DECISION to get Totally Abstinent. There is hope for addicts to find freedom from ALL these issues if we choose them. "Recovery as experienced through our Twelve Steps is our goal, not mere physical abstinence." basic Text Pg. 69, line 1-2 Total Abstinence is just the start to our new way of life. Are we sure we want to stop using? Did jails and institutions take over the care of our lives? taking any mood-changing mind-altering chemical to treat the disease of addiction and its symptoms (the same symptoms of physical (drug induced psychosis) (steroids) mental health symptoms (anxiety, depression, manic depression, Bi-Polar, Personality disorders, fractured personalities, (Jimmy K quote) ADHD, OCD, Schizophrenia anything that affects the way we think) Many of us became addicted at an early age because of being prescribed medications for behavioral problems without knowing it. Social acceptability doesn't equal recovery. Spiritual (resentments, (don't react and pee on your neighbors shoes. no marking your territory) no relief and identification with outside entities. One of issues we have is members suggesting others to seek outside help for issues that Narcotics Anonymous does address. NA does address anxiety, depression, fear, How addictive mental health drugs are dangerous for addicts. 3 disturbing realizations facing our problems without using drugs to face them. Using drugs blocks our conscience and sedates our feelings such as right and wrong, and how we react in certain situations. "Often doctors didn't understand our dilemna: they tried to help by giving us medication." Basic Text Why Are We Here Street drugs were killing us but the drugs prescribed. After stopping using we began to feel emotional pain that we were always afraid to feel (look for Basic Text quote) Basic Text Why Are We Here. Depression and anxiety are part of the disease of addiction they are not an outside issue. The result of our Spiritual illness was the use of drugs, we put in our body psychoactive drugs in insane quantities, which resulted in catastrophic consequences both emotional, physical and mental, someone to a large extent at someone in less. This is the consequences of the use of chemicals. In some cases, it is irreversible

unmappedHistorical.quote: "Learning to live through changes by practicing the principles of the program helps insure our ongoing recovery."
unmappedHistorical.body: Many of us are in the midst of one or several crisis's when we first come to the rooms. Before coming to NA many of us used drugs to cope with changes in our lives. Most often times the alterations that were taking place in our lives were not good ones, after all we are addicts. Most of us knew we needed something different, and we thought we had found it in drugs. We used drugs to avoid change many times. The first change many of us experience is learning to not react when life reminds us that we are not in control. Since we abstain from all mood and mind-altering drugs, the feeling and emotions may be amplified. Many of us were terrified of anything unknown because we wanted to control everything. Our disease got in the way of reality often as our denial kept us from seeing it or facing it. The one constant In life Is change. Some of us have heard that the only thing we need to change is everything. We had to change our playgrounds, playtoys and playmates if we were to recover. Through working the Steps and using our tools we begin to recover. This can be frightening if we have not learned how to practice acceptance. We learn to listen to our feelings, share with our Sponsor and other trusted members in meetings. This allows us to receive the help that we so desperately needed. When we notice changes in us, this is a sign to continue down this path, recovery is an ongoing process. If we are going to recover, we will find that we are constantly changing. We go from one surrender to another. After a few meetings and a honest desire to stop using we quickly learned that a few simple principles could help us stay

unmappedHistorical.quote: “Trusting others doesn't come naturally to us, but we must learn to trust because an addict alone is in bad company.”
unmappedHistorical.body: We came to NA not trusting ourselves; left alone our addictive personalities grew. The only thing many of us were sure of was that we had made a mess of our lives. In addiction we had developed a deep mistrust of everyone and everything, often finding ourselves acting out of desperation and fear. We had a loser's point of view that kept us always looking at the negativity of life rather than seeking solutions. This caused us to think everyone was out to get us. In NA we found there were addicts just like us that had been hurt. Our past was not filled with love and trust. It was mostly fear and obsession. For most of us trusting others isn't natural. When we came to N.A. as the result of being powerless, we started to realize that it wasn't a good idea to completely trust ourselves. Trust is a new idea for most of us. It was a hard learned experience yet as addicts we had to surrender so that we could recover. We found comfort in being alone, because that is what we were used to in the past. Being alone was dangerous; it put us in danger of slipping up and telling ourselves that “one won’t harm us”. Distrust is a bi-product of our disease, practicing Spiritual Principle's allows us to take that first step. Trust begins with faith. In recovery we surrendered and found that we must trust a Higher Power and at first, we had to find a constant that we visualized as a Higher Power that helped us with our focus. This started to make sense. It would be insane to continue all by ourselves, yet it was also scary to let people in to let them know what was going on inside of us. We needed to be surrounded by others in recovery, likeminded people, so that we can bounce ideas off of them and to get other options.... our ways don’t work anymore for us. Those addicts though learned how to let others be human beings instead of expecting perfection from everyone. We learned how to accept our responsibilities by seeing the part we have had in every situation in our lives rather than blaming others. Without trusting other addicts to help us to recover we stay alone...an addict alone is in bad company as the last addict we used with was ourselves. We found other addicts that care for us and will be there for us. We found a Sponsor that was able to guide us by sharing their Experience, Strength and Hope and how they went through similar experiences. By seeing others’ actions and care we began to learn to trust. Learning to live the spiritual principles of NA is the foundation of our recovery. Trusting others is a process we develop over time; we were untrustworthy so why would we trust others. We develop this trust as our faith grows. We lose the belief that the world was out to get us and see that trusting others is a strength, not a weakness. In N.A. we learn to rely on the guidance and experience of other members, our sponsors and a loving God. We came to find out that people are here to help us, not to judge us. With this we are well on our way to a day clean. A day clean is a day won.
unmappedHistorical.moment: By opening up we start to feel a part of each other’s lives and we don't have to live in isolation ever again.

unmappedHistorical.quote: "One thing you can't hide, is when you're crippled inside."
unmappedHistorical.body: We covered up our depression and sadness using dope. We were reduced to mere animal levels. Some of us were great at hiding our pain until it got too much for us to bear. We reached a point where we felt our lives were being ripped apart from us. We no longer could cover up our depression and sadness. We find we can get clean inside yet we still can't hide our emotions. It is hard for us to walk our path when we laid it so fast. We can only pray we find the G.ift O.f D.esperation.
unmappedHistorical.moment: we will be grateful we have found there is hope without dope. ___
